definition_zh: 含蓄地；不言明地；内隐地；绝对地；默认地
definition_en: in a way that is suggested rather than stated, or in a complete and unquestioning way
core_image: 不把话说出口，只把话折好递过去
scene: 这里指「含蓄地」。 By signing the form she implicitly accepted the conditions printed on the back.
sceneCN: 这里指第 1 个义项。这里 implicitly 是「以默认方式」（第 1、5 个义项：未明说即成立）；句意：签下表格，她就默认接受了背面印着的条件。图中可辨识物件：签字的笔、翻到背面的表格、压在纸上的手指。

pos.zh: 含蓄地；不言明地；绝对地；默认地

senses.title: Without putting it into words
senses.definition: in a manner that conveys meaning without stating it
senses.definitionCN: 以传达意义却不明说的方式
senses.example: She implicitly blamed the manager for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 她含蓄地把延误归咎于经理。
senses.why: The adverb modifies the verb, so it tells us how an act was done: the blame was delivered folded, not spoken.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词修饰动词，说明动作是“怎样”做的：责备被折起来递出，而没有说出口。

senses.title: By suggestion rather than statement
senses.definition: through hints and context rather than explicit words
senses.definitionCN: 通过暗示与语境而非明确言语
senses.example: The ending implicitly tells us that he never returned.
senses.exampleCN: 结局暗示他再也没有回来。
senses.why: Here the adverb describes how a text works, not how a person acts. Meaning arrives by implication.
senses.whyCN: 这里副词描述的是文本如何运作，而不是人如何行动。意义是靠暗示到达的。

senses.title: Completely, holding nothing back
senses.definition: with absolute and undoubting confidence
senses.definitionCN: 带着绝对且不存疑虑的信任
senses.example: He trusted her implicitly.
senses.exampleCN: 他绝对信任她。
senses.why: This is the 'folded into another's will' branch: the adverb says no reservation was kept outside the trust.
senses.whyCN: 这是“折进他人意志”的分支：副词说明信任之外没有留下任何保留。

senses.title: Without conscious notice
senses.definition: in a way that operates automatically, below awareness
senses.definitionCN: 以自动、低于意识的方式运作
senses.example: We implicitly learn the rules of our first language.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在无意识中习得母语的规则。
senses.why: The learning is folded into habit, so the adverb marks an act that leaves no memory of learning it.
senses.whyCN: 学习被折进习惯，因此这个副词标记的是一个没有留下“学习”记忆的动作。

senses.title: As an unstated premise
senses.definition: in logic, in a way that is assumed rather than argued
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑中作为被假定而非被论证的前提
senses.example: The model implicitly assumes stable prices.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型默认假定价格稳定。
senses.why: The assumption never appears as a line in the proof; the adverb says it was folded into the background.
senses.whyCN: 该假设从未作为一行出现在证明里；副词说明它被折进了背景。

senses.title: Indirectly, in manner or style
senses.definition: in an indirect manner of expression or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 以间接的表达或行为方式
senses.example: He implicitly criticized the plan by praising its opposite.
senses.exampleCN: 他通过称赞相反做法而含蓄地批评了该计划。
senses.why: The adverb names the route, not the content: the criticism travels around the statement instead of through it.
senses.whyCN: 副词命名的是路径而不是内容：批评绕过陈述，而不是穿过陈述。

senses.title: With unquestioning obedience
senses.definition: with obedience or belief that asks for no justification
senses.definitionCN: 带着不求理由的服从或相信
senses.example: The staff followed the order implicitly.
senses.exampleCN: 员工不加质疑地服从了命令。
senses.why: Obedience is complete when nothing is held outside the fold. The adverb marks the absence of a reserve.
senses.whyCN: 服从之所以彻底，是因为没有东西留在折叠之外。副词标记的正是那份保留的缺席。

senses.title: As part of what is meant
senses.definition: as something contained in the meaning of a word or act even if not spelled out
senses.definitionCN: 作为词或行为的含义所包含、却未被写明的内容
senses.example: The promise implicitly includes a duty to warn.
senses.exampleCN: 这项承诺隐含了告知的义务。
senses.why: Here the adverb points at the contents of a concept. What is included was always inside, awaiting articulation.
senses.whyCN: 这里副词指向概念的内容。被包含的东西一直在内部，只等着被表述出来。

intro.en: Implicitly is implicit plus -ly. The adjective comes from Latin implicitus, 'folded in', the participle of implicare. The adverb therefore describes actions and statements whose meaning or commitment is folded inside them.
intro.cn: implicitly 是 implicit 加 -ly。形容词来自拉丁语 implicitus“折入的”，即 implicare 的分词。因此这个副词描述的是意义或承诺被折在里面的动作与陈述。

items.en: The root *plek-, 'to fold or plait', is reconstructed and generally accepted behind Latin plicare and plectere.
items.cn: 词根 *plek-“折叠、编织”是重构形式，一般被接受为拉丁语 plicare 与 plectere 的来源。

items.en: In- plus plicare gave implicare, 'to fold in, to involve'. The participle implicitus described something already folded, not something being folded.
items.cn: in- 加 plicare 构成 implicare“折入、牵连”。分词 implicitus 描述已经折好的东西，而不是正在折的动作。

items.en: English borrowed implicit as a learned adjective meaning 'contained though not expressed'. The adverb followed once the adjective was established.
items.cn: 英语借入 implicit 作学术形容词，意为“内含而未表达”。形容词站稳之后，副词随之出现。

items.en: The suffix -ly turns adjectives into manner adverbs. It comes from Old English -lice, and in this word it asks 'in what manner was it folded?'
items.cn: 后缀 -ly 把形容词变成方式副词，源自古英语 -lice。在这个词里，它问的是“是以何种方式折叠的？”。

items.en: The 'unstated meaning' use and the 'absolute trust' use both appear in the 18th and 19th centuries, sometimes in the same sentence.
items.cn: “未明说的意义”与“绝对信任”两种用法都出现在 18、19 世纪，有时同处一句。

items.en: Psychology and law gave the adverb technical work: implicitly learned rules, implicitly accepted terms. Both rely on the same image of an unprinted clause.
items.cn: 心理学与法律赋予这个副词技术任务：内隐习得的规则、默认接受的条款。两者都依赖同一个“未印出的条款”意象。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the adjective, the verb and the noun. The meaning group compares adverbs of indirect or silent communication.
note.cn: 形近组区分形容词、动词与名词；词义组比较表示间接或沉默传达的副词。

entries.definition: folded in, not stated. The adverb says that an action is carried out in that folded way.
entries.definitionCN: 折入的、未明说的。副词说明某动作以这种折叠方式完成。

entries.definition: to involve someone in wrongdoing. It is active and judicial, not adverbial.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人卷入过错。它是主动的、司法性的，不是副词用法。

entries.definition: a suggested meaning or a consequence. It is the thing an implicit act leaves behind.
entries.definitionCN: 暗示的含义或后果。它是隐含行为留下的东西。

entries.definition: by agreement or understanding without words. It is very close to sense 01 but comes from 'silent', not from 'folded'.
entries.definitionCN: 不发一言地同意或理解。它很接近第 1 义项，但词源是“沉默”，而非“折叠”。

entries.definition: in a way that does not go straight to the point. It matches sense 06 and stresses route rather than silence.
entries.definitionCN: 不走直线地。它对应第 6 义项，强调路径而非沉默。

entries.definition: totally, without limit. It matches senses 03 and 07 but lacks the image of trust folded into another.
entries.definitionCN: 完全地、无限制地。它对应第 3、7 义项，但缺少“信任折进他人”的意象。

entries.definition: without conscious control. It matches sense 04 and stresses mechanism, not concealment.
entries.definitionCN: 不受意识控制地。它对应第 4 义项，强调机制而非隐藏。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build implicitly from implicit plus -ly and keep the image of an act done with the meaning folded inside.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩从 implicit 加 -ly 搭起 implicitly，并保留“动作完成时意义折在里面”的意象。

normal.en: See implicit + -ly: in a folded manner. Ask 'how?' and the answer is 'without saying it'.
normal.cn: 看成 implicit 加 -ly：以折叠的方式。问“怎么做的？”，答案就是“没说出口”。

normal.en: Picture a signed form: the signature says nothing, yet it accepts every clause on the back.
normal.cn: 想象一份签好的表格：签名一言不发，却接受了背面的每一条款。

normal.en: When someone replies 'if you like', they are implicitly refusing.
normal.cn: 当有人回答“随你吧”，他们其实在含蓄地拒绝。

normal.en: Trusting implicitly means keeping nothing back outside the trust.
normal.cn: 绝对信任意味着在信任之外不留任何东西。

normal.en: Learning implicitly means the rule entered your hands without a lesson.
normal.cn: 内隐学习意味着规则没上课就进了你的手。

abstract.en: Keep one image: a hand passing a closed note across a table.
abstract.cn: 只记一个意象：一只手把折好的纸条推过桌面。

abstract.en: Treat the adverb as answering 'how', never 'what'; the content stays folded.
abstract.cn: 把这个副词当作回答“如何”，而不是“什么”；内容始终折着。

abstract.en: Notice that silence can carry both criticism and consent, and only context unfolds it.
abstract.cn: 注意沉默既能携带批评也能携带同意，只有语境能把它展开。

examples.en: The report implicitly criticizes the previous administration.
examples.cn: 这份报告含蓄地批评了前任政府。

examples.en: She trusted his judgement implicitly.
examples.cn: 她绝对信任他的判断。

examples.en: Children learn grammar implicitly long before they study it.
examples.cn: 儿童在系统学习语法之前，早已内隐地习得语法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“阴里塞得利”：把话藏在阴处塞进去，还办得利落——这就是含蓄地、默认地。

root: 拉丁语 implicitus（implicare“折入”的过去分词，in- + plicare 折叠）加英语副词后缀 -ly；与 explicit“展开的”相对。

sensesIntro.en: Implicitly always answers the question 'how'. It says that a blame, a promise, a trust, a learning, an assumption, a criticism, an obedience or an inclusion was carried out with the meaning folded in. The eight senses differ in which act is being performed and whether the fold hides a message or hides a reservation.
sensesIntro.cn: implicitly 始终回答“如何”这个问题。它说责备、承诺、信任、学习、假定、批评、服从或包含，都是以“意义折在里面”的方式完成的。八个义项的差别在于执行的是什么动作，以及这次折叠是藏起了一则讯息，还是藏起了一份保留。

core.en: Acting or meaning in a folded way, with the content left inside.
core.cn: 以折叠的方式行动或表意，内容留在里面。

branches.en: COMMUNICATION: blame, hints and criticism delivered by implication.
branches.cn: 沟通：以暗示递出的责备、提示与批评。

branches.en: COMMITMENT: trust and obedience with nothing held back.
branches.cn: 承诺：毫无保留的信任与服从。

branches.en: MIND: rules absorbed below awareness.
branches.cn: 心智：在意识之下吸收的规则。

branches.en: REASONING: premises assumed but never listed.
branches.cn: 推理：被假定却从未列出的前提。

branches.en: MEANING: duties contained inside a promise.
branches.cn: 意义：包含在承诺内部的义务。

intro.en: Implicitly is the adjective plus -ly. The items below show the fold family across parts of speech, and show that the adverb is simply the manner form of the adjective.
intro.cn: implicitly 是形容词加 -ly。下列条目展示“折叠”词族跨词类的分布，并说明副词只是形容词的方式形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries repeat the small family behind the adverb: a verb, its participle and the bare root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目重复了副词背后的小家族：一个动词、它的分词与裸词根。

items.example: He implicitly acknowledged the error.
The condition was implicit in the offer.
The implication frightened the investors.
items.exampleCN: 言下之意吓到了投资者。

items.example: The testimony implicated three others.
The implicitness of the rule caused confusion.
items.exampleCN: 规则的不言明造成了混乱。

items.example: The contract states the deadline explicitly.
items.exampleCN: 合同明确写明了截止日期。

items.example: The implied threat was clear to everyone.
items.exampleCN: 那隐含的威胁人人都看得出。

items.structure: Old French emplier, from Latin implicare
items.example: Are you implying that I lied?

definition_zh: 记忆；把信息反复记入脑中的过程，也常指死记硬背
definition_en: the process of committing information to memory, often by repeated practice or rote learning
core_image: 一个人把卡片一张张翻过，直到不看也能复述
scene: 考前一周，学生每天抄写同一列年代，直到合上书也能按顺序说出。 For a week before the exam the student writes the same list of dates until she can recite it with the book closed, a routine of pure memorization.
sceneCN: 这里 memorization 指「把信息反复记入脑中的过程」（第 1 个义项：靠重复把内容固定下来）；句意为学生一周内每天抄写同一列年代，直到合上书也能按顺序背出。图中可辨识物件：卡片、年代列表、合上的书、计时器。

pos.zh: 记忆；背诵；死记硬背（不可数）

senses.title: The process of committing to memory
senses.titleCN: 把信息记入脑中的过程
senses.definition: the process of fixing information in the mind through study or repetition
senses.definitionCN: 通过学习或重复把信息固定在心中的过程
senses.example: She writes the dates until she can recite them with the book closed.
senses.exampleCN: 她把年代写到合上书也能背出的程度。
senses.why: the -ation suffix names an action, so memorization is the work of putting something in, not the thing stored.
senses.whyCN: -ation 后缀命名一个动作，因此 memorization 是「放进去」的工作，而非被存放的东西。

senses.title: The state of having been memorized
senses.definition: the condition of being held in memory as a result of such work
senses.definitionCN: 因这番工夫而被保存在记忆中的状态
senses.example: The dates were kept in memorization for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这些年代被记住并保留了很多年。
senses.why: an action noun can slide into its result; what has been done stays done, and the word names that staying.
senses.whyCN: 动作名词可以滑向结果；做过的事保持完成状态，而这个词命名这种保持。

senses.title: Rote learning without understanding
senses.definition: learning by repetition alone, often with the implication that meaning is neglected
senses.definitionCN: 仅靠重复的学习，常暗示忽略了意义
senses.example: The course rewards memorization over explanation.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课奖励背诵多于解释。
senses.why: the same process becomes a criticism when it is separated from understanding; the word carries that judgement in school talk.
senses.whyCN: 同一种过程一旦与理解分离就变成批评；在学校话语里，这个词带着这种评判。

senses.title: Material that has been memorized
senses.definition: the text, list or lines one has learned by heart
senses.definitionCN: 已经熟记的文本、清单或台词
senses.example: The actor ran through his memorization before the scene.
senses.exampleCN: 演员在开场前把背下的台词过了一遍。
senses.why: metonymy turns the act into the thing acted on, as when a recitation is called a memorization.
senses.whyCN: 转喻把动作变成被作用之物，于是背下来的内容也被称作 memorization。

senses.title: A classroom exercise
senses.definition: a school task in which pupils learn facts or texts by heart
senses.definitionCN: 要求学生熟记事实或文本的课堂任务
senses.example: The weekly memorization test covers twenty words.
senses.exampleCN: 每周的记忆测验覆盖二十个单词。
senses.why: schools need countable exercises, so the general process becomes an item on the timetable.
senses.whyCN: 学校需要可计数的练习，于是一般过程变成课表上的一个项目。

senses.title: Encoding and consolidation in psychology
senses.titleCN: 心理学中的编码与巩固
senses.definition: the laboratory process by which material is encoded and then stabilized in long-term memory
senses.definitionCN: 材料被编码并在长时记忆中稳定下来的实验过程
senses.example: Sleep improves the memorization of new vocabulary.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠有助于新词汇的记忆巩固。
senses.why: when psychologists look inside the process, repetition splits into encoding and consolidation, and this word covers both stages.
senses.whyCN: 心理学家看进过程内部后，重复被分成编码与巩固，而这个词覆盖两个阶段。

senses.title: Learning lines for performance
senses.definition: the actor's or musician's work of fixing lines, cues or scores in memory
senses.definitionCN: 演员或乐手把台词、提示或乐谱记牢的工作
senses.example: Her memorization of the monologue took three days.
senses.exampleCN: 她背下那段独白用了三天。
senses.why: performance cannot pause for a script, so the same process becomes a professional skill with its own practice routines.
senses.whyCN: 演出不能为剧本暂停，因此同一种过程成为有专门练法的职业技能。

senses.title: Recitation of sacred or traditional texts
senses.titleCN: 宗教或传统经典的记诵
senses.definition: the disciplined learning by heart of scriptures, poems or oral tradition
senses.definitionCN: 对经文、诗篇或口传传统的有纪律的熟记
senses.example: Monks begin memorization of the sutras at an early age.
senses.exampleCN: 僧侣很早就开始记诵经文。
senses.why: where a text must survive without copying, memory is the medium, and memorization is the technology.
senses.whyCN: 当文本必须在不靠复制的情况下流传，记忆就是媒介，而记诵就是那项技术。

intro.en: Memorization joins memorize with -ation; memorize itself comes from memory, from Latin memoria. The word is a modern English formation, not a classical Latin noun. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: memorization 由 memorize 加 -ation 构成；memorize 又来自 memory，源自拉丁 memoria。这是现代英语的构造，并非古典拉丁名词。年代为约数。

items.en: Memoria 'memory' comes from memor 'mindful'; it supplied the noun from which the English verb was later built.
items.cn: memoria「记忆」源自 memor「记得的」，为后来英语动词提供名词基础。

items.en: English memory appeared in the thirteenth century; the verb memorize 'commit to memory' is recorded from the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语 memory 在 13 世纪出现；动词 memorize「记入记忆」在 16 世纪有记录。

items.en: The suffix -ation, from Latin -atio, names an action or its result; adding it to memorize produced memorization in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 后缀 -ation 源自拉丁 -atio，命名动作或结果；加在 memorize 上，于 19 世纪构成 memorization。

items.en: British English also writes memorisation with -isa-, following the same pattern as organise; both forms are current.
items.cn: 英式英语也写作 memorisation，用 -isa-，与 organise 的拼法一致；两种形式都在使用。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the first recorded use of memorization is usually placed in the nineteenth century, but the exact year is not agreed, and the boundary with memorisation is purely orthographic.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：memorization 的最早书证通常定在 19 世纪，但确切年份没有定论；它与 memorisation 的差别纯属拼写。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike forms, including a technical term from computing that is not the same word; group two holds methods and products of learning by heart.
note.cn: 第一组是外形相近的形式，其中含一个并非同词的计算机术语；第二组是熟记的方法与产物。

entries.definition: The same word spelled with -isa-; the difference is orthographic only.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的英式拼写，用 -isa-；差别只在拼写。

entries.definition: A programming technique that caches function results; it is coined from memo, not from memory, and has nothing to do with human recall.
entries.definitionCN: 一种缓存函数结果的编程技术；由 memo 而非 memory 造出，与人的回忆无关。

entries.definition: To commit something to memory; memorization is the noun naming that activity.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物记入记忆；memorization 是命名该活动的名词。

entries.definition: The faculty or content of remembering; memorization names the effort that fills it.
entries.definitionCN: 记忆的能力或内容；memorization 命名填满它的那番努力。

entries.definition: Learning by repetition without attention to meaning; memorization can be rote, but need not be.
entries.definitionCN: 不看意义、只靠重复的学习；memorization 可以是死记，但不必然如此。

entries.definition: Doing or saying the same thing again; it is the engine that makes memorization work.
entries.definitionCN: 重复做或说同一件事；是让记忆生效的引擎。

entries.definition: Saying aloud what has been learned by heart; it displays memorization rather than producing it.
entries.definitionCN: 出声说出背下的内容；展示记忆，而非产生记忆。

entries.definition: How much remains available after learning; it is the measure of successful memorization.
entries.definitionCN: 学习后还能保留多少；是记忆成功与否的度量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: memory + -ize + -ation: the store, the act of filling it, and the name of that act.
normal.cn: memory + -ize + -ation：库房、装填的动作，以及这一动作的名称。

normal.en: The family runs memorize, memorizer, memory, memorable and memorization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 memorize、memorizer、memory、memorable 与 memorization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: rote memorization, memorization task, memorization technique.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：死记硬背、记忆任务、记忆技巧。

normal.en: Memorization is the process; memory is the store; recall is the retrieval.
normal.cn: memorization 是过程，memory 是库房，recall 是取出。

normal.en: Do not confuse memorization with memoization: the computing term comes from memo, not memory.
normal.cn: 不要把 memorization 与 memoization 混淆：计算机术语来自 memo，而非 memory。

abstract.en: Picture a hand copying the same line until the line lives in the hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手反复抄同一行，直到那一行住进手里。

abstract.en: Picture a door closing on a full shelf and opening only when called.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门在一排满架前关上，只在被呼唤时打开。

abstract.en: Picture a monk reciting in the dark because the book is inside him.
abstract.cn: 想象僧人在黑暗中诵经，因为书就在他体内。

examples.en: The exam rewards memorization more than analysis.
examples.cn: 这场考试奖励背诵多于分析。

examples.en: Daily memorization of ten words beats one long session.
examples.cn: 每天记十个词胜过一次性长时间苦背。

examples.en: Sleep supports the consolidation that memorization requires.
examples.cn: 睡眠支持记忆所需要的巩固过程。

dict_mnemonic.text: memory（记忆）+ ization（过程）——把东西一遍遍放进记忆的过程 → 记忆、背诵

root: memory（拉丁 memoria）+ -ize（使……化）+ -ation（过程）；19 世纪英语构造，指把信息反复记入脑中的过程。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses describe the same work from different angles: the act, its result, rote method, learned material, classroom task, laboratory encoding, stage work and sacred recitation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从不同角度描述同一番工夫：动作、结果、死记方法、背下的材料、课堂任务、实验编码、舞台功夫，以及经文记诵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same line written again and again until it can be said without the page.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一行字被反复抄写，直到不看纸也能说出。

branches.en: ACT AND RESULT: the work of putting in, then the state of being held.
branches.cn: 动作与结果：先放入的工夫，再是被保存的状态。

branches.en: WITHOUT MEANING: repetition alone turns the method into a criticism.
branches.cn: 不求意义：只剩重复时，方法就成了批评对象。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND STAGE: what is held can be a list for a test or lines for a scene.
branches.cn: 材料与舞台：记住的可以是测验清单，也可以是场景台词。

branches.en: INSTITUTION AND LAB: the same act becomes a timetable item and an encoding stage.
branches.cn: 建制与实验：同一动作既成为课表项目，也成为编码阶段。

branches.en: SACRED USE: where no copy exists, memory is the only medium.
branches.cn: 神圣用法：在没有副本的地方，记忆是唯一媒介。

intro.en: Memorization stacks three pieces: the Latin stem memor, the verb suffix -ize and the noun suffix -ation.
intro.cn: memorization 叠了三层：拉丁词干 memor、动词后缀 -ize、名词后缀 -ation。

latinIntro.en: Latin memor 'mindful' yields memoria; English memory, memorize and memorization continue the line, while the computing term memoization comes from memo instead.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 memor「记得的」生成 memoria；英语 memory、memorize、memorization 延续这条线，而计算机术语 memoization 来自 memo。

items.example: Memor is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: memor 是整个词族的基础。

items.meaning: to make, to subject to a process
items.example: Memory plus -ize gives the verb memorize.
items.exampleCN: memory 加 -ize 构成动词 memorize。

items.meaning: the act or result of a process
items.example: Memorize plus -ation names the activity.
items.exampleCN: memorize 加 -ation 命名这项活动。

items.meaning: the act of committing to memory
items.meaningCN: 把信息记入记忆的行为
items.example: Memorization without meaning fades fast.
items.exampleCN: 没有意义的背诵忘得很快。

items.example: She memorized the dates in a week.
items.exampleCN: 她一周内背下了这些年代。

items.example: A good memorizer still needs a schedule.
items.exampleCN: 擅长背诵的人仍然需要计划。

items.example: Memory supplies the material.
A memorable fact is easier to keep.
items.exampleCN: 难忘的事实更容易保留。

items.example: The memorized lines sounded flat.
items.exampleCN: 背下的台词听起来很平。

items.example: The day is one of commemoration, not study.
items.exampleCN: 这一天是纪念，不是学习。

definition_zh: 有毒的；毒性的；由毒物引起的；比喻有害的
definition_en: poisonous to living organisms, or harmful in a way compared to poison
core_image: 水边一只死鸟旁，黑色油泥泛着彩光，沾在手套上久久不散
scene: 志愿者在水边捡起一只死鸟，手套上沾着发亮的黑色油泥。 The spill left a toxic residue along the shoreline.
sceneCN: 这里 toxic 指「对生物有毒的、能造成伤害的」（第 1 个义项：物质对活体生物具有毒性）；句意为泄漏在岸线上留下一层有毒残留物。图中可辨识物件：死鸟、黑色油泥、手套、岸线。

pos.zh: 有毒的；毒性的；有害的

senses.title: Poisonous to living organisms
senses.definition: capable of harming or killing an organism by chemical action
senses.definitionCN: 能通过化学作用伤害或杀死生物的
senses.example: The spill left a toxic residue along the shoreline.
senses.exampleCN: 泄漏在岸线上留下一层有毒残留物。
senses.why: The word began as the adjective of Greek toxikon, the poison smeared on arrows, so its core image is a substance that kills at a distance.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是希腊 toxikon 的形容词，指涂在箭上的毒，因此核心意象是「能在远处致死的物质」。

senses.title: Caused by poison, as a medical condition
senses.definition: describing an illness, dose or effect produced by a poison or drug
senses.definitionCN: 描述由毒物或药物引起的疾病、剂量或效应
senses.example: The patient showed a toxic reaction to the drug.
senses.exampleCN: 病人对该药出现了毒性反应。
senses.why: Medicine needed an adjective for harm caused by a substance, as distinct from harm caused by infection or injury.
senses.whyCN: 医学需要一个形容词来指「由物质造成的伤害」，以区别于感染或外伤造成的伤害。

senses.title: Chemically hazardous in industry
senses.definition: describing waste, gas or material that must be handled under special safety rules
senses.definitionCN: 描述必须在专门安全规则下处理的废物、气体或材料
senses.example: Toxic waste must be stored away from the water table.
senses.exampleCN: 有毒废物必须远离地下水位存放。
senses.why: Regulation turned the adjective into a label that triggers permits, protective gear and disposal rules.
senses.whyCN: 监管把这个形容词变成一个标签，一贴上就触发许可、防护装备与处置规则。

senses.title: Produced by a living organism
senses.definition: describing a poison made by a plant, animal or microbe, as in a toxic secretion
senses.definitionCN: 描述由植物、动物或微生物制造的毒物，如毒性分泌物
senses.example: The frog's skin carries a toxic secretion.
senses.exampleCN: 这只蛙的皮肤带有毒性分泌物。
senses.why: Biology separates what is made by life from what is made in a factory, though both are called toxic.
senses.whyCN: 生物学要区分「生命制造的」与「工厂制造的」，尽管两者都叫 toxic。

senses.title: Harmful to a person's mind or relationships
senses.titleCN: 对人的心理或关系有害的
senses.definition: describing behaviour, a relationship or an atmosphere that damages people psychologically
senses.definitionCN: 描述在心理上伤害人的行为、关系或氛围
senses.example: She left a toxic working environment.
senses.exampleCN: 她离开了一个有害的工作环境。
senses.why: The metaphor works because the harm is slow, cumulative and hard to see, like exposure to a poison.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻成立，是因为伤害缓慢、累积且难以看见，像接触毒物一样。

senses.title: Worthless and dangerous financial assets
senses.definition: describing loans or securities whose value has collapsed and which threaten the holder
senses.definitionCN: 描述价值已崩塌、并危及持有者的贷款或证券
senses.example: The bank was left holding toxic assets.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行最后手里握着有毒资产。
senses.why: Finance borrowed the word because the asset poisons the balance sheet it sits on.
senses.whyCN: 金融界借用这个词，因为这类资产会毒害它所在的资产负债表。

senses.title: Slang: extremely bad or unpleasant
senses.titleCN: 口语：极糟的、令人难受的
senses.definition: an informal use meaning very bad, offensive or unbearable
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法，指很糟、令人反感或难以忍受
senses.example: The traffic was toxic all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 整个下午的交通都糟透了。
senses.why: Slang strips the word down to pure intensity, keeping the sense of harm without any chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 口语把这个词剥离成纯粹的强度，只留「有害」的感觉，不带任何化学含义。

senses.title: Listed as toxic by regulation
senses.definition: formally classified as a hazardous substance with a defined threshold and reporting duty
senses.definitionCN: 被正式归为危险物质，附有明确阈值与申报义务
senses.example: The solvent is toxic under the clean-air rules.
senses.exampleCN: 这种溶剂在清洁空气法规下被列为有毒。
senses.why: A legal label is a separate sense because the classification does not depend on how the substance behaves in each case.
senses.whyCN: 法律标签之所以是独立义项，是因为归类并不取决于该物质在每种情形下的实际表现。

senses.title: Abstract: corrosive to a group or culture
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：对群体或文化起腐蚀作用
senses.definition: describing norms, speech or incentives that slowly damage trust and cooperation
senses.definitionCN: 描述缓慢损害信任与合作的规范、言论或激励机制
senses.example: The report called the incentives toxic for new staff.
senses.exampleCN: 报告称这些激励机制对新员工有害。
senses.why: The final extension keeps the medical shape: a small repeated exposure produces a systemic illness.
senses.whyCN: 最后的延伸保留了医学形态：少量而反复的接触会造成全身性的病症。

intro.en: Toxic came to English through Latin from Greek, where the original poison was the one put on arrows. The figurative senses are modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: toxic 经拉丁语从希腊语进入英语，原本的毒是涂在箭上的那种。比喻义是近代的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Toxon meant 'bow'. Its own origin is uncertain; it is often treated as a borrowing from a non-Greek language, so any older form offered for it is a hypothesis rather than a proved source.
items.cn: toxon 意为「弓」。它本身的来源不确定；常被看作借自某种非希腊语，因此凡为它给出的更早形式都是假说，而非已证实的来源。

items.en: Toxikon (pharmakon) meant 'arrow poison', literally the thing of the bow; the adjective toxikos described what belonged to the bow or to its poison.
items.cn: toxikon（pharmakon）意为「箭毒」，字面是「属于弓的东西」；形容词 toxikos 描述属于弓或其毒物者。

items.en: Latin toxicum meant 'poison', and toxicus was its adjective; medieval and early modern writers used both for venoms and drugs.
items.cn: 拉丁 toxicum 意为「毒」，toxicus 是其形容词；中世纪与近代早期作者用两者兼指毒液与药物。

items.en: English toxic appears in the seventeenth century as a learned adjective meaning 'poisonous', alongside the noun toxicum.
items.cn: 英语 toxic 在十七世纪作为学术形容词出现，意为「有毒的」，同时还有名词 toxicum。

items.en: Toxicology and industrial hygiene made toxic a standard term for chemical harm, and twentieth-century law turned it into a regulatory category.
items.cn: 毒理学与工业卫生使 toxic 成为化学危害的标准术语，二十世纪的法律又把它变成监管类别。

items.en: Source uncertain (origin of toxon, first date of the figurative senses): the bow word may be a foreign borrowing whose source is unknown, and no single earliest citation is fixed for the relational or slang senses, so their dates are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（toxon 的来源、比喻义的首见年代）：「弓」这个词可能是外来借词，而借自何处不明；关系义与口语义也没有公认的最早书证，年代只能约计。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same poison stock that differ in part of speech or in sense; group two holds adjectives of harm, each with its own route of injury.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「毒」词干、词性或含义不同的词；第二组是表示「有害」的形容词，各自的伤害路径不同。

entries.definition: A poison made by a living organism, such as a bacterial toxin; toxic is the adjective describing such a substance or its effect.
entries.definitionCN: 由活生物制造的毒物，如细菌毒素；toxic 是描述这种物质或其效应的形容词。

entries.definition: The study of poisons and their effects; it is a discipline name, not a description of a substance.
entries.definitionCN: 研究毒物及其效应的学科；它是学科名称，而非物质描述。

entries.definition: To make drunk or wildly excited, from the same toxicum; the modern sense has left poison behind.
entries.definitionCN: 使醉或使极度兴奋，同出 toxicum；现代义已离开了「毒」的意思。

entries.definition: A condition in which toxins are present in the blood; it names the medical state rather than the property.
entries.definitionCN: 毒素存在于血液中的状况；它命名的是医学状态，而非性质。

entries.definition: Able to harm when eaten, drunk or touched; it is the everyday word, while toxic is the technical and figurative one.
entries.definitionCN: 吃下、喝下或接触时能造成伤害；它是日常词，而 toxic 更技术化、也更多比喻用法。

entries.tag: injected by a bite or sting
entries.definition: Able to inject poison through a bite or sting; a venomous animal is not simply toxic, because the delivery matters.
entries.definitionCN: 能通过咬或蜇注入毒液；venomous 的动物不能简单说成 toxic，因为「如何送入」很关键。

entries.definition: Harmful, especially to health or to the senses, as of fumes; it stresses the unpleasant exposure rather than the chemistry.
entries.definitionCN: 有害的，尤指对健康或感官，如烟气；它强调难受的接触，而非化学性质。

entries.definition: Extremely infectious or severe, used of pathogens and, figuratively, of hostility; it is about spreading power, not poison.
entries.definitionCN: 传染性极强或极严重的，用于病原体，也比喻敌意；它讲的是传播力，而非毒性。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root is Greek toxon 'bow': the first toxic thing was arrow poison.
normal.cn: 词根是希腊 toxon「弓」：最早的「有毒之物」是箭毒。

normal.en: The family runs toxin, toxicity, toxicology, toxicologist and detoxify.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 toxin、toxicity、toxicology、toxicologist 与 detoxify。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: toxic waste, toxic substance, toxic effect, highly toxic.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：有毒废物、有毒物质、毒性效应、剧毒的。

normal.en: Toxic is the adjective; toxin is the substance; toxicity is the degree.
normal.cn: toxic 是形容词；toxin 是物质；toxicity 是程度。

normal.en: Venomous means injected by bite or sting, which is narrower than toxic.
normal.cn: venomous 指经咬或蜇注入，比 toxic 窄。

abstract.en: Picture a drop of poison that takes hours to show its work.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴毒物要过几个小时才显出作用。

abstract.en: Picture a room where every conversation leaves you a little more tired.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，每次谈话都让你更疲惫一点。

abstract.en: Picture a loan on a ledger that quietly poisons every page around it.
abstract.cn: 想象账本上的一笔贷款，悄悄毒害周围每一页。

examples.en: The compound is toxic to fish at very low concentrations.
examples.cn: 这种化合物在极低浓度下就对鱼类有毒。

examples.en: Workers handling toxic waste wear sealed suits.
examples.cn: 处理有毒废物的工人穿着密封防护服。

examples.en: The label toxic is also used for relationships and cultures.
examples.cn: toxic 这个标签也被用于关系和职场文化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「tox（弓/箭）+ ic」——涂在箭上的那种东西 → 有毒的

root: 拉丁 toxicus < toxicum「毒」< 希腊 toxikon（pharmakon）「箭毒」< toxon「弓」；toxon 的来源不确定，可能借自非希腊语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one poison: the substance, the dose, the body, the damage, the label, and then relationships, money, slang and culture borrow the same shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一种毒展开：物质、剂量、身体、损害、标签，随后关系、金钱、口语与文化都借用了同一形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: arrow poison, a substance that kills from a distance.
core.cn: 核心意象：箭毒，一种能在远处致死的物质。

branches.en: BODY: the property of poison and the medical reaction are the same harm seen from outside and inside.
branches.cn: 身体：毒的性质与医学反应，是同一伤害从外面与里面看到的样子。

branches.en: LABEL: industrial handling and legal classification both turn toxicity into a rule.
branches.cn: 标签：工业处置与法律归类都把毒性变成一条规则。

branches.en: LIFE-MADE: a secretion from a plant or animal is poison with a maker.
branches.cn: 生物制造：植物或动物的分泌物，是有制造者的毒。

branches.en: SOCIAL AND FINANCIAL: a relationship and a bad loan both poison what contains them.
branches.cn: 社会与金融：一段关系与一笔坏账，都会毒害容纳它们的东西。

branches.en: INTENSITY: slang keeps only the harm, and culture keeps the slow cumulative exposure.
branches.cn: 强度：口语只留下「有害」，文化义保留「缓慢累积的接触」。

intro.en: Toxic is a Greek-derived adjective with a root that reaches back to the bow and a suffix that makes a quality.
intro.cn: toxic 是希腊来源形容词，词根可追到「弓」，后缀则构成性质形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin toxicum gives toxic, toxin, toxicity, toxicology and intoxicate; Greek toxon 'bow' is the root behind all of them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 toxicum 衍生 toxic、toxin、toxicity、toxicology 与 intoxicate；希腊 toxon「弓」是它们共同的根。

items.example: The bow word gave its name to arrow poison.

items.structure: toxikon (Greek adjective/noun, 'of the bow; arrow poison')
items.example: Toxikon named the poison on the arrowhead.
items.exampleCN: toxikon 指涂在箭头上的毒。

items.example: The adjective entered English as toxic.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词以 toxic 进入英语。

items.example: The suffix makes a quality adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成性质形容词。

items.example: The gas was toxic in the tunnel.

items.meaning: a poison, especially from an organism
items.example: The bacterium released a toxin.
They measured the toxicity of the sample.
items.exampleCN: 他们测定了样本的毒性。

items.example: Toxicology screened the water.
The liver detoxifies the blood.
The drink intoxicated him quickly.

latinEntries.structure: toxicus, toxica, toxicum (adjective, first and second declension)

definition_zh: 食物链；生物之间谁吃谁的线性传递序列
definition_en: a single linear sequence of organisms in which each is eaten by the next, tracing the transfer of energy from producer to consumer
core_image: 一幅直排的图：水下藻类在最下层，小虾在其上，鱼再上一层，最后是一只俯冲的鹭
scene: 同一片水塘里，藻类被小虾吃，小虾被鱼吃，鱼又被岸边的鹭叼走。 The pond's food chain runs from algae through shrimp and fish to the heron.
sceneCN: 这里指谁吃谁的单线传递序列（第 1 个义项：线性的取食与能量序列）；句意为这片水塘的食物链从藻类经小虾与鱼直到鹭。

pos.zh: 食物链（可数短语名词）
某一特定取食序列（用于生态学与教学）

derivatives.zh: 该短语的前半，源自古英语表示食物的词，义为「食物」
该短语的后半，源自拉丁语表示锁链的词，义为「链」
由该短语与表示「网」的词构成的相邻术语，义为「食物网」，指多条链交织成的网络
相关术语，由希腊语表示「营养」的词构成，义为「营养级」，指链上的位置
早期同义术语，义为「食物循环」，强调物质回流而非单线传递
由该后半与表示「长度」的词构成，义为「链长」，指链上环节数目

senses.title: A linear sequence of who eats whom
senses.definition: a single ordered line of organisms in which each is eaten by the one above it
senses.definitionCN: 一条有次序的单线，其中每一种生物都被上一层的那一种吃掉
senses.example: A food chain from pondweed to heron has only four links here.
senses.exampleCN: 这里从池草到鹭的一条食物链只有四个环节。
senses.why: The second word is a chain, and a chain has links in order, which is exactly what a sequence of eaters is.
senses.whyCN: 后半的意思是锁链，而锁链是有次序的环节，这正是「一连串取食者」的样子。

senses.title: Energy passing from producer to consumer
senses.titleCN: 能量从生产者向消费者的传递
senses.definition: the route by which captured energy moves from plants to herbivores and then to predators
senses.definitionCN: 被固定的能量从植物到植食者、再到捕食者的移动路线
senses.example: Every food chain begins with a plant or an alga that captures sunlight.
senses.exampleCN: 每条食物链都始于固定阳光的植物或藻类。
senses.why: A chain of eaters is also a chain of transfers, so the term widened from bodies to the energy inside them.
senses.whyCN: 一连串取食者也是一连串转移，因此这个词从身体扩展到了身体里的能量。

senses.title: The three positions of producer, consumer and decomposer
senses.titleCN: 生产者、消费者与分解者的三个位置
senses.definition: the standard three-part division of roles along the sequence, with decomposers closing the loop
senses.definitionCN: 沿这条序列划分的标准三种角色，分解者负责把环闭上
senses.example: A food chain in a log has a fungus where a pond has a fish.
senses.exampleCN: 木头里的一条食物链，用真菌占用了池塘里鱼的位置。
senses.why: Three jobs are enough to describe any sequence, so the term took the standard three-part division.
senses.whyCN: 三种角色足以描述任何序列，因此这个词采用了标准的三分法。

senses.title: A length limited by energy loss
senses.titleCN: 受能量损耗限制的长度
senses.definition: a sequence that rarely exceeds four or five links because most energy is lost at each step
senses.definitionCN: 很少超过四五个环节的序列，因为每一步都会损失大部分能量
senses.example: No food chain in this lake is longer than five links.
senses.exampleCN: 这个湖里没有一条食物链超过五个环节。
senses.why: The tenth rule makes long chains impossible, and the limit itself became part of what the word describes.
senses.whyCN: 「一成」规则使长链不可能，而这一限度本身也成了这个词描述的内容。

senses.title: A simplified model of a food web
senses.definition: an abstraction taken out of a network so that one pathway can be taught or measured
senses.definitionCN: 从网络中抽出的一条路径，以便教学或测量
senses.example: A textbook food chain hides the fact that the fish also eats insects.
senses.exampleCN: 教科书里的一条食物链掩盖了鱼也吃昆虫这一事实。
senses.why: Teaching needs a single line, so a path is cut out of the network and given the name of the whole.
senses.whyCN: 教学需要一条单线，于是从网络中切出一条路径，并冠以整体的名字。

senses.title: Grazing and detrital chains
senses.definition: two kinds of chain, one starting from living plants and one from dead matter and its microbes
senses.definitionCN: 两种链，一种始于活植物，一种始于死有机质及其微生物
senses.example: The detrital food chain in the marsh starts with fallen reed litter.
senses.exampleCN: 这片沼泽的碎屑食物链从落下的芦苇枯叶开始。
senses.why: Dead matter supports a sequence of its own, and the term had to cover both starting points.
senses.whyCN: 死有机质支撑着它自己的序列，这个词必须覆盖两种起点。

senses.title: A route for accumulating toxins
senses.definition: a pathway along which fat-soluble substances build up in ever higher concentrations
senses.definitionCN: 脂溶性物质在其中以越来越高浓度积累的路径
senses.example: Mercury climbs the food chain until top predators carry the heaviest load.
senses.exampleCN: 汞沿食物链上行，直到顶级捕食者携带最重的负担。
senses.why: Fat-soluble substances do not leave a body easily, so the sequence became the route of their concentration.
senses.whyCN: 脂溶性物质不易排出体外，这条序列于是成了它们浓缩的路线。

senses.title: The top predator at the end
senses.definition: the final position, occupied by a predator that is eaten by few or none
senses.definitionCN: 最后一个位置，由很少被吃或不被吃的捕食者占据
senses.example: The eagle sits at the top of this food chain and accumulates everything below it.
senses.exampleCN: 鹰坐在这条食物链的顶端，把下面的一切都累积在身上。
senses.why: Every line has an end, and the end is where fewest eaters remain.
senses.whyCN: 每条线都有末端，而末端正是取食者最少的地方。

senses.title: A chain that can be broken
senses.definition: a sequence that collapses when one link is removed, with effects passing down the line
senses.definitionCN: 某一环被移除时会断裂、并使影响沿线下传的序列
senses.example: Draining the pond broke the food chain at its second link.
senses.exampleCN: 排干池塘，把这条食物链在第二个环节处打断了。
senses.why: A chain is only as strong as its links, so the word began to be used for the event of losing one.
senses.whyCN: 链的强度取决于环扣，于是这个词开始用于「失去一环」这件事。

intro.en: Both words are old English nouns. Food is native Germanic and chain came from Latin through French; the compound is a twentieth-century ecology term.
intro.cn: 两个词都是古老的英语名词：前半「食物」属日耳曼本族词，后半「链」经法语来自拉丁语；这一复合词是二十世纪的生态学术语。

items.en: Foda meant food or nourishment, and it is related to the verb for feeding.
items.cn: 这个词意为食物、养料，与表示「喂养」的动词同源。

items.en: Catena meant a chain, and it named a series of linked rings.
items.cn: 这个词意为锁链，指一串相连的环节。

items.en: French carried the noun into English, where chain already meant linked metal and then any linked series.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词带入英语，链在英语中先指相连的金属，后指任何相连的系列。

items.en: Animal ecology fixed the compound for a sequence of eaters in the nineteen twenties.
items.cn: 动物生态学在二十世纪二十年代把这个复合词固定为「一连串取食者」的意思。

items.en: Ecologists later stressed that a chain is a simplification cut from a web, and the term kept both uses.
items.cn: 生态学家后来强调链是从网中切出的简化，这个术语同时保留两种用法。

note.en: The first group shares food or chain; the second group is the network and the position vocabulary that surrounds the term.
note.cn: 第一组共用 food 或 chain；第二组是围绕这个术语的网络与位置词汇。

entries.definition: Nourishment taken by an organism, the first element.
entries.definitionCN: 指生物摄取的养料，是前半部分。

entries.definition: A series of linked parts, the second element.
entries.definitionCN: 指一串相连的部分，是后半部分。

entries.definition: The network the chain is cut from.
entries.definitionCN: 指链所从属的网络。

entries.definition: A linked record of handling; the same chain word in law.
entries.definitionCN: 指一串交接记录；同一个「链」字用于法律。

entries.definition: A connected series of vehicles; close in image but a different word.
entries.definitionCN: 指相连的车列；意象相近，但属另一个词。

entries.definition: The full network of feeding links, of which a chain is one path.
entries.definitionCN: 指取食关系的完整网络，链是其中一条路径。

entries.definition: A position on the chain, counted in feeding steps.
entries.definitionCN: 指链上的位置，按取食步数计算。

entries.definition: The movement of captured energy through a system, of which the chain is one route.
entries.definitionCN: 指被固定能量在系统中的移动，链是其中一条路线。

entries.definition: An older term stressing the return of matter rather than a one-way line.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的术语，强调物质回流而不是单向线路。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the linked-ring image, the energy rule and the difference from a web.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「相连环扣」的形象、能量规则以及与网的区别。

normal.en: A chain is rings in a row, which is why the term is linear and why it is a simplification.
normal.cn: 链是一排环扣，这正是这个术语线性、也正是它简化之处。

normal.en: Each step loses most of the energy, so no chain can be very long.
normal.cn: 每一步都损失大部分能量，所以链不可能很长。

normal.en: Food chain is one path; food web is all paths at once.
normal.cn: 食物链是一条路径，食物网是同时展开的所有路径。

normal.en: Top of the food chain is the everyday phrase for an apex predator.
normal.cn: 「食物链顶端」是顶级捕食者的日常说法。

normal.en: Grazing chains start from living plants, detrital chains from dead matter.
normal.cn: 牧食链始于活植物，碎屑链始于死有机质。

abstract.en: A chain is a story told as if there were only one plot, and ecology keeps the simplification because teaching needs a line.
abstract.cn: 链是假设只有一条情节的故事，生态学保留这种简化，因为教学需要一条线。

abstract.en: Energy moves up and matter goes round, and the chain shows only the first half of that double movement.
abstract.cn: 能量往上走，物质绕圈转，链只展示了这场双向运动的前一半。

abstract.en: The higher the link, the more concentrated the world becomes inside one body.
abstract.cn: 环节越高，世界在一个身体里就越浓缩。

examples.en: The food chain here begins with algae attached to the stones.
examples.cn: 这里的食物链始于附着在石头上的藻类。

examples.en: Removing the midge broke the food chain that fed the fish.
examples.cn: 移除这种摇蚊，打断了喂养鱼群的那条食物链。

examples.en: A short food chain loses less energy before reaching the predator.
examples.cn: 较短的食物链在到达捕食者之前损失的能量更少。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「富德 拆恩」——富德是食物，拆恩是链子，把吃与被吃串成一条链子，就是食物链

root: 古英语 fōda「食物」；拉丁语 catena「锁链」→ 古法语 chaine → 英语中表示「链」的名词。两词在二十世纪二十年代的动物生态学中被固定为「一连串取食关系」的术语，后与表示网络的「食物网」相对。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses keep the line in view while changing what it carries: eaters, energy, roles, length, its status as a model, two kinds of chain, toxins, the apex and the break.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项守住这条线，只换它承载的东西：取食者、能量、角色、长度、作为模型的地位、两种链、毒素、顶端与断裂。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vertical row from algae to shrimp to fish to a stooping heron.
core.cn: 核心意象：一幅从藻类到小虾到鱼再到俯冲的鹭的竖排图。

branches.en: THE LINE AND ITS CARGO: a sequence of eaters, and the energy that travels along it.
branches.cn: 线与货物：取食者的序列，以及沿线旅行的能量。

branches.en: THE ROLES AND THE START: producer, consumer and decomposer, with grazing and detrital beginnings.
branches.cn: 角色与起点：生产者、消费者、分解者，以及牧食与碎屑两种起点。

branches.en: THE LIMIT: energy loss at each step caps the number of links.
branches.cn: 限度：每一步的能量损失给环节数上了限。

branches.en: THE ABSTRACTION: a single path cut out of a network for teaching or measurement.
branches.cn: 抽象：为教学或测量从网络中切出的单一路径。

branches.en: THE CONSEQUENCES: toxins concentrating upward, an apex at the end, and a line that snaps when a link is pulled.
branches.cn: 后果：向上浓缩的毒素、末端的顶级者，以及抽掉一环就会断的线。

intro.en: The first element is native Germanic and the second came through French from Latin, so the compound mixes two layers of English.
intro.cn: 前半是日耳曼本族词，后半经法语来自拉丁语，因此这个复合词混合了英语的两个层次。

latinIntro.en: Only the second element has a Latin source, recorded as catena and carried through French.
latinIntro.cn: 只有后半有拉丁语来源，有记录的形式为锁链一词，并经法语传来。

items.example: It names what is eaten.
It names the ordered connection.
It is the recorded source of the second element.
items.exampleCN: 它是后半部分有记录的来源。

items.example: It is the term the chain is contrasted with.
It names the position on the chain.
It names the final position.
It starts the detrital chain.

items.meaning: build-up of a substance in a body
items.example: It travels along the chain.

derivatives.zh: 由该短语换成表示「网」的后半构成，义为「食物网」
由该短语换成表示「循环」的后半构成，义为「食物循环」
由该后半与表示「长度」的词构成，义为「链长」

definition_zh: 考古遗址；保存有古代人类活动遗存并被研究的地点；发掘现场
definition_en: a place where the material remains of past human activity are preserved and studied
core_image: 黄土剖面上露出半截陶罐与石墙基，标尺和刷子放在一旁的托盘里
scene: 荒野的土坡被切开一条整齐的探沟，剖面里露出陶片与墙基，工作人员蹲在网格旁记录编号。 The archaeology site, a place holding ancient remains, yielded pottery that dated the settlement to the Bronze Age.
sceneCN: 这里 archaeology site 指「保存有古代遗存并被研究的地点」（第 1 个义项：具有考古价值的具体地点）；句意为这处考古遗址出土的陶器把聚落年代定在青铜时代。可辨识物件：土坡剖面、探沟、陶片、石墙基、记录网格。

pos.zh: 考古遗址；考古地点（可数，复数 archaeology sites）

senses.title: A place with archaeological remains
senses.definition: a location that holds material traces of past human activity and is studied as such
senses.definitionCN: 保存过去人类活动物质痕迹并作为研究对象的地点
senses.example: The archaeology site yielded pottery that dated the settlement to the Bronze Age.
senses.exampleCN: 这处考古遗址出土的陶器把聚落年代定在青铜时代。
senses.why: archaeology names the study and site names the place, so the phrase is the place where that study works.
senses.whyCN: archaeology 指研究，site 指地点，因此短语就是这门研究作业的地点。

senses.title: An active excavation site
senses.definition: a place currently being dug, recorded and sampled by a team
senses.definitionCN: 正由团队挖掘、记录与取样的地点
senses.example: The archaeology site was closed to visitors during the dig.
senses.exampleCN: 发掘期间，考古现场不对游客开放。
senses.why: a site becomes active when tools arrive, and the phrase then names a workplace rather than a dot on a map.
senses.whyCN: 工具一到，遗址就成为活动场所，此时短语指工作现场而非地图上的一个点。

senses.title: A protected or managed site
senses.definition: a place legally protected, fenced or maintained for preservation and public interpretation
senses.definitionCN: 依法保护、围护或维护以供保存与公众解读的地点
senses.example: The archaeology site is managed by the regional museum.
senses.exampleCN: 这处考古遗址由地区博物馆管理。
senses.why: once a place is valued, it acquires rules, staff and boundaries, and the phrase takes on administration.
senses.whyCN: 一旦地点被珍视，它就有了规则、人员与边界，短语也随之带行政管理色彩。

senses.title: A type of site
senses.definition: a category such as settlement, tomb, city, kiln or workshop
senses.definitionCN: 聚落、墓葬、城址、窑址或作坊等类别
senses.example: Each archaeology site type leaves a different pattern in the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 每一类考古遗址在土壤中留下不同的图案。
senses.why: archaeologists classify places by function, and the phrase can name the class as well as the instance.
senses.whyCN: 考古学家按功能给地点分类，这个短语既可指实例，也可指类别。

senses.title: A registered or listed site
senses.definition: a place entered in an official inventory with a number and a boundary
senses.definitionCN: 以编号与边界录入官方名录的地点
senses.example: The archaeology site appears on the national register.
senses.exampleCN: 这处考古遗址见于国家名录。
senses.why: modern heritage practice turns places into records, and the phrase follows them into the archive.
senses.whyCN: 现代遗产实践把地点变成记录，短语也随之进入档案。

senses.title: An underwater or underground site
senses.definition: a place of remains preserved beneath water, sediment or later construction
senses.definitionCN: 遗存保存在水下、沉积物下或后期建筑之下的地点
senses.example: Divers mapped an archaeology site beneath the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水员绘制了港湾水下的考古遗址。
senses.why: the same definition applies wherever the layers lie, so the phrase extends below the surface.
senses.whyCN: 无论地层在哪里，定义都适用，因此短语延伸到地表之下。

senses.title: Metaphor: a layered place of memory
senses.titleCN: 比喻：层层叠压的记忆之地
senses.definition: by extension, any place where earlier lives remain visible under later ones
senses.definitionCN: 引申指早期生活仍能在后期痕迹下看见的任何地点
senses.example: The old quarter is an archaeology site of the city's habits.
senses.exampleCN: 老城区是这座城市生活习惯的「考古遗址」。
senses.why: the metaphor uses stratigraphy: each generation leaves a layer that the next covers.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻使用地层学：每一代人留下一层，下一代将其覆盖。

senses.title: Abstraction: a readable field of traces
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：可解读的痕迹场
senses.definition: any bounded field of traces that can be read as evidence of a past order
senses.definitionCN: 任何可被解读为过去秩序证据的有界痕迹场
senses.example: A trial is an archaeology site of decisions.
senses.exampleCN: 一场审判是决策的「考古遗址」。
senses.why: the deepest sense removes the soil: what matters is that traces survive in order and can be read.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层抽掉了泥土：重要的是痕迹有序留存并可被解读。

intro.en: Archaeology joins Greek arkhaios 'ancient' to -logia 'study'; site comes from Latin situs 'place'. The phrase is a modern English combination. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: archaeology 把希腊 arkhaios「古老的」与 -logia「学问」结合；site 来自拉丁 situs「地点」。短语是近代英语组合。年代均为约数。

items.en: Arkhaios meant 'ancient, from the beginning', built on arkhē 'beginning, first place'; the deeper origin of arkhē is debated.
items.cn: arkhaios 意为「古老的、自起初的」，由 arkhē「开端、首位」构成；arkhē 的更深来源有争论。

items.en: Arkhaiologia meant 'the study or telling of ancient things'; it joined arkhaios to -logia, from logos 'account, reason'.
items.cn: arkhaiologia 意为「对古老事物的研究或讲述」；它把 arkhaios 与 -logia 结合，后者来自 logos「叙述、理性」。

items.en: The Latinized form archaeologia entered European scholarly language in the seventeenth century, and English archaeology followed.
items.cn: 拉丁化形式 archaeologia 在十七世纪进入欧洲学术语言，英语 archaeology 随之而来。

items.en: Situs meant 'a place, position, situation', from sinere 'to let, set down'; its past participle situs also gave the English adjective site-related forms.
items.cn: situs 意为「地点、位置、处境」，来自 sinere「放置、允许」；其过去分词 situs 也衍生英语中与 site 相关的形式。

items.en: Archaeology site is a modern English phrase; the more usual form in professional writing is archaeological site, and both are current.
items.cn: archaeology site 是近代英语短语；专业写作中更常见的形式是 archaeological site，两者都在使用。

items.en: Source uncertain (first attestation and root shapes): no dictionary fixes the first use of the exact phrase, the origin of arkhē is debated, and the pre-Latin root of sinere is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与词根形态）：没有辞书确定这一确切短语的首次使用；arkhē 的来源有争论，sinere 的拉丁语前词根属重构。

note.en: Group one holds site and archaeology words constantly confused with the phrase; group two holds neighbouring heritage ideas.
note.cn: 第一组是常与该短语混淆的 site 与 archaeology 类词；第二组是遗产领域的邻近概念。

entries.definition: The standard adjective-plus-noun wording; archaeology site is an abbreviated variant used in some writing.
entries.definitionCN: 标准形容词加名词说法；archaeology site 是某些写作中的简略变体。

entries.definition: The study of past human activity through material remains; it names the field, not a place.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过物质遗存研究过去人类活动的学科；命名领域，不指地点。

entries.definition: A practitioner of archaeology; a site is where that practitioner works.
entries.definitionCN: 指从事考古学的人；遗址是其工作地点。

entries.definition: A place currently being dug; an archaeology site may be protected and unexcavated.
entries.definitionCN: 指正在被挖掘的地点；考古遗址可能受保护且尚未发掘。

entries.definition: The standing or fallen remains of a structure; a site can be ruinous or buried and invisible.
entries.definitionCN: 指建筑物的残存或倒塌部分；遗址可以是有残迹的，也可以完全埋在地下。

entries.definition: A structure built to commemorate or preserve memory; it may be part of a site but is not the site itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指为纪念或保存记忆而建的构筑物；它可能是遗址的一部分，但不等于遗址。

entries.definition: A place recognised for cultural or natural value; the label comes from preservation policy rather than from research.
entries.definitionCN: 指因文化或自然价值而受认可的地点；这一标签来自保护政策，而非研究。

entries.definition: An excavation, especially in informal speech; it names the work, not the place.
entries.definitionCN: 指发掘，尤用于口语；命名工作，而非地点。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Greek roots, the Latin word for place and the stratigraphic picture.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：希腊词根、拉丁语「地点」一词，以及地层剖面图。

normal.en: arkhaios 'ancient' + -logia 'study': the study of ancient things.
normal.cn: arkhaios「古老」+ -logia「学问」：对古老事物的研究。

normal.en: site is from Latin situs, a place set down.
normal.cn: site 来自拉丁 situs，指被放置下来的地点。

normal.en: The family runs archaeology, archaeological, archaeologist, site, situate, situation.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 archaeology、archaeological、archaeologist、site、situate、situation。

normal.en: A site is read in layers: the lowest layer is usually the oldest.
normal.cn: 遗址按层解读：最下面的层通常最古老。

normal.en: The usual professional wording is archaeological site.
normal.cn: 专业写作中通行的说法是 archaeological site。

abstract.en: Picture a page of earth where each generation wrote one line over the last.
abstract.cn: 想象一页泥土，每一代人在上一行之上写一行。

abstract.en: Picture a city whose older streets still shape the newer ones above them.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市，旧街道仍在塑造其上的新街道。

abstract.en: Picture a room where furniture was moved but the dents in the floor remain.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间，家具搬走了，地板上的凹痕还在。

examples.en: The archaeology site was fenced before the road was widened.
examples.cn: 在道路拓宽之前，这处考古遗址被围护起来。

examples.en: Students mapped the archaeology site with a simple grid.
examples.cn: 学生们用简单网格绘制了这处考古遗址。

examples.en: A single pottery shard can date an archaeology site.
examples.cn: 一片陶片就能确定一处考古遗址的年代。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「archaeology（考古）+ site（地点）」——考古学家工作的那片地点 → 考古遗址

root: archaeology 来自希腊 arkhaiologia = arkhaios「古老的」+ -logia「学问」，arkhē 为「开端」；site 来自拉丁 situs「地点」，源于 sinere「放置」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings move from a place holding remains, through the active dig and the managed and classified site, to the registered, underwater and buried place, then to a layered metaphor and finally to any readable field of traces.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从保存遗存的地点出发，经过活动中的发掘现场、受管理与分类的遗址，再到登记、水下与埋藏的地点，再到层叠比喻，最后落到任何可解读的痕迹场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cut slope showing a broken jar and a stone footing, with a ruler and brush on a tray.
core.cn: 核心意象：切开的土坡露出破陶罐与石墙基，托盘上放着标尺与刷子。

branches.en: THE PLACE AND THE WORK: a dot on the map becomes a workplace when the tools arrive.
branches.cn: 地点与工作：地图上的一个点在工具到来时变成工作现场。

branches.en: CARE AND CATEGORY: protection gives boundaries, function gives types.
branches.cn: 照管与类别：保护给出边界，功能给出类型。

branches.en: THE RECORD AND THE DEPTH: registers name places, and layers hide them.
branches.cn: 记录与深度：名录给地点命名，地层把它们藏起。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: any old quarter can be read as stratified memory.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何老城区都可读作层叠的记忆。

branches.en: TRACES WITHOUT SOIL: the deepest sense is ordered evidence that can be read.
branches.cn: 无土的痕迹：最深的一层是有序、可解读的证据。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Greek-derived discipline word with a Latin-derived place word, so both halves are readable.
intro.cn: 这个短语把希腊来源的学科词与拉丁来源的地点词结合，两部分都可读。

latinIntro.en: Greek arkhaios and logos give archaeology and archaeological; Latin situs and sinere give site, situate and situation.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 arkhaios 与 logos 衍生 archaeology 与 archaeological；拉丁 situs 与 sinere 衍生 site、situate 与 situation。

items.example: The prefix marks the age of the material.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出材料的古老。

items.example: The suffix turns a subject into a discipline.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把主题变成学科。

items.example: Archaeology reads objects as evidence.
items.exampleCN: 考古学把物件读作证据。

items.example: The report used the archaeological record.
The archaeologist brushed the surface.
The site lay beside a dry stream.
items.exampleCN: 这处地点在一条干涸小溪旁。

items.example: The Latin noun supplied the English word site.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词提供英语 site。

items.example: The village was situated above the flood line.

items.meaning: a position or set of circumstances
items.example: The word also means a state of affairs.
