definition_zh: 周期性的；定期的；元素周期表的；周期函数的；周期性发作的；天体周期性回归的；掉尾句的；周期性结构的；间歇反复的
definition_en: repeating at fixed intervals of time or space, happening at regular planned intervals, or relating to a cycle such as the table of elements or a mathematical function
core_image: 钟摆每回到同一个位置就敲一下，每两下之间的间隔都一样长
scene: 实验室的仪器每隔六小时自动校准一次，值班表上记着这件事。 The instrument calibrates itself at periodic intervals of six hours.
sceneCN: 这里 periodic 是「定期的」（第 2 个义项：按计划在固定间隔重复进行）；句意：这台仪器按六小时的固定间隔定期自行校准。

pos.zh: 周期性的；定期的；周期的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Repeating at equal intervals
senses.definition: recurring after the same interval of time or space, so that each cycle resembles the one before
senses.definitionCN: 在相同的时间或空间间隔之后再次出现，使每个周期都与前一个相似
senses.example: The signal is periodic, with one peak every two seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 这个信号是周期性的，每两秒出现一个峰。
senses.why: Greek periodos is 'a going around', from peri- 'around' plus hodos 'way'. A pendulum goes around its arc and returns: periodic means the return happens at the same interval every time.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 periodos 是“绕行一圈”，由 peri-“绕”加 hodos“路”构成。钟摆沿弧线绕一圈又回来：periodic 意为每次都在同样的间隔后回来。

senses.title: Done at planned intervals
senses.definition: carried out at regular planned intervals as part of maintenance, inspection, or routine
senses.definitionCN: 作为维护、检查或例行工作的一部分，按固定的计划间隔执行
senses.example: Periodic maintenance prevents most of these failures.
senses.exampleCN: 定期维护能防止这类故障中的大部分。
senses.why: A schedule is a pendulum drawn on paper. The word marks the planned return of a task, not the physical swinging, so routine work acquires the sense.
senses.whyCN: 日程表是画在纸上的钟摆。这个词标记的是任务按计划返回，而不是物理的摆动，例行工作于是获得这一义项。

senses.title: Of the table of elements
senses.definition: relating to the arrangement of chemical elements by increasing atomic number, in which properties repeat in rows and columns
senses.definitionCN: 指化学元素按原子序数递增排列、性质在行与列中重复的排布方式
senses.example: Mendeleev left gaps in his periodic table for elements not yet found.
senses.exampleCN: 门捷列夫在周期表里为尚未发现的元素留下了空格。
senses.why: Chemistry found that properties come back after a certain number of elements, like a pendulum returning. The table is literally a map of returns, hence the periodic table.
senses.whyCN: 化学发现性质在经过一定数目的元素之后会重新出现，就像钟摆回来。这张表字面上就是一张“回归地图”，所以叫元素周期表。

senses.title: Of a function that repeats
senses.definition: of a mathematical function, having the property that its value repeats after a fixed interval of the variable
senses.definitionCN: 指数学函数在自变量经过固定间隔后取值重复的性质
senses.example: Sine is a periodic function with a period of two pi.
senses.exampleCN: 正弦是周期为二π的周期函数。
senses.why: Mathematics strips the image to its skeleton: a value returns to the same height after the same step. The word then names pure repetition, with no clock or pendulum required.
senses.whyCN: 数学把这个意象剥到骨架：经过同样的步长之后，数值回到同样的高度。此时这个词命名的是纯然的重复，不需要钟或钟摆。

senses.title: Of symptoms that return
senses.definition: of a medical condition, recurring in episodes at intervals rather than staying constant
senses.definitionCN: 指医学症状以间隔性的发作形式反复出现，而不是持续不变
senses.example: Periodic fever brings chills every few weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 周期性发热每隔几周就会带来寒战。
senses.why: The body can behave like a clock: healthy between attacks, then returning to the same state. Medicine uses the word for that rhythm, which is why it appears in names of syndromes.
senses.whyCN: 身体也能像钟一样运行：发作之间是健康的，然后又回到同样的状态。医学用这个词描述这种节律，所以它出现在多种综合征的名称里。

senses.title: Of a comet or orbit that returns
senses.definition: of a comet, orbit, or astronomical event, returning at intervals that can be predicted
senses.definitionCN: 指彗星、轨道或天文事件以可预测的间隔回归
senses.example: Halley's comet is periodic, returning roughly every seventy-six years.
senses.exampleCN: 哈雷彗星是周期性的，大约每七十六年回归一次。
senses.why: The earliest scientific sense is astronomical: a body goes around and comes back. The sky provided the first proof that some returns can be predicted exactly.
senses.whyCN: 最早的科学义项是天文学的：天体绕行一圈又回来。天空提供了最早的证据，证明有些回归可以被精确预测。

senses.title: Of a sentence that delays its point
senses.titleCN: 把重点留到句末的掉尾句
senses.definition: of a sentence whose main clause is held back until the end, so that the meaning arrives with a closing turn
senses.definitionCN: 指主要从句被留到句末、意义在收尾处才落下的句子
senses.example: A periodic sentence keeps the reader waiting for the verb.
senses.exampleCN: 掉尾句让读者一直等到动词才落地。
senses.why: Rhetoric borrowed the word for a shape that returns: the sentence suspends, then closes on the point. The period at the end is the pendulum's click.
senses.whyCN: 修辞学借这个词形容一种“回归”的形状：句子先悬着，最后落在重点上。句末的句号就是钟摆那一声。

senses.title: Of a repeating structure in matter
senses.titleCN: 物质中重复排列的结构
senses.definition: of a crystal, lattice, or material, having a structure that repeats at regular spacings
senses.definitionCN: 指晶体、晶格或材料具有按规则间距重复的结构
senses.example: The alloy has a periodic lattice that diffracts X-rays.
senses.exampleCN: 这种合金具有能衍射 X 射线的周期性晶格。
senses.why: Atoms can stand in rows like the marks on a ruler. The same equal spacing that makes a sound periodic makes a crystal periodic, and diffraction is the proof.
senses.whyCN: 原子可以像尺子上的刻度一样排成行。使声音成为周期性的那种等间距，也使晶体成为周期性的，衍射就是证据。

senses.title: Coming back in waves
senses.definition: of events such as outbreaks, shortages, or protests, appearing again after quiet intervals rather than steadily
senses.definitionCN: 指疫情、短缺或抗议等事件在平静间隔之后再次出现，而非持续不断
senses.example: Periodic droughts shaped the history of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 周期性的干旱塑造了这座山谷的历史。
senses.why: The clock is social or ecological rather than mechanical. The word still promises a return, but the interval may be irregular and the cause unknown.
senses.whyCN: 这时的钟是社会或生态的，而不是机械的。这个词仍承诺会回来，但间隔可能不规律，原因也可能不明。

intro.en: Periodic comes from Greek periodikos 'of a period', from periodos 'a going around, circuit', built on peri- 'around' and hodos 'way, journey'. English took it in the 17th century for things that recur at fixed intervals, first in medicine and astronomy. The chemical sense dates from Mendeleev's periodic law of 1869, and the grammatical sense from the same century's study of sentence shape.
intro.cn: periodic 来自希腊语 periodikos“周期的”，出自 periodos“绕行一圈、循环”，由 peri-“绕”与 hodos“路、行程”构成。英语在 17 世纪借入，指按固定间隔重现的事物，最早用于医学与天文学。化学义来自 1869 年门捷列夫的元素周期律，语法义则来自同一世纪对句子形态的研究。

items.en: Hodos means 'way, road, journey'. With peri- 'around', periodos is 'a going around', used of a circuit, a cycle of time, or the path of a heavenly body.
items.cn: hodos 意为“路、道路、行程”。加上 peri-“绕”，periodos 就是“绕行一圈”，用于环路、时间循环或天体路径。

items.en: English periodic first describes diseases and orbits that return at set intervals. The word inherits the Greek image of a circuit rather than the modern clock.
items.cn: 英语 periodic 最早描述按固定间隔回归的疾病与轨道。这个词继承的是希腊语“绕行”的意象，而不是现代的钟表。

items.en: Mendeleev's periodic law states that elemental properties repeat after certain intervals of atomic weight, and the periodic table becomes the standard name for its chart.
items.cn: 门捷列夫的元素周期律指出元素性质在一定的原子量间隔后重复，periodic table 成为这张表的标准名称。

items.en: Mathematics adopts periodic for functions whose values repeat, and rhetoric adopts periodic sentence for a sentence whose point is withheld to the close.
items.cn: 数学用 periodic 指取值重复的函数，修辞学用 periodic sentence 指把重点留到句末的句子。

items.en: The -ic ending is Greek -ikos 'of, relating to'. The noun period itself had entered English earlier from the same Greek word, which is why the adjective and the noun share a stem across two languages.
items.cn: -ic 词尾是希腊 -ikos“关于……的”。名词 period 本身更早从同一个希腊词进入英语，所以形容词与名词在两种语言之间共享词干。

items.en: Periodontal also begins with peri-, but its second element is odous, odont- 'tooth', so it means 'around the tooth'. Periodic's second element is hodos 'way'. The shared peri- is a prefix, not a family.
items.cn: periodontal 也以 peri- 开头，但第二部分是 odous、odont-“牙”，所以意为“牙周”。periodic 的第二部分是 hodos“路”。共享的 peri- 只是前缀，不是同一词族。

note.en: The first group separates period's family from the peri- prefix that looks like kinship. The second group compares regular, recurrent, cyclical, and intermittent, the four words closest to periodic.
note.cn: 第一组把 period 的词族与看起来像亲戚、其实只是共享 peri- 前缀的词分开。第二组比较 regular、recurrent、cyclical、intermittent，这四个词最接近 periodic。

entries.definition: a length of time, a cycle, a full stop, or a class hour. Periodic is the adjective of its repeating sense.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间、一个周期、一个句号或一节课。periodic 是其重复义的形容词。

entries.definition: a magazine or journal published at regular intervals, or an adjective meaning 'recurring'. The noun sense belongs to publishing, not to science.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定间隔出版的杂志或期刊，或作形容词表示“周期性发生的”。名词义属于出版业，不属于科学。

entries.definition: the quality of being periodic, often measured as a rate. It names the property, while periodic names the thing that has it.
entries.definitionCN: 具有周期性的性质，常以比率测量。它命名属性，而 periodic 命名具有该属性的事物。

entries.definition: relating to the tissue around the teeth. Its second element is odont- 'tooth', so only the prefix matches periodic.
entries.definitionCN: 与牙齿周围组织有关的。它的第二部分是 odont-“牙”，所以只有前缀与 periodic 相同。

entries.definition: occurring at even, predictable intervals. It stresses the evenness of the spacing, while periodic stresses the return itself.
entries.definitionCN: 以均匀、可预测的间隔发生。它强调间隔的均匀，而 periodic 强调“回来”这件事本身。

entries.definition: occurring again, often repeatedly and sometimes without a fixed interval. It is weaker than periodic on timing.
entries.definitionCN: 再次发生的，常反复出现，有时没有固定间隔。它在时间规律性上比 periodic 弱。

entries.definition: following a repeating sequence of stages, as in a business cycle. It stresses the order of phases; periodic stresses the equal spacing.
entries.definitionCN: 遵循重复的阶段序列，如商业周期。它强调阶段的顺序，而 periodic 强调相等的间隔。

entries.definition: stopping and starting at irregular intervals. It lacks the promise of equal spacing that periodic carries.
entries.definitionCN: 以不规律间隔时断时续。它没有 periodic 所带的“间隔相等”这一承诺。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: peri- 'around', hodos 'way', periodos, Mendeleev's 1869 law, the Fourier sense, and the odont- trap.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：peri-“绕”、hodos“路”、periodos、1869 年门捷列夫周期律、傅里叶的数学义，以及 odont- 陷阱。

normal.en: Periodos is a going around: peri- 'around' plus hodos 'way', so periodic means the thing comes back by the same road.
normal.cn: periodos 是绕行一圈：peri-“绕”加 hodos“路”，所以 periodic 指事物沿同一条路回来。

normal.en: A pendulum returns to the same point after the same time: that return is the whole image behind periodic.
normal.cn: 钟摆经过同样的时间回到同一点：这个回归就是 periodic 背后的全部意象。

normal.en: Mendeleev's table is called periodic because properties come back after a fixed number of elements, exactly like a returning swing.
normal.cn: 门捷列夫的表被称为周期表，因为性质在固定数目的元素之后重新出现，就像摆回来一样。

normal.en: Periodontal looks like a relative but its root is odont- 'tooth': peri- is only a prefix, not a family tie.
normal.cn: periodontal 看起来像亲戚，但词根是 odont-“牙”：peri- 只是前缀，不是血缘。

normal.en: The grammatical periodic sentence delays its point to the end, so the meaning clicks into place like the pendulum at the top of its swing.
normal.cn: 语法上的掉尾句把重点留到句末，意义像钟摆摆到最高点那样“咔”地落定。

abstract.en: A clock is a machine built to make the same moment happen again; periodic is the name of that promise.
abstract.cn: 钟表是一台让同一时刻再次发生的机器；periodic 就是这个承诺的名字。

abstract.en: The tide does not remember the last high water, yet it arrives on time; repetition needs no memory.
abstract.cn: 潮水不记得上一次高潮，却准时到来；重复不需要记忆。

abstract.en: A crystal is a silence made of equal spacing, and X-rays are the ears that hear it.
abstract.cn: 晶体是一片由等间距构成的沉默，X 射线就是听见它的耳朵。

examples.en: The doctor ordered periodic blood tests over the next year.
examples.cn: 医生要求在未来一年里定期做血检。

examples.en: Sodium and potassium sit in the same column of the periodic table.
examples.cn: 钠和钾位于元素周期表的同一列。

examples.en: The waveform is periodic but not a simple sine wave.
examples.cn: 这个波形是周期性的，但不是简单的正弦波。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮瑞奥迪克」——皮瑞围着操场一圈一圈地跑，每圈都在同一个点“打卡” → periodic 周期性的；定期的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 希腊 periodos「绕行一圈、循环」，由 peri-「绕」+ hodos「路」构成，形容词为 periodikos；后缀 -ic（希腊 -ikos）表“关于……的”。核心是「沿同一条路绕一圈，又在同样的间隔后回到原点」。periodontal（peri- + odont-「牙」）只是共享前缀，词根不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of periodic all describe a return after an interval. What changes is the road and the clock: a pendulum, a maintenance schedule, the table of elements, a function, a fever, a comet, a sentence, a crystal lattice, or a drought.
sensesIntro.cn: periodic 的九个义项都描述“经过一段间隔后回来”。变化的是那条路与那座钟：钟摆、维护日程、元素表、函数、发热、彗星、句子、晶格，还是干旱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pendulum that returns to the same point every time, with equal spacing between the clicks.
core.cn: 核心意象：钟摆每次都回到同一点，每两声之间的间隔相等。

branches.en: THE PURE RETURN: equal intervals in time or space, and the mathematical function that repeats its value.
branches.cn: 纯粹的回归：时间或空间上的相等间隔，以及取值重复的数学函数。

branches.en: HUMAN SHAPES: planned routines such as maintenance, and the sentence whose point waits until the end.
branches.cn: 人造的形状：维护等计划性例行工作，以及把重点留到句末的句子。

branches.en: MATTER ARRANGED: the table of elements and the repeating lattice of a crystal.
branches.cn: 排列起来的物质：元素周期表，以及晶体中重复的晶格。

branches.en: THE RETURN OF EVENTS: fevers that come back and droughts or outbreaks that arrive in waves.
branches.cn: 事件的回归：反复发作的发热，以及一波一波到来的干旱或疫情。

branches.en: THE SKY: comets and orbits whose returns can be predicted years ahead.
branches.cn: 天空：可以提前多年预测回归的彗星与轨道。

intro.en: Periodic is Greek periodikos, from periodos (peri- 'around' + hodos 'way') plus -ikos, the adjective suffix English renders as -ic. English also has the noun period, taken earlier from the same Greek word, and the derived adverb periodically.
intro.cn: periodic 是希腊语 periodikos，出自 periodos（peri-“绕”+ hodos“路”）加 -ikos，即英语写作 -ic 的形容词后缀。英语还有更早从同一个希腊词借入的名词 period，以及派生副词 periodically。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here: the word is Greek through and through. Latin only supplied the connecting forms periodus and periodicus in scientific writing, which is why the spelling reached English unchanged.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁来源：它从头到尾都是希腊语。拉丁语只在科学写作中提供了连接形式 periodus 与 periodicus，所以拼写原样进入英语。

items.meaning: of a going around; recurring at intervals
items.meaningCN: 属于绕行一圈的；按间隔重现的（-ic 形容词后缀）
items.example: Periodic checks caught the leak early.
items.exampleCN: 定期检查及早发现了泄漏。

items.structure: Greek periodos 'a going around', via Latin periodus
items.meaning: a length of time, a cycle, a full stop
items.meaningCN: 一段时间、一个周期、一个句号
items.example: The period of the wave is 0.2 seconds.
items.exampleCN: 这个波的周期是 0.2 秒。

items.meaningCN: 按固定间隔地；定期地（-ally 副词）
items.example: The database is backed up periodically.

items.meaning: the quality of recurring at intervals
items.meaningCN: 按间隔重现的性质；周期性（-ity 性质名词）
items.example: The periodicity of the signal is not exact.
items.exampleCN: 这个信号的周期性并不精确。

items.meaning: a publication issued at regular intervals
items.meaningCN: 按固定间隔出版的刊物；期刊（-al 构成名词）
items.example: The library subscribes to forty periodicals.
items.exampleCN: 图书馆订阅了四十种期刊。

items.meaningCN: 不按固定间隔重复的；非周期的（a- 否定）
items.example: The aperiodic tiling never repeats itself.
items.exampleCN: 这种非周期拼贴永不自我重复。

items.example: The hodos inside period once meant a journey along a road.
items.exampleCN: “时期”一词里的 hodos 曾指沿路的一段行程。

items.example: Peri- appears in words describing a circuit, such as a perimeter.
items.exampleCN: peri- 出现在描述环行一周的词语里，例如表示“周长”的词。

items.meaningCN: 牙周的（peri- 绕 + odont- 牙）
items.example: Periodontal disease affects the gums.

latinEntries.meaning: a circuit, a cycle, a period of time
latinEntries.meaningCN: 一圈、一个循环、一段时间

definition_zh: 磷
definition_en: the chemical element of atomic number 15, a non-metal that occurs in several coloured forms and glows faintly in the dark
core_image: 暗室中一块蜡状白色固体发出淡绿色微光，旁边是一盒火柴
scene: 这里指「磷」。 In the dark, the white phosphorus on the stick glowed with a faint green light.
sceneCN: 这里 phosphorus 指「白磷」（第 2 个义项：会自燃、在暗处发光的同素异形体）；它在黑暗中缓慢氧化，发出淡绿微光。图中可辨识物件：暗室、白磷块、淡绿光晕、防火手套。

pos.zh: 磷（不可数；化学符号 P）

senses.title: The element
senses.definition: the chemical element with atomic number 15, a non-metal essential to life and to fertiliser
senses.definitionCN: 原子序数为 15 的元素，非金属，为生命与肥料所必需
senses.example: Phosphorus has fifteen protons and occurs in several allotropes.
senses.exampleCN: 磷有十五个质子，并以多种同素异形体存在。
senses.why: The name is used for the element as a whole, so it covers the white, red and black forms alike.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字用于整个元素，因此白磷、红磷与黑磷都适用。

senses.title: White phosphorus
senses.titleCN: 白磷：会自燃与发光的蜡状固体
senses.definition: the waxy, highly reactive form that ignites in air and glows faintly in the dark, and is also toxic
senses.definitionCN: 蜡状、极易反应的同素异形体，在空气中自燃，暗处发微光，且有毒性
senses.example: White phosphorus must be stored under water to keep it from igniting.
senses.exampleCN: 白磷必须保存在水下，以免自燃。
senses.why: Its glow is the very reason for the name, since Greek phosphoros meant 'light-bearer'.
senses.whyCN: 它的发光正是名字的由来，因为希腊 phosphoros 意为「带光者」。

senses.title: Red phosphorus
senses.titleCN: 红磷：火柴盒上的安全形态
senses.definition: the safer, less reactive allotrope used on matchbox surfaces and in flame retardants
senses.definitionCN: 较安全、较不活泼的同素异形体，用于火柴盒面与阻燃剂
senses.example: Red phosphorus on the box turns friction into a flame.
senses.exampleCN: 盒面上的红磷把摩擦变成火焰。
senses.why: Chemistry names the allotropes by colour, so the same element appears under adjectives rather than new nouns.
senses.whyCN: 化学按颜色给同素异形体命名，于是同一元素以形容词形式出现，而不是另造名词。

senses.title: In DNA and ATP
senses.titleCN: 核酸与能量分子中的磷
senses.definition: the element as bound in phosphate groups that link DNA backbones and store energy in ATP
senses.definitionCN: 结合在磷酸基团中的元素，连接 DNA 骨架并在 ATP 中储存能量
senses.example: Phosphorus in the sugar-phosphate backbone gives DNA its negative charge.
senses.exampleCN: 糖-磷酸骨架中的磷赋予 DNA 负电荷。
senses.why: Life's energy currency is a phosphate chain, so the element name appears wherever energy transfer is discussed.
senses.whyCN: 生命的能量货币是一条磷酸链，因此凡讨论能量转移处都会出现这个元素名。

senses.title: Bones and teeth
senses.titleCN: 骨骼与牙齿：羟基磷灰石中的磷
senses.definition: the element stored in bone mineral as calcium phosphate, the main solid of skeleton and teeth
senses.definitionCN: 以磷酸钙形式储存在骨矿物中的元素，是骨骼与牙齿的主要固体成分
senses.example: Nearly all the body's phosphorus sits in the skeleton.
senses.exampleCN: 人体几乎全部的磷都储存在骨骼里。
senses.why: Bone is a mineral crystal, so the element that builds it is discussed as a reserve as well as a nutrient.
senses.whyCN: 骨是一种矿物晶体，因此构成它的元素既被当作养分，也被当作储备。

senses.title: Fertiliser and phosphate rock
senses.titleCN: 磷肥与磷矿：农业的三大养分之一
senses.definition: the nutrient mined as phosphate rock and applied to soil as fertiliser
senses.definitionCN: 以磷矿石开采、作为肥料施入土壤的养分
senses.example: Phosphorus is one of the three main nutrients in fertiliser.
senses.exampleCN: 磷是肥料中三大主要养分之一。
senses.why: Agriculture names the nutrient by the element, even though the bag contains phosphate salts.
senses.whyCN: 农业以元素名来称呼这种养分，尽管袋子里装的是磷酸盐。

senses.title: Eutrophication
senses.titleCN: 富营养化：磷过量引发藻华
senses.definition: the element as a pollutant that limits or, when excessive, overfeeds freshwater algae
senses.definitionCN: 作为污染物的元素，在淡水里限制藻类生长，过量时则使其疯长
senses.example: Extra phosphorus from detergent runoff fed the algal bloom.
senses.exampleCN: 洗涤剂径流带来的额外磷助长了藻华。
senses.why: Because freshwater algae are usually phosphorus-limited, a small excess changes the whole lake.
senses.whyCN: 由于淡水藻类通常受磷限制，少量过量就能改变整个湖泊。

senses.title: The morning star
senses.titleCN: 启明星：名字里的「带光者」
senses.definition: the sense carried by the name, which was an epithet of the planet Venus as the morning star before it named the element
senses.definitionCN: 名字携带的义项：在成为元素名之前，它是金星作为启明星的称号
senses.example: The word phosphorus meant 'light-bearer' long before it meant element fifteen.
senses.exampleCN: 在表示 15 号元素之前很久，phosphorus 的意思就是「带光者」。
senses.why: Hennig Brand named the glowing substance after the star, so the old celestial sense is still readable in the word.
senses.whyCN: 布兰德以那颗星为发光的物质命名，因此旧的天文义至今仍能从词中读出。

intro.en: Phosphorus is Latin for the morning star, borrowed from Greek phosphoros 'light-bearer'. The element took the name because it glows in the dark.
intro.cn: phosphorus 是拉丁语「启明星」，借自希腊 phosphoros「带光者」。这种元素因在暗处发光而得名。

items.en: Greek phos, photos meant 'light'. It is related to phaos and phainein 'to show, to appear', the root behind English phenomenon and fantasy.
items.cn: 希腊 phos、photos 意为「光」，与 phaos 及 phainein「显现、出现」相关，后者是英语 phenomenon、fantasy 的词根。

items.en: The second element comes from pherein 'to carry', so phosphoros is literally 'light-carrying'. The same verb gives English -phore and metaphor.
items.cn: 第二部分出自 pherein「携带」，因此 phosphoros 字面就是「带着光的」。同一动词也给英语留下 -phore 与 metaphor。

items.en: Latin phosphorus named the morning star, that is Venus at dawn, and was used as an epithet for things that bring light.
items.cn: 拉丁 phosphorus 指启明星，即黎明时的金星，也用作带来光明之物的称号。

items.en: Hennig Brand isolated a glowing substance from urine in 1669 and called it phosphorus, after the star, because it shone in the dark.
items.cn: 1669 年亨尼格·布兰德从尿液中分离出一种发光物质，因它在暗处发亮而以那颗星命名，称之为 phosphorus。

items.en: Later chemistry kept the name for element 15, while the adjective phosphoric was reserved for its higher acid and phosphorous for the lower one.
items.cn: 后来的化学把这一名称留给 15 号元素，同时把形容词 phosphoric 留给高价酸、phosphorous 留给低价形态。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the Indo-European root behind Greek phos is reconstructed, not recorded; and the exact date when phosphorus replaced the older Latin star name in English chemistry is uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定：希腊 phos 背后的印欧词根属重构而非有记录；phosphorus 在英语化学中取代旧拉丁星名的确切年代亦存疑。

note.en: The first group holds words whose endings differ by a single letter and mean different oxidation states; the second holds neighbouring substances that are often confused with the element.
note.cn: 第一组是词尾仅差一个字母、却表示不同氧化态的词；第二组是常与元素本身混淆的邻近物质。

entries.definition: An adjective for the lower oxidation state, as in phosphorous acid. It is spelled with -ous, while the element noun ends in -us.
entries.definitionCN: 表示较低氧化态的形容词，如亚磷酸。它拼作 -ous，而元素名词以 -us 结尾。

entries.definition: An adjective for the higher oxidation state, as in phosphoric acid. It never names the element itself.
entries.definitionCN: 表示较高氧化态的形容词，如磷酸。它从不指元素本身。

entries.definition: A salt or ester containing the PO4 group, such as calcium phosphate in bone. Phosphorus is the element; phosphate is one of its commonest compounds.
entries.definitionCN: 含 PO₄ 基团的盐或酯，如骨中的磷酸钙。phosphorus 是元素，phosphate 是它最常见的化合物之一。

entries.definition: The slow emission of light after exposure to radiation, named after phosphorus because both glow in the dark.
entries.definitionCN: 受辐射后缓慢发光的现象，因二者都在暗处发光而以磷命名。

entries.definition: A yellow non-metal that also burns and is mined for fertiliser and chemicals. It is often mistaken for phosphorus in old match recipes.
entries.definitionCN: 一种黄色非金属，也能燃烧，并用于肥料与化工。在旧式火柴配方中常与磷混淆。

entries.definition: The metal that combines with phosphate to form bone mineral. Bones need both, so the two are usually discussed together.
entries.definitionCN: 与磷酸结合形成骨矿物的金属。骨骼两者都需，因此常被一起讨论。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek phos 'light' + phoros 'bearing': the light-bearer, first a star and then a glowing element.
normal.cn: 希腊 phos「光」+ phoros「携带」：带光者，先是星辰，后是发光的元素。

normal.en: The family runs phosphate, phosphoric, phosphorous, phosphide, phosphorylate and phospholipid.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 phosphate、phosphoric、phosphorous、phosphide、phosphorylate、phospholipid。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: white phosphorus, red phosphorus, phosphorus cycle, phosphorus deficiency.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：白磷、红磷、磷循环、缺磷。

normal.en: The element is stored under water because white phosphorus ignites in air.
normal.cn: 这种元素保存在水下，因为白磷在空气中会自燃。

normal.en: Phosphorus is one of the three main fertiliser nutrients, beside nitrogen and potassium.
normal.cn: 磷是肥料三大主要养分之一，与氮、钾并列。

abstract.en: Picture a dark room where a lump of wax-like solid gives off a faint green glow.
abstract.cn: 想象一间暗室，一块蜡状固体散出淡淡的绿光。

abstract.en: Picture a matchbox surface that turns a short scrape into a flame.
abstract.cn: 想象火柴盒面把一次短促的摩擦变成火焰。

abstract.en: Picture a lake turning green as an invisible nutrient tips the balance.
abstract.cn: 想象一种看不见的养分打破平衡，湖面转绿。

examples.en: Phosphorus is essential for ATP, the cell's energy currency.
examples.cn: 磷是细胞能量货币 ATP 的必需成分。

examples.en: The mine supplies phosphate rock rich in phosphorus.
examples.cn: 这座矿山供应富含磷的磷矿石。

examples.en: White phosphorus burns through clothing and is banned in some weapons.
examples.cn: 白磷能烧穿衣物，在某些武器中被禁用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「phos（光）+ phoros（带着）」——在暗处发光的元素 → phosphorus 磷

root: 希腊 phos「光」+ pherein「携带」→ phosphoros「带光者」→ 拉丁 phosphorus（启明星）→ 英语 phosphorus 磷。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one element from the periodic table through white and red forms, DNA, bone, fertiliser, pollution and the star name inside the word.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一个元素从周期表走进白磷与红磷、DNA、骨骼、肥料、污染，最后落在词里那颗星的名字上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a waxy lump glowing green in the dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：暗处一块蜡状固体发出绿光。

branches.en: THE ATOM: element 15 exists in several allotropes, which the next senses name by colour.
branches.cn: 原子：15 号元素有多个同素异形体，随后几个义项按颜色为它们命名。

branches.en: ALLOTROPES: one glows and burns, the other is safe enough for a matchbox.
branches.cn: 同素异形体：一个会发光自燃，另一个安全到能放在火柴盒上。

branches.en: INFORMATION: phosphate groups give DNA its charge and ATP its energy.
branches.cn: 信息：磷酸基团赋予 DNA 电荷、赋予 ATP 能量。

branches.en: BODY AND FIELD: the same element is bone mineral and the bag of fertiliser.
branches.cn: 身体与田野：同一元素既是骨矿物，也是那袋肥料。

branches.en: EXCESS AND ORIGIN: too much phosphorus ruins a lake, while the name still remembers a star.
branches.cn: 过量与起源：磷太多会毁掉湖泊，而名字仍记着一颗星。

intro.en: Phosphorus is a Greek compound meaning 'light-bearer', taken into Latin as a star name and then attached to a glowing element.

latinIntro.en: Latin phosphorus kept the Greek meaning, and later chemistry built phosphoric, phosphorous, phosphate and phosphide on the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 phosphorus 保留了希腊词义，后来的化学又用同一词干造出 phosphoric、phosphorous、phosphate 与 phosphide。

definition_zh: 气象学家；从事气象观测、研究或预报的专家
definition_en: a scientist who studies the atmosphere or who prepares weather observations and forecasts
core_image: 值班室里，一个人盯着雷达回波，手指沿着雨带边缘移动
scene: 值班室里，一个人盯着雷达回波，判断雨带是否会转向城区。 The meteorologist expected the rain band to reach the coast by evening.
sceneCN: 这里 meteorologist 指「从事气象工作的专家」（第 1 个义项：气象学家）；句意为这位气象学家预计雨带将在傍晚抵达海岸。图中可辨识物件：雷达回波、雨带、值班台、时钟。

pos.zh: 气象学家；气象工作者（可数名词；复数 meteorologists）

senses.title: A weather scientist
senses.definition: a scientist whose subject is the atmosphere and its weather
senses.definitionCN: 以大气及其天气为研究对象的科学家
senses.example: The meteorologist explained why the fog formed in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这位气象学家解释了雾为何在山谷里形成。
senses.why: the person suffix added to the discipline names whoever practises it.
senses.whyCN: 加在学科名上的人物后缀，指从事这门学科的人。

senses.title: An operational forecaster
senses.definition: one whose daily work is to issue forecasts and warnings on a shift
senses.definitionCN: 日常工作是在轮班中发布预报与警报的人
senses.example: The meteorologist on duty updated the coastal warning.
senses.exampleCN: 值班气象员更新了沿海警报。
senses.why: the shift produces forecasts, and the title follows the shift.
senses.whyCN: 轮班产出预报，头衔就跟着轮班走。

senses.title: A research meteorologist
senses.definition: one who studies atmospheric processes rather than issuing routine forecasts
senses.definitionCN: 研究大气过程、而非发布日常预报的研究者
senses.example: A research meteorologist modelled how hail grows.
senses.exampleCN: 一位研究型气象学家模拟了冰雹如何生长。
senses.why: the same craft also asks how processes work, not only what happens next.
senses.whyCN: 同一门手艺也追问过程如何运作，而不只问接下来会怎样。

senses.title: A broadcast meteorologist
senses.definition: one who presents forecasts on radio or television and explains them to the public
senses.definitionCN: 在广播或电视上呈现预报并向公众解释的人
senses.example: The broadcast meteorologist kept the map simple.
senses.exampleCN: 这位广播气象播报员把图讲得很简单。
senses.why: a forecast needs a voice, and broadcasting created a version of the role.
senses.whyCN: 预报需要一张嘴，广播就造出这个角色的一种版本。

senses.title: An aviation meteorologist
senses.definition: one who briefs pilots on winds, icing and visibility along a route
senses.definitionCN: 向飞行员简报航线上的风、结冰与能见度的人
senses.example: An aviation meteorologist warned of icing over the pass.
senses.exampleCN: 一位航空气象员警告山口上空有结冰。
senses.why: flying needs route-specific warnings, so a specialism formed.
senses.whyCN: 飞行需要航线专项警报，于是形成一个专长。

senses.title: A military meteorologist
senses.definition: one who supplies weather support to military operations
senses.definitionCN: 为军事行动提供气象保障的人
senses.example: The military meteorologist timed the exercise around the front.
senses.exampleCN: 这位军事气象员围绕锋面安排了演习时间。
senses.why: operations need weather support, and the military kept its own specialists.
senses.whyCN: 行动需要气象保障，军队便保留自己的专家。

senses.title: A climate-adjacent specialist
senses.titleCN: 与气候研究交叉的专家
senses.definition: one whose atmospheric work overlaps with climate science and long-range outlooks
senses.definitionCN: 大气工作与气候科学及长期展望交叉的研究者
senses.example: The meteorologist worked with climatologists on the seasonal outlook.
senses.exampleCN: 这位气象学家与气候学家合作做季节展望。
senses.why: weather and climate meet at the seasonal scale, so the roles overlap.
senses.whyCN: 天气与气候在季节尺度上相遇，两个角色便重叠。

senses.title: The older sense: a sky phenomenon scholar
senses.titleCN: 旧义：研究高空现象的人
senses.definition: historical: a person who studied things high in the air, including meteors
senses.definitionCN: 历史义：研究高空之物（包括流星）的人
senses.example: An early meteorologist catalogued comets and winds alike.
senses.exampleCN: 早期这类学者把彗星与风一并记录。
senses.why: before the science split, anyone who watched the sky bore the same title.
senses.whyCN: 在学科分开之前，任何观天的人都带同一头衔。

intro.en: Meteorologist joins meteorology with the Greek-derived person suffix -ist. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: meteorologist 由 meteorology 加希腊来源的人物后缀 -ist 构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Meteōron 'thing high up' was built on meta- 'up' and aeirein 'to lift'; its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: meteōron「高处之物」由 meta-「向上」与 aeirein「举起」构成；其更深来源不确定。

items.en: The suffix for a reasoned study comes from logos 'word, reason', through Latin -logia.
items.cn: 表示有理据研究的前缀出自 logos「言词、理性」，经拉丁 -logia 传入。

items.en: Greek -istēs named a person who does something; Latin -ista and French -iste carried it into English -ist.
items.cn: 希腊 -istēs 指从事某事的人；拉丁 -ista 与法语 -iste 把它带入英语 -ist。

items.en: The title appears in the nineteenth century, as weather services begin to employ trained staff.
items.cn: 这一职称在十九世纪出现，正值气象服务开始雇用受过训练的人员。

items.en: In the twentieth century the role divided into forecast desks, research groups, aviation briefings, broadcasting and military support.
items.cn: 二十世纪这个角色分成预报台、研究组、航空简报、广播与军事保障。

items.en: First English date approximate: no exact first use of meteorologist is recorded, and it is usually dated to the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 首见年代为约数：meteorologist 的确切首见英语书证未被记录，通常定在十九世纪。

note.en: Group one holds titles that look like meteorologist but belong elsewhere; group two holds real alternatives for the same profession.
note.cn: 第一组是外形像 meteorologist、实则属于其他领域的职称；第二组才是同一职业的真正替代说法。

entries.definition: A specialist in measurement, from Greek metron; not a weather scientist.
entries.definitionCN: 研究测量的专家，词根为希腊 metron；不是气象学家。

entries.definition: A specialist in meteorites, a branch of planetary science.
entries.definitionCN: 研究陨石的专家，属行星科学分支。

entries.definition: An older word for the same profession, now rare.
entries.definitionCN: 同一职业的较旧称呼，现已罕见。

entries.definition: The adjective, not the person; it describes data and stations.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，不指人；它描述数据与台站。

entries.definition: The everyday title for the operational side of the job; a meteorologist may also do research.
entries.definitionCN: 该职业业务一侧的日常称谓；气象学家也可能做研究。

entries.definition: An informal and older word, most often for a broadcast presenter.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的非正式说法，多指广播播报员。

entries.definition: A specialist in climates over decades, not in this week's weather.
entries.definitionCN: 研究数十年尺度气候的专家，而非本周天气。

entries.definition: A broader title covering atmospheric chemistry and physics as well as weather.
entries.definitionCN: 更宽泛的头衔，除天气外还涵盖大气化学与物理。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.

normal.en: Job titles take prefixes: broadcast, aviation, research, military, agricultural.

definition_zh: 人科动物；人科成员（现含大猿与人类，旧义仅指人类一支）
definition_en: a member of the family Hominidae, which now includes great apes and humans
core_image: 抽屉里一块骨盆与一根股骨拼在一起，标签上的分类层级写着「科」
scene: 化石柜的抽屉里，一块骨盆与一根股骨被拼在一起，标签只剩地层号。 The hominid pelvis in the drawer had been mislabelled for thirty years.
sceneCN: 这里「人科动物」指人科的一个化石个体（第 3 个义项：化石标本）；句意为抽屉里这块人科骨盆被错标了三十年。

pos.zh: 人科动物；人科成员（可数，复数 hominids）
人科的；人科动物特征的

derivatives.zh: 拉丁 homo（人）+ -idae（科级分类词尾）→ 人科（分类学上的科名）
拉丁 homo + -ini（族级词尾）→ 人族成员（语义偏移：层级从科降到族，范围收窄）
homo + -oid（形似）→ 人形总科的；类人猿（语义偏移：层级升到总科，范围放宽）
homo + -inae（亚科词尾）→ 人亚科的（语义偏移：指人亚科，含大猿与人类）
humanus（homo 的形容词）→ 人的；人
hominid + like（相似）→ 类似人科的（语义偏移：用于描述特征而非归类）

senses.title: A member of the family Hominidae
senses.titleCN: 现代分类：人科（含大猿与人类）的成员
senses.definition: any member of the family Hominidae in its modern sense, including great apes and humans
senses.definitionCN: 现代意义上的科级分类上的人科成员，包括大猿与人类
senses.example: The ape in the next case is, strictly speaking, also a hominid.
senses.exampleCN: 严格说来，隔壁展柜里的那只猿也是人科成员。
senses.why: The suffix -idae marks a zoological family, and the family now holds gorillas, chimpanzees, humans and their fossil relatives; the word therefore covers more than most readers expect.
senses.whyCN: -idae 是动物学上的科级词尾，而这个科如今包含大猩猩、黑猩猩、人类及其化石亲属；因此这个词覆盖的范围比多数读者预想的大。

senses.title: The human line only, in older usage
senses.titleCN: 旧义：仅指人类这一支及其近亲
senses.definition: in older literature, a member of the human family only, excluding the other great apes
senses.definitionCN: 旧文献中仅指人类这一支的成员，不含其他大猿
senses.example: Older papers use hominid where a modern author would write hominin.
senses.exampleCN: 旧论文用 hominid 的地方，现代作者会写 hominin。
senses.why: When Hominidae meant only humans and their extinct relatives, the word was narrower; taxonomy changed and the word did not, so both senses circulate in the literature.
senses.whyCN: 当 Hominidae 只指人类及其已灭绝亲属时，这个词更窄；分类变了而词没变，于是两种义在文献里同时流通。

senses.title: A fossil specimen
senses.titleCN: 化石标本：博物馆或论文里的一个个体
senses.definition: a particular fossil individual assigned to that family
senses.definitionCN: 被归入该科的某一具体化石个体
senses.example: The hominid pelvis in the drawer had been mislabelled for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 抽屉里这块人科骨盆被错标了三十年。
senses.why: Specimens are what fill drawers and catalogues, so the noun shifted from a class to a counted thing; a label on a bone says hominid in the same way it says femur.
senses.whyCN: 标本才是抽屉与目录里的实物，因此名词从一类变成可数的一件；骨头上写 hominid，与写 femur 是同一种用法。

senses.title: A descriptive adjective
senses.titleCN: 描述性形容词：具人科特征的
senses.definition: having the anatomical features associated with the family
senses.definitionCN: 具有该科解剖特征的
senses.example: The hominid jaw was deep and the teeth were large.
senses.exampleCN: 这块人科下颌很深，牙齿很大。
senses.why: English lets many taxonomic nouns double as adjectives; here the adjective means 'shaped like a member of this family', which is looser than the classification itself.
senses.whyCN: 英语里许多分类名词可兼作形容词；此处形容词意为「形状像该科成员」，比分类本身更宽松。

senses.title: Popular 'early human ancestor'
senses.titleCN: 通俗用法：早期人类祖先
senses.definition: in popular writing, any early ancestor of modern humans
senses.definitionCN: 通俗写作中现代人类的任何早期祖先
senses.example: The documentary called every fossil ape a hominid and every one of them our grandfather.
senses.exampleCN: 纪录片把每块化石猿都称作人科动物，把每一块都说成我们的祖父。
senses.why: Popular writing needs a short word for 'old human relative', and hominid was available; the loose sense then spread through museums and film.
senses.whyCN: 通俗写作需要一个短词来说「古老的人类亲戚」，hominid 正好可用；这个宽松义随后经博物馆与影片扩散。

senses.title: The taxonomic rank label
senses.titleCN: 分类层级标签：科这一级的名称
senses.definition: the family-level category itself, as used in classification
senses.definitionCN: 分类学中「科」这一级所用的名称
senses.example: The label on the case reads Hominidae, of which hominid is the everyday form.
senses.exampleCN: 展柜上的标签写着 Hominidae，hominid 是它的日常说法。
senses.why: The noun is a back-formation from the family name: -idae belongs to the taxon, -id to one member of it, a pattern repeated across zoology.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是从科名反向构成的：-idae 属于分类单元，-id 属于其中一个成员，这一模式在动物学中反复出现。

senses.title: A comparative-anatomy reference
senses.titleCN: 比较解剖学的参照：用来对照的骨架
senses.definition: a reference specimen in comparative anatomy, as in a hominid skeleton
senses.definitionCN: 比较解剖学中作对照的标本，如人科骨架
senses.example: Students compare a hominid skeleton with a chimpanzee's on the same bench.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们在同一张台子上把人科骨架与黑猩猩骨架对照。
senses.why: Anatomy teaches by comparison, and the word became a convenient label for one side of the comparison, independent of any claim about ancestry.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学靠比较来教，这个词于是成了比较中一侧的方便标签，与任何关于祖先的主张无关。

senses.title: An evolutionary grade
senses.titleCN: 演化等级：以「人科水平」描述形态阶段
senses.definition: a grade of organisation rather than a strictly defined family, as in hominid-grade
senses.definitionCN: 指形态组织的一种水平，而非严格界定的科，如 hominid-grade
senses.example: Some writers speak of hominid-grade posture without committing to a family.
senses.exampleCN: 有些作者说有「人科水平」的体态，却不对科属表态。
senses.why: Grade and clade are different ideas: a grade describes a level of adaptation, which lets hominid be used for a body plan rather than a branch.
senses.whyCN: 等级与支系是两回事：等级描述适应水平，于是 hominid 可用来指一套身体方案，而不是一个分支。

intro.en: Hominid is a nineteenth-century taxonomic formation from the Latin stem for 'person' plus a family ending; the family ending is clear, the stem's deeper origin is not.
intro.cn: hominid 是 19 世纪从拉丁「人」词干加科级词尾构成的分类学术语；词尾清楚，词干的更深来源则不然。

items.en: Homo, hominis meant 'human being'. Its deeper origin is disputed; a connection with humus 'earth' would give 'earthling', but that is a hypothesis and not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: homo, hominis 意为「人」。其更深来源有争议；与 humus「土地」联系可得出「地上之人」，但这只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Nineteenth-century zoologists formed family names on Latin stems with the ending -idae, and Hominidae was coined for the family containing humans.
items.cn: 19 世纪动物学者用拉丁词干加 -idae 构成科名，Hominidae 即为人所在的科所造。

items.en: English took the family name and made a singular noun hominid for one member, with the adjective following immediately.
items.cn: 英语取用科名，造出单数名词 hominid 指一个成员，形容词用法随即跟上。

items.en: From the late twentieth century comparative genetics placed gorillas and chimpanzees inside the same family, so Hominidae widened and hominid with it.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期比较遗传学把大猩猩与黑猩猩放进同一个科，Hominidae 因此变宽，hominid 也随之变宽。

items.en: Older textbooks and museum labels still use the pre-reclassification sense, so the word has two live readings that differ by a whole family.
items.cn: 旧教科书与博物馆标签仍用重新分类之前的义，因此这个词有两种并行的读法，相差整整一个科。

items.en: Source uncertain: the taxonomic date is approximate for the English noun, and the pre-Latin origin of homo is unknown, with all proposed forms reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语名词的确切分类年代只有约数；homo 在拉丁语之前的来源不明，所拟形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the taxonomic words one rank away from hominid, which are the usual source of error; group two holds the everyday relatives.
note.cn: 第一组是与 hominid 相差一个分类层级的词，也是错误的常见来源；第二组是日常说法中的亲属词。

entries.definition: A member of the tribe Hominini, the human line after the split from chimpanzees; narrower than hominid and now preferred for fossils on that line.
entries.definitionCN: 人族成员，指与黑猩猩分开之后的人类这一支；比 hominid 窄，今多用于该支的化石。

entries.definition: A member of the superfamily Hominoidea, which adds the great apes to the picture; broader than hominid.
entries.definitionCN: 人形总科成员，把大猿也算进来；比 hominid 宽。

entries.definition: A member of the subfamily Homininae, the African apes and humans together; a rank between family and tribe.
entries.definitionCN: 人亚科成员，即非洲猿与人类；层级在科与族之间。

entries.definition: A member of Homo sapiens only, with no fossil relatives included.
entries.definitionCN: 仅指智人这一物种，不含化石亲属。

entries.definition: A member of the order Primates, which contains hominids among many others.
entries.definitionCN: 灵长目成员，人科只是其中一支。

entries.definition: A gorilla, chimpanzee, orangutan or human, in plain language; the same set as modern Hominidae.
entries.definitionCN: 日常语言中的大猩猩、黑猩猩、猩猩或人；与现代 Hominidae 同一集合。

entries.definition: Any earlier population from which a later one descends; it makes no taxonomic claim.
entries.definitionCN: 后代所出自的任何较早群体；不作分类学断言。

entries.definition: An animal that walks on two legs; several hominids are bipeds, but the words are not equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 两足行走的动物；若干人科动物是两足，但两词并不等同。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real ranks and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实词尾、真实分类层级与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: -idae marks a family, -id marks one member of it; the same pattern runs through zoology.
normal.cn: -idae 标记科，-id 标记其中一个成员；动物学中同一模式反复出现。

normal.en: The family now includes the great apes, so a gorilla is a hominid even though it is not a human ancestor.
normal.cn: 这个科如今包含大猿，因此大猩猩是人科成员，尽管它不是人类祖先。

normal.en: The family runs Hominidae, hominid, hominin, hominoid, hominine, human.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 Hominidae、hominid、hominin、hominoid、hominine、human。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: early hominid, hominid fossils, hominid evolution.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：早期人科动物、人科化石、人科演化。

normal.en: Older texts use the narrow sense; modern texts use the wide sense; ask which family the author means.
normal.cn: 旧文用窄义，现代文用宽义；要问作者指的是哪个科。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer where a pelvis and a femur are introduced to each other after thirty years apart.
abstract.cn: 想象抽屉里一块骨盆与一根股骨，分离三十年后才被介绍相识。

abstract.en: Picture a family photograph in which the cousins keep being cropped out and then restored.
abstract.cn: 想象一张全家福，表亲们先被裁掉，后来又被放回。

abstract.en: Picture a label that is one rank too low for the bone it describes.
abstract.cn: 想象一张标签，比它所描述的骨头低了整整一级。

examples.en: The hominid fossil was reassigned to a different genus after the jaw was cleaned.
examples.cn: 下颌清理之后，这块人科化石被改归另一个属。

examples.en: Every hominid in the case shares a shoulder built for climbing.
examples.cn: 展柜里每一具人科骨架都有为攀爬而生的肩。

examples.en: The word hominid now covers the apes too, which surprises many visitors.
examples.cn: hominid 如今也涵盖猿类，这让许多参观者意外。

dict_mnemonic.text: homin（人）+ id（科成员）＝ 人科的成员；记「层级三件套：hominoid 总科、hominid 科、hominin 族」。

root: 新拉丁 Hominidae：拉丁 homo（homin-「人」）+ -idae（科级分类词尾）；homo 更深来源不确定，与 humus「土地」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one taxonomic word as its family grew: the modern wide family, the older narrow one, a counted fossil, a descriptive adjective, a popular ancestor, the rank label, an anatomical reference and an evolutionary grade.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着一个分类词随其科的范围扩大：现代宽义、旧日窄义、可数的化石、描述性形容词、通俗的祖先义、层级标签、解剖参照，以及演化等级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pelvis and a femur joined in a drawer under a label that names a rank, not a bone.
core.cn: 核心意象：抽屉里拼在一起的骨盆与股骨，标签写的是分类层级，而不是骨名。

branches.en: TWO WIDTHS OF ONE FAMILY: the modern reading that admits apes, and the older one that excluded them.
branches.cn: 同一个科的两种宽度：含猿的现代读法，与排除猿的旧读法。

branches.en: FROM CLASS TO OBJECT: a counted fossil in a drawer, and a skeleton used for comparison.
branches.cn: 从类到物：抽屉里可数的化石，与用作对照的骨架。

branches.en: DESCRIPTION AND STORY: the adjective for features, and the museum word for an ancestor.
branches.cn: 描述与故事：指特征的形容词，与博物馆里指祖先的词。

branches.en: THE RANK ITSELF: a family name turned back into a noun for its members.
branches.cn: 层级本身：科名反向构成指其成员的名词。

branches.en: THE LOOSER IDEA: a level of adaptation rather than a branch of the tree.
branches.cn: 更松的概念：一种适应水平，而非树上的一支。

intro.en: The word is a taxonomic suffix on a Latin stem, and the same stem with different rank endings produces the words most often confused with it.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁词干加分类学词尾，同一词干换不同层级词尾，就产生最易与它混淆的几个词。

latinIntro.en: Latin homo supplies the stem homin-; the endings -idae, -ini, -inae and -oidea mark family, tribe, subfamily and superfamily, and English adds -id for a single member.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 homo 提供词干 homin-；-idae、-ini、-inae、-oidea 分别标记科、族、亚科、总科，英语再加 -id 指单个成员。

items.example: The stem is shared by every rank name in the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干为这一族的各层级名称共用。

items.structure: New Latin family ending from Greek -idai
items.example: The ending marks the rank that contains genera.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾标记包含属的那一级。

items.example: The word names one member, not the family itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词指一个成员，而非科本身。

items.example: The same stem with a tribe ending gives hominin.
items.exampleCN: 同一词干换族级词尾即成 hominin。

items.example: The same stem with a subfamily ending gives hominine.
items.exampleCN: 同一词干换亚科词尾即成 hominine。

items.example: The same stem with a superfamily ending gives hominoid.
items.exampleCN: 同一词干换总科词尾即成 hominoid。

items.example: The family name is capitalized and italicized in zoology.
items.exampleCN: 科名在动物学中大写并用斜体。

items.example: The narrower word is now standard for the human line.
items.exampleCN: 较窄的这个词如今是人类这一支的标准称谓。

items.example: The wider word includes the apes.
items.exampleCN: 较宽的这个词包含猿类。

latinEntries.structure: Hominidae (New Latin, f. plural, family rank)
latinEntries.meaning: the family of humans and great apes

definition_zh: 火山作用；火山活动；火山现象；行星火山作用
definition_en: the set of processes by which magma, gases and other fluids rise from a planet's interior to its surface, and the phenomena that result
core_image: 地下的熔融物质沿裂隙上涌，在地表堆出锥丘、铺开岩流，同时把气体送入大气
scene: 裂谷边缘，勘察队刚布好仪器，地面正在缓慢抬升。 Along the rift, volcanism keeps building new crust even between eruptions.
sceneCN: 这里 volcanism 是「火山作用」（第 1 个义项：岩浆与气体由星球内部上升到地表的过程及其产物）；句意为裂谷一带的火山作用在两次喷发之间仍在不断生成新的地壳。

pos.zh: 火山作用；火山活动；火山现象的总称

forms.label: 形容词（火山的；火山作用的）

derivatives.zh: 火山的；火山作用的；火山似的
以火山方式；由火山作用
冰火山作用（喷出的是水、氨等挥发性物质）

senses.title: The process itself
senses.definition: the rise of magma and associated fluids from the interior to the surface, together with the phenomena it produces
senses.definitionCN: 岩浆及相关流体由内部上升到地表的过程，连同它所造成的现象
senses.example: Along the rift, volcanism keeps building new crust even between eruptions.
senses.exampleCN: 裂谷一带的火山作用在两次喷发之间仍在不断生成新的地壳。
senses.why: volcanism adds -ism to volcano, and that suffix turns a thing into a process, so the word names activity rather than a mountain.
senses.whyCN: volcanism 在 volcano 之后加 -ism，这个后缀把事物变成过程，因此此词指活动而非山体。

senses.title: The global pattern of activity
senses.titleCN: 全球火山作用的分布格局
senses.definition: the worldwide distribution of volcanic activity, concentrated at plate boundaries, rifts and hot spots
senses.definitionCN: 全球火山活动的分布，集中于板块边界、裂谷与热点
senses.example: Global volcanism clusters along the rim of the Pacific.
senses.exampleCN: 全球火山作用集中分布在太平洋边缘。
senses.why: once the process was mapped, the same noun could name a pattern on a world map rather than a single vent.
senses.whyCN: 当这个过程被绘制成图之后，同一个名词便能指世界地图上的格局，而不只是一个喷口。

senses.title: Volcanic activity on other worlds
senses.definition: volcanic activity on any solid body, driven by internal heat from tidal flexing, decay or residual accretion
senses.definitionCN: 任何固态天体上的火山活动，由潮汐揉搓、放射性衰变或残余吸积的内热驱动
senses.example: On Io, volcanism renews the surface faster than impacts can mark it.
senses.exampleCN: 在木卫一上，火山作用更新表面的速度快过撞击留下痕迹的速度。
senses.why: the process does not depend on Earth's particular tectonics, so planetary science kept the noun and changed only the setting.
senses.whyCN: 这一过程并不依赖地球特有的构造机制，因此行星科学保留了这个名词，只更换了场景。

senses.title: Effusive versus explosive style
senses.titleCN: 溢流式与爆炸式喷发方式
senses.definition: the manner in which material leaves a vent, from quiet lava flows to violent fragmentation and tall columns
senses.definitionCN: 物质离开喷口的方式，从安静的岩流到猛烈的碎化与高耸灰柱
senses.example: Effusive volcanism builds broad shields instead of steep cones.
senses.exampleCN: 溢流式火山作用堆出宽阔的盾状体，而不是陡峭的锥体。
senses.why: the noun covers the whole process, so a style adjective can pick out one mode of that process without changing the noun.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词涵盖整个过程，因此加一个方式形容词就能挑出其中一种模式，而名词本身不变。

senses.title: Ancient volcanism in the rock record
senses.titleCN: 岩石记录中的古老火山作用
senses.definition: volcanic activity of the geological past, read from lava flows, ash layers and intrusive bodies
senses.definitionCN: 地质历史时期的火山活动，从岩流、火山灰层与侵入体读出
senses.example: Ancient volcanism left thick basalt flows across the basin.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的火山作用在整个盆地留下厚厚的玄武岩流。
senses.why: a process can be ancient, so the same noun describes activity known only from its products, with no live vent left.
senses.whyCN: 过程可以是古老的，因此同一个名词能描述仅由产物得知、已无活动喷口的活动。

senses.title: Cryovolcanism
senses.definition: eruption of water, ammonia or other volatiles instead of molten rock, chiefly on icy bodies
senses.definitionCN: 喷出的是水、氨或其他挥发性物质而非熔岩，主要见于冰质天体
senses.example: Cryovolcanism on icy moons releases water through cracks in the shell.
senses.exampleCN: 冰质卫星上的冰火山作用通过冰壳裂缝释放水。
senses.why: the prefix cryo- marks the fluid as cold, while volcanism supplies the whole rising-and-erupting frame.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 cryo- 标明流体是冷的，而 volcanism 提供整套上涌并喷出的框架。

senses.title: Volcanism and climate
senses.definition: the effect of volcanic gases and particles on atmospheric temperature, chemistry and circulation
senses.definitionCN: 火山气体与颗粒对大气温度、化学成分与环流的影响
senses.example: Large-scale volcanism can cool the climate for several years.
senses.exampleCN: 大规模的火山作用能使气候变冷数年。
senses.why: because the word names a process with outputs, it easily takes a second noun naming what those outputs act upon.
senses.whyCN: 因为此词指带产物的过程，它很容易再接一个名词，说明这些产物作用于什么。

senses.title: The object of a science
senses.definition: the process as observed, measured and modelled by volcanologists
senses.definitionCN: 被火山学家观测、测量与建模的过程
senses.example: Researchers treat volcanism as a process to be measured, not merely described.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者把火山作用视为需要测量的过程，而不只是加以描述。
senses.why: a named process can become a research object, so the noun also serves as the subject matter of a discipline.
senses.whyCN: 被命名的过程可以成为研究对象，因此这个名词也充当一门学科的主题。

intro.en: Volcanism is an English coinage of the nineteenth century: volcano plus the suffix -ism, which reached English through French and Latin from Greek -ismos. It names the process rather than the mountain.
intro.cn: volcanism 是十九世纪英语新构的词：volcano 加后缀 -ism，而 -ism 经法语与拉丁语来自希腊语 -ismos。它指过程，而非山体。

items.en: Volcanus was the Roman god of fire and the forge, and his name passed to a smoking island north of Sicily.
items.cn: Volcanus 是罗马的火与锻造之神，他的名字传给了西西里以北一座冒烟的岛。

items.en: Italian vulcano gave English volcano, so the stem already meant a burning mountain before any suffix was added.
items.cn: 意大利语 vulcano 给了英语 volcano，因此在加任何后缀之前，这个词干已指燃烧的山。

items.en: -ismos was a Greek suffix forming nouns of action, practice or system; Latin -ismus and French -isme carried it into English.
items.cn: -ismos 是希腊语后缀，构成表示动作、实践或体系的名词；拉丁 -ismus 与法语 -isme 把它带入英语。

items.en: English formed volcanism to name the process as a subject of study, at a time when geology was separating into specialised fields.
items.cn: 英语构造出 volcanism，把这一过程作为研究对象命名，当时地质学正分化为若干专门领域。

items.en: Twentieth-century planetary science widened volcanism to any solid world and coined cryovolcanism for icy bodies.
items.cn: 二十世纪的行星科学把 volcanism 扩展到任何固态天体，并为冰质天体造出 cryovolcanism。

items.en: The older spelling vulcanism persists in some texts and carried alchemical overtones; the deeper origin of Volcanus is uncertain and possibly Etruscan.
items.cn: 较旧的拼法 vulcanism 仍见于部分文本，并带炼金术色彩；Volcanus 的更深来源不确定，可能与伊特鲁里亚语有关。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same volcano stem, including the old spelling; group two holds terms for the activity or its products.
note.cn: 第一组是由同一个 volcano 词干构成的形式，包括旧拼法；第二组是表示这种活动或其产物的词。

entries.definition: The mountain or vent structure itself; volcanism is what that structure does over time.
entries.definitionCN: 山体或喷口构造本身；volcanism 是这种构造在时间中的活动。

entries.definition: Of or produced by a volcano; it describes material or origin, while volcanism names the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 火山的或火山造成的；描述材料或来源，而 volcanism 指整个过程。

entries.definition: An older variant spelling of volcanism, also used in alchemical writing for the action of fire; not a separate process.
entries.definitionCN: volcanism 的较旧异体拼写，也用于炼金术文献指火的作用；并非另一种过程。

entries.definition: The science that studies volcanism and its products; the discipline is named after the process, not the reverse.
entries.definitionCN: 研究火山作用及其产物的学科；学科名由过程名而来，而非相反。

entries.definition: The generation and movement of magma anywhere in a planet, including bodies that never reach the surface; volcanism is its surface expression.
entries.definitionCN: 行星内部岩浆的生成与运移，包括从未到达地表的部分；volcanism 是它的地表表现。

entries.definition: A single act of material bursting out; volcanism is the long-running process that produces many such events.
entries.definitionCN: 物质冲出的一次动作；volcanism 是产生许多此类事件的长过程。

entries.definition: Activity involving molten rock and its solidification; it stresses the rock produced rather than the surface phenomena.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及熔融岩石及其固结的活动；强调生成的岩石，而非地表现象。

entries.definition: Surface evidence of internal heat such as hot springs and steam; it can occur with little or no magma involved.
entries.definitionCN: 内部热量的地表表现，如温泉与蒸汽；可以在很少或没有岩浆参与时发生。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: volcano plus -ism: the mountain name turned into the name of a process.
normal.cn: volcano 加 -ism：山名变成了过程名。

normal.en: The family runs volcanism, volcanic, volcanically, volcanology, volcanologist and cryovolcanism.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 volcanism、volcanic、volcanically、volcanology、volcanologist、cryovolcanism。

normal.en: Style pairs fix the meaning: effusive volcanism, explosive volcanism.
normal.cn: 方式搭配固定词义：溢流式火山作用、爆炸式火山作用。

normal.en: Planetary contexts extend it: global volcanism, planetary volcanism, subglacial volcanism.
normal.cn: 行星语境扩展它的用法：全球火山作用、行星火山作用、冰下火山作用。

normal.en: Spelling note: modern science writes volcanism, while vulcanism survives as an older and alchemy-tinged variant.
normal.cn: 拼写提示：现代科学写作 volcanism，而 vulcanism 作为较旧且带炼金术色彩的异体仍存。

abstract.en: Picture a kettle that never stops steaming, even when nobody is watching.
abstract.cn: 想象一只没人看守却始终冒汽的水壶。

abstract.en: Picture a slow conveyor laying new floor tiles from below, year after year.
abstract.cn: 想象一条缓慢的传送带，年复一年从下面铺出新地砖。

abstract.en: Picture a city whose subway map shows many lines rising from one deep source.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地铁图，许多线路从同一个深处源头升起。

examples.en: Volcanism built the island chain over millions of years.
examples.cn: 火山作用在数百万年间建起了这条岛链。

examples.en: Satellite images revealed active volcanism beneath the ice sheet.
examples.cn: 卫星图像显示冰盖之下存在活跃的火山作用。

examples.en: The course compares Earth's volcanism with the ice-driven kind on distant moons.
examples.cn: 这门课程把地球的火山作用与遥远卫星上由冰驱动的类型作比较。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「volcan（火山）＋ism（过程、体系）」——把山名变成持续发生的过程 → 火山作用

root: volcano（← 意大利语 vulcano ← 拉丁 Volcanus「火神」）+ 后缀 -ism（← 希腊 -ismos，经拉丁 -ismus）→ volcanism；词指过程，不指山体。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a process rather than an object: the process itself, its global pattern, its planetary reach, its eruption styles, its record in old rock, its icy variant, its effect on climate, and its status as a measured science.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着一个过程而非一个物件展开：过程本身、全球格局、行星范围、喷发方式、古老岩石中的记录、冰质变体、对气候的影响，最后成为被测量的学科对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: melt rising through a crack, piling a cone and feeding the air above.
core.cn: 核心意象：熔融物沿裂缝上涌，堆起锥丘，并向上方大气供料。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: activity, not a thing, which is what -ism contributes.
branches.cn: 过程本身：是活动而非物件，这正是 -ism 带来的意义。

branches.en: WHERE IT HAPPENS: a pattern on a world map, then a process on any solid body.
branches.cn: 发生之处：先是世界地图上的格局，随后是任何固态天体上的过程。

branches.en: HOW IT HAPPENS: quiet flows and violent columns are two modes of one process.
branches.cn: 发生方式：安静的岩流与猛烈的灰柱是同一过程的两种模式。

branches.en: DEEP TIME AND COLD FLUIDS: the same frame survives in old rock and in icy eruptions.
branches.cn: 深时与冷流体：同一框架在古老岩石与冰质喷发中都成立。

branches.en: EFFECT AND STUDY: outputs change the climate, and the process becomes a measured object.
branches.cn: 影响与研究：产物改变气候，过程本身成为被测量的对象。

intro.en: Volcanism joins a borrowed proper-name stem to a productive suffix, which is why the word names a process despite its foreign root.
intro.cn: volcanism 把一个借入的专名词干接到一个能产后缀上，因此尽管词根来自外语，这个词却指一种过程。

latinIntro.en: Latin Volcanus supplies the stem, and Latin -ismus, from Greek -ismos, supplies the process suffix seen in volcanism.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 Volcanus 提供词干，来自希腊 -ismos 的拉丁 -ismus 提供 volcanism 中所见的过程后缀。

items.structure: Volcanus (Latin name of the fire god)

items.example: The stem volcan- is the name of the fire god.
items.exampleCN: 词干 volcan- 就是那位火神的名字。

items.exampleCN: 意大利语词尾 -o 在借入的 volcano 中保留下来。

items.example: The suffix -ism turns a thing into a practice or process.

items.example: Volcanism is the process, not the mountain.

items.meaning: of or produced by a volcano
items.example: The volcanic layer marks a pause in deposition.
items.exampleCN: 火山层标志着沉积的一次停顿。

items.example: The region is volcanically active along its axis.
items.exampleCN: 该区域沿轴部火山活动活跃。

items.meaning: the scientific study of volcanic processes
items.example: Volcanology draws on geophysics and petrology.
items.exampleCN: 火山学借助地球物理学与岩石学。

items.example: A volcanologist watched the tilt meter all night.
items.exampleCN: 一位火山学家整夜盯着倾斜仪。

items.meaning: eruption of cold volatiles such as water or ammonia
items.meaningCN: 喷出冰冷挥发物（如水或氨）的火山作用
items.example: Cryovolcanism builds domes of frozen water on icy moons.
items.exampleCN: 冰火山作用在冰质卫星上堆出冻结的水丘。

items.example: Older texts write vulcanism where modern science writes volcanism.
items.exampleCN: 较早的文本写作 vulcanism，现代科学写作 volcanism。

definition_en: a broad bend in a coastline, or a loop or slack bend in a rope
core_image: 海岸线弯出一臂宽的怀抱；绳上松松的一圈弯
scene: 船帆的绳子松出一弯，水手顺手把它收紧。 The storm drove the boat into the wide bight of the coast.
sceneCN: 这里 bight 是「海湾」（第 1 个义项：海岸的大弧弯）；句意是风暴把小船吹进了海岸的大湾。

（绳索的）绳圈；绳弯

senses.title: A broad coastal curve
senses.definition: a long, gentle bend or curve in a coastline forming a bay
senses.definitionCN: 海岸线形成的宽缓弧弯，构成海湾
senses.example: The storm drove the boat into the wide bight of the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴把小船吹进了海岸的大湾。
senses.why: Old English byht meant a bend, of coasts as of anything else.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 byht 意为「弯曲」，先用于海岸等处。

senses.title: A loop of rope
senses.definition: the middle slack part of a rope bent into a U shape
senses.definitionCN: 绳子弯成 U 形时中部松弛的部分
senses.example: Pass the end through the bight and pull.
senses.exampleCN: 把绳端穿过绳圈后拉紧。
senses.why: A rope bends as a coast does; the bend names the loop.
senses.whyCN: 绳如海岸般弯曲，「弯」即得名绳圈。

senses.title: A curve or turn of any line
senses.definition: any bend or curve, as of a road, river, or line
senses.definitionCN: 道路、河流或线条的任何弯曲
senses.example: The road follows every bight of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 公路顺着河流的每一道弯。
senses.why: The bend idea generalizes beyond coasts.
senses.whyCN: 「弯曲」之义由海岸推广到一切线条。

senses.title: The bight in knot-tying
senses.definition: the U-shaped part used in making knots and hitches
senses.definitionCN: 打结、系索时所用的 U 形部分
senses.example: Tie the hitch on the bight for quick release.
senses.exampleCN: 把系结打在绳弯上以便快速解开。
senses.why: Riggers name the loop precisely because knots depend on it.
senses.whyCN: 索具工特意为绳圈命名，因为打结全赖它。

senses.title: A shallow bay as shelter
senses.definition: a bay shallow or curved enough to offer anchorage
senses.definitionCN: 水浅或弯度足以为船只提供泊地之湾
senses.example: The fleet sheltered in a grassy bight overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 船队夜宿于长满青草的小湾。
senses.why: A bend in the shore naturally shelters boats.
senses.whyCN: 岸的弯折天然庇护船只。

senses.title: A recess in geography
senses.definition: any concave bend or recess in land forms
senses.definitionCN: 陆地形态上的凹陷弯折
senses.example: The map marked a forested bight in the cliff line.
senses.exampleCN: 地图标出崖线上一处林木葱茏的凹弯。
senses.why: Coastline vocabulary migrates inland with maps.
senses.whyCN: 海岸词汇随地图向内陆迁移。

senses.title: The bight of a sail or tackle
senses.definition: the loop formed in a sail's sheet or tackle under load
senses.definitionCN: 帆的缭绳或索具受拉时形成的弯环
senses.example: Keep clear of the bight while the sail is loading.
senses.exampleCN: 帆受风拉紧时切勿靠近绳弯。
senses.why: Working ropes on ships keep the loop sense alive.
senses.whyCN: 船上作业的绳索让绳圈义沿用至今。

senses.title: Named coastal bights
senses.definition: a proper name element for great coastal indentations
senses.definitionCN: 用作大型海岸凹入的专名成分
senses.example: The Great Australian Bight stretches for hundreds of miles.
senses.exampleCN: 澳大利亚大湾绵延数百英里。
senses.why: Great bends on maps took the old word as a title.
senses.whyCN: 地图上的大弯以古词为名。

definition_zh: 现代性；现代的状态；现代社会与文化的处境；现代时期；现代风格
definition_en: the condition, experience or period of being modern
core_image: 深夜的地铁站里广告屏亮着，乘客各自盯着手机，谁也不看谁
scene: 深夜的地铁站里广告屏亮着，乘客各自盯着手机，谁也不看谁， The novel captures the loneliness of modernity in a crowded city.
sceneCN: 这里 modernity 指「现代都市生活的体验与处境」（第 4 个义项：现代生活的文化体验）；句意为这部小说捕捉了拥挤城市中现代性的孤独。图中可辨识物件：广告屏、手机、站台长椅、互不相视的乘客。

pos.zh: 现代性；现代的状态、处境或时期

derivatives.zh: 现代主义者；现代主义的

senses.title: The condition of being modern
senses.definition: the state or quality of belonging to the modern age
senses.definitionCN: 属于现代时代的处境或性质
senses.example: Modernity is not a date but a condition that keeps changing.
senses.exampleCN: 现代性不是一个日期，而是一种不断变化的处境。
senses.why: The suffix names a quality of a thing, so modernity is modern-ness itself, abstracted from any particular object.
senses.whyCN: 后缀命名事物的性质，因此现代性就是「现代」本身，从任何具体物件中抽象出来。

senses.title: A historical period
senses.definition: the era after the medieval period, or the period of modern societies, depending on the field
senses.definitionCN: 中世纪之后的时代，或现代社会所处的时期，视学科而定
senses.example: Historians place the start of modernity at different centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家把现代性的起点放在不同的世纪。
senses.why: A quality can be turned into a period: if societies are modern, there must be a time when modernity begins.
senses.whyCN: 性质可以变成一个时期：如果社会是现代的了，就必然有一个现代性开始的时刻。

senses.title: The sociological condition
senses.definition: the social condition marked by rationalization, secularization, industry and impersonal institutions
senses.definitionCN: 以理性化、世俗化、工业与非人格化制度为特征的社会处境
senses.example: Modernity promised that reason would make institutions predictable.
senses.exampleCN: 现代性曾许诺，理性能让制度变得可预测。
senses.why: Sociology made the abstract quality into a system: modernity is a way of organizing work, belief and time.
senses.whyCN: 社会学把这个抽象性质变成一个系统：现代性是组织工作、信仰与时间的一套方式。

senses.title: The experience of modern life
senses.definition: the lived texture of modern life, often described as speed, anonymity and loneliness
senses.definitionCN: 现代生活的实际质感，常被描述为速度、匿名与孤独
senses.example: The novel captures the loneliness of modernity in a crowded city.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说捕捉了拥挤城市中现代性的孤独。
senses.why: The same condition can be felt rather than measured: crowds, screens and speed produce a new inner weather.
senses.whyCN: 同一种处境可以被感受，而不只是被测量：人群、屏幕与速度造出一种新的内心气候。

senses.title: The quality of modern art
senses.definition: the stylistic quality of art that belongs to the modern movement or period
senses.definitionCN: 属于现代运动或时期的艺术风格特质
senses.example: Critics praised the modernity of the score, not its difficulty.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称赞这部配乐的现代性，而不是它的难度。
senses.why: A work can have modernity as a property, which is how the abstract noun becomes an art-critical judgement.
senses.whyCN: 一件作品可以把现代性作为一种属性，抽象名词由此变成艺术评论的判断。

senses.title: Political modernity
senses.definition: the political condition of constitutional government, citizenship and public law
senses.definitionCN: 宪政、公民身份与公法所构成的政治处境
senses.example: Political modernity made the citizen a bearer of rights rather than a subject.
senses.exampleCN: 政治现代性使公民成为权利持有者，而不再是臣民。
senses.why: Modernity has separate faces, and politics is one: the state is reorganized around law and citizenship.
senses.whyCN: 现代性有各自的面孔，政治是其中之一：国家围绕法律与公民身份被重新组织。

senses.title: Economic modernity
senses.definition: the economic condition of industrial capitalism, mass production and wage labour
senses.definitionCN: 工业资本主义、大规模生产与雇佣劳动所构成的经济处境
senses.example: Economic modernity arrived with the factory clock.
senses.exampleCN: 经济现代性随工厂的时钟一同到来。
senses.why: The same condition can be counted in output and hours, which is how the noun enters economic history.
senses.whyCN: 同一种处境可以用产量与工时来计数，这个名词由此进入经济史。

senses.title: Being up to date in everyday life
senses.titleCN: 日常生活中「跟得上时代」
senses.definition: the ordinary quality of being current, fashionable or technologically up to date
senses.definitionCN: 在当下、时髦或技术上跟得上时代的普通性质
senses.example: The shop's modernity is a card reader and a very old chair.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店的现代性是一台读卡器和一把很旧的椅子。
senses.why: The grand noun has a small everyday version: anyone can have a little modernity, measured in gadgets and habits.
senses.whyCN: 宏大的名词有一个小小的日常版本：任何人都可以拥有一点现代性，用器物与习惯来衡量。

intro.en: Modernity is modern plus the Latin noun ending -ity, which came from -itas. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: modernity 是 modern 加拉丁语名词词尾 -ity 构成，后者来自 -itas。年代均为约数。

items.en: Modo meant just now; it is usually derived from modus, measure or manner, though that link is a standard account rather than a certainty.
items.cn: modo 意为「刚刚」；通行说法认为它来自 modus「尺度、方式」，但这一联系只是标准解释，并非确证。

items.en: Late Latin modernus, of the present time, was built from the time word plus -nus; English modern came through French.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 modernus 意为「当下的」，由这个时间词加 -nus 构成；英语 modern 经法语进入。

items.en: The noun ending -itas named a state or quality, as in civitas from civis. English -ity continues it.
items.cn: 名词词尾 -itas 命名状态或性质，如 civitas 来自 civis。英语的 -ity 延续了它。

items.en: French modernité appeared in the nineteenth century, and English modernity followed in the same period.
items.cn: 法语 modernité 在十九世纪出现，英语 modernity 也在同一时期跟进。

items.en: Sociologists made modernity a technical term for the condition of industrial, rationalized societies, distinct from modernization as a process.
items.cn: 社会学家把 modernity 变成指工业、理性化社会处境的技术术语，并与作为过程的 modernization 区分开。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use of modernity is dated differently, and the pre-Latin origin of modo and modus remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定：modernity 在英语中的最早使用各家记载不一；modo 与 modus 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: The first group holds members of the same modern- family that are often swapped; the second holds terms for the modern age or its mood.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 modern- 词族、常被误换的词；第二组是关于现代时代或其情绪的词。

entries.definition: The artistic movement that broke with inherited forms; modernity is the condition that the movement responded to.
entries.definitionCN: 打破继承形式的艺术运动；modernity 是该运动所回应的处境。

entries.definition: The process of becoming modern; modernity is the state reached, or the experience of living in it.
entries.definitionCN: 走向现代的过程；modernity 是抵达的状态，或身处其中的体验。

entries.definition: Belonging to the present age; the adjective qualifies a thing, while modernity names the condition itself.
entries.definitionCN: 属于当下时代的；形容词修饰事物，而 modernity 命名处境本身。

entries.definition: A way or manner of doing something; it shares a distant Latin root with modern but means a method, not an era.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的方式；它与 modern 共享遥远的拉丁词根，但指方法，不指时代。

entries.definition: The quality of existing at the same time; it stresses the shared present, while modernity stresses a historical condition.
entries.definitionCN: 同时存在的性质；它强调共处的当下，而 modernity 强调历史处境。

entries.definition: The eighteenth century movement that trusted reason and progress; it is one source of modernity, not modernity itself.
entries.definitionCN: 十八世纪信任理性与进步的运动；它是现代性的一个来源，而非现代性本身。

entries.definition: Advance toward a better condition; modernity may believe in progress, but the noun does not itself mean improvement.
entries.definitionCN: 朝更好处境的推进；现代性可能相信进步，但这个名词本身不表示改善。

entries.definition: The growth of cities; it is a major producer of modern experience, not a synonym for modernity.
entries.definitionCN: 城市的增长；它是现代体验的主要制造者，而不是现代性的同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real quality ending, the real modern stem and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示性质的真实词尾、真实的 modern 词干，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: modern plus the quality ending -ity: the same ending builds reality and activity, so modernity is the state of being modern.
normal.cn: modern 加表示性质的名词词尾 -ity：同一词尾也构成 reality（真实）与 activity（活动），所以 modernity 就是「现代的状态」。

normal.en: The family runs modern, modernity, modernization, modernism, modernist and modernize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 modern（现代的）、modernity（现代性）、modernization（现代化）、modernism（现代主义）、modernist（现代主义者）、modernize（使现代化）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: late modernity, early modernity, urban modernity, political modernity.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：晚期现代性、早期现代性、城市现代性、政治现代性。

normal.en: The word is a condition, not a process: modernization is the road, modernity is where you stand.
normal.cn: 这个词是处境，不是过程：modernization 是路，modernity 是你站立的地方。

normal.en: Its art-world cousin is modernism, which is a movement rather than a condition.
normal.cn: 它在艺术界的亲戚是 modernism（现代主义），后者是运动，而不是处境。

abstract.en: Picture a crowded platform where every face is lit from below by a screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一个拥挤的站台，每张脸都被屏幕从下方照亮。

abstract.en: Picture a clock tower replaced by a timetable that never sleeps.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟楼被一张从不休息的时刻表取代。

abstract.en: Picture a room with the newest reader and the oldest chair.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，有最新的读卡器和最旧的椅子。

examples.en: Modernity is uneven: the same city can be early modern and late modern in one street.
examples.cn: 现代性并不均衡：同一座城市可以在一条街上同时是早期现代与晚期现代。

examples.en: The painter's modernity lies in what she leaves out.
examples.cn: 这位画家的现代性在于她省略了什么。

examples.en: Critics of modernity ask whether rational order has made life colder.
examples.cn: 现代性的批评者追问：理性秩序是否让生活更冷了？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩登」加「性」——一个时代整体的摩登状态与体验，就是现代性。

root: 由 modern 加表示性质的名词词尾 -ity 构成，-ity 来自拉丁语 -itas。modern 来自晚期拉丁语 modernus「当下的」，通行说法追溯至 modo「刚刚」，modo 又常被解释为来自 modus「尺度、方式」。modo 与 modus 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one condition: a quality, a period, a social system, a felt experience, an artistic property, a politics, an economy and a small everyday version.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种处境展开：一种性质、一个时期、一套社会系统、一种切身感受、一种艺术属性、一种政治、一种经济，最后是一个小小的日常版本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowded platform lit by screens, where everyone is modern and alone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个被屏幕照亮的拥挤站台，人人都是现代的，也人人孤独。

branches.en: QUALITY AND HABIT: modernity can be a grand condition or a card reader in a small shop.
branches.cn: 性质与习惯：现代性可以是宏大的处境，也可以是一家小店里的读卡器。

branches.en: PERIOD: a quality becomes a dateable era with a beginning and an end.
branches.cn: 时期：一种性质变成有起点与终点的可断代时代。

branches.en: SYSTEM: rationalization, secularization and industry organize life impersonally.
branches.cn: 系统：理性化、世俗化与工业以非人格的方式组织生活。

branches.en: EXPERIENCE: the system is felt as speed, anonymity and loneliness.
branches.cn: 体验：这套系统被感受为速度、匿名与孤独。

branches.en: FACES: art, politics and economy each show a distinct face of the same condition.
branches.cn: 面孔：艺术、政治与经济各自显出同一处境的不同面孔。

intro.en: Modernity is a time adjective plus the Latin quality ending, and the same stem builds the process and the movement words.
intro.cn: modernity 是一个时间形容词加拉丁语性质词尾，同一词干又造出过程词与运动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin modernus supplies modern, and -itas supplies the noun of quality that became English -ity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 modernus 提供 modern，-itas 提供后来成为英语 -ity 的性质名词词尾。

items.example: The adverb is usually linked to modus, measure.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词通常被联系到 modus「尺度」。

items.example: The adjective entered English through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词经法语进入英语。

items.example: The ending builds reality and activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 reality（真实）与 activity（活动）。

items.example: Urban modernity shaped the novel.
items.exampleCN: 城市现代性塑造了这部小说。

items.example: Modernization preceded modernity in some regions.
items.exampleCN: 在一些地区，现代化先于现代性。

items.meaning: the cultural movement of the new
items.example: Modernism is a movement, not a condition.
items.exampleCN: 现代主义是运动，不是处境。

items.example: The town modernized its port.
items.exampleCN: 这座镇使港口现代化了。

items.example: The modernist preferred the new city.
items.exampleCN: 这位现代主义者更喜欢新城市。

items.example: The station has a modernistic canopy.
items.exampleCN: 车站有一片现代主义风格的顶棚。

derivatives.meaning: the cultural movement of the new

definition_zh: n. 一炉；一批（一次做出或处理的量）；一组（同时处理的人或物）　v. 分批处理
definition_en: a quantity of something produced or dealt with at one time; a group handled together; to divide work into batches
core_image: 凌晨三点整盘推进炉膛的那一炉面包
scene: 面包房凌晨三点开了第一炉，热气把玻璃糊白了。 The bakery opened its first batch at three in the morning, and the steam clouded the glass.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：batch 指一次烘烤做出的整批量；句意是面包房凌晨三点开出第一炉。

pos.zh: 一批；一炉；一组
分批处理

derivatives.zh: 一批；一组（拍卖或交易用语）

senses.title: One oven load
senses.definition: the whole quantity of bread or other goods produced in a single operation
senses.definitionCN: 一次操作中做出的全部面包或其他产品
senses.example: The second batch came out darker than the first.
senses.exampleCN: 第二炉比第一炉颜色更深。
senses.why: The word is a noun built on bake, so its first meaning is exactly what one heating produces.
senses.whyCN: 该词是建在 bake「烘烤」上的名词，因此初义正是「一次加热所出」。

senses.title: A group handled together
senses.definition: a set of people or things dealt with at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 同时处理的一组人或一批物
senses.example: A new batch of applicants arrived on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 周一又来了一批申请人。
senses.why: The oven is dropped and only the togetherness remains, which lets the word cover people and data.
senses.whyCN: 烤炉被抽掉，只剩「一起」这一层，于是该词也能指人和数据。

senses.title: To group into batches
senses.definition: to arrange work or data so that it is processed in groups rather than one by one
senses.definitionCN: 把作业或数据安排成组处理，而非逐件处理
senses.example: The system batches the invoices overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 系统在夜间把发票分批处理。
senses.why: Computing turned the noun back into a verb, because queued group processing is exactly the oven pattern.
senses.whyCN: 计算机把这个名词又转回动词，因为排队成组处理正是烤炉那一套模式。

intro.en: Batch is a noun grown out of bake: one heating of the oven, then any set made or handled together, then a computing term.
intro.cn: batch 是从 bake「烘烤」长出的名词：先是炉中一次加热，再是任何一起制作或处理的集合，最后成为计算机术语。

items.en: The root bhe meant to warm or heat, the deep source of bake.
items.cn: 词根 bhe 意为使暖、加热，是 bake 的深层来源。

items.en: Old English bacan meant to bake, and its noun side gave a word for a baking.
items.cn: 古英语 bacan 意为烘烤，其名词一侧给出「一次烘烤」之词。

items.en: Middle English bache names the whole quantity of bread baked in one heating.
items.cn: 中古英语 bache 指一次加热中烤出的全部面包。

items.en: The spelling settles as batch, still tied to the oven.
items.cn: 拼写定为 batch，仍与烤炉相连。

items.en: The word widens from bread to any set of things made or handled together.
items.cn: 词义由面包扩为任何一起制作或处理的集合。

items.en: Batch processing names work queued and run without a person at each step.
items.cn: 批处理指排队执行、无需逐步人工干预的作业。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the -atch shape so the spelling sticks; the near-meaning group covers trade, shipping and statistics words for a group.
note.cn: 形近组保留 -atch 字形以固化拼写；近义组覆盖贸易、航运与统计中表示「一组」的词。

entries.definition: To seize something in motion.
entries.definitionCN: 抓住运动中的东西。

entries.tag: to break out of a shell
entries.definition: To emerge from an egg, or a small opening.
entries.definitionCN: 孵出；小舱口。

entries.definition: A thing that pairs with another, or a fire stick.
entries.definitionCN: 相配之物；火柴。

entries.definition: A wash of the whole body.
entries.definitionCN: 洗澡；浴缸。

entries.definition: A set of items sold or offered together.
entries.definitionCN: 一起出售或提供的一组物品。

entries.definition: A quantity of goods sent at one time.
entries.definitionCN: 一次发出的一批货物。

entries.definition: A group sharing a period or a trait.
entries.definitionCN: 共享同一时期或特征的一群人。

entries.definition: One portion of a larger sum or issue.
entries.definitionCN: 较大总额或发行量中的一份。

normalIntro.en: Batch is bake with a different tail: what comes out of the oven in one go is a batch.
normalIntro.cn: batch 就是 bake 换了个尾巴：一次从炉里出来的东西就是一 batch。

normal.en: Bake is the action; batch is the result.
normal.cn: bake 是动作，batch 是结果。

normal.en: One tray in, one tray out: that is a batch.
normal.cn: 一盘进、一盘出，那就是一 batch。

normal.en: Batches is the plural, with -es after ch.
normal.cn: 复数是 batches，ch 后加 -es。

normal.en: In batches means not all at once.
normal.cn: in batches 意为不一次全做。

normal.en: Batch processing runs a queue while you sleep.
normal.cn: batch processing 在你睡觉时跑完队列。

abstract.en: Time cut into equal loaves.
abstract.cn: 被切成等大 loaf 的时间。

abstract.en: A group defined only by when it was made.
abstract.cn: 一个仅由「何时被做出」定义的集合。

abstract.en: Patience built into a machine.
abstract.cn: 被造进机器里的耐心。

examples.en: She baked two batches before the shop opened.
examples.cn: 开店前她烤了两炉。

examples.en: The letters were printed in batches of fifty.
examples.cn: 信件按每批五十封打印。

examples.en: We batched the orders to save on delivery.
examples.cn: 我们把订单分批处理以节省运费。

dict_mnemonic.text: 换尾记忆：bake「烤」把 ke 换成 tch 就是 batch「一炉、一批」。一条线记住：一炉面包 → 一批货 → 一批人 → 分批处理。复数 batches。

root: 与 bake 同族，上溯原始印欧语词根 bhe「加热」；古英语 bacan「烘烤」的名词一侧产生 bæcce，中古英语约 1400 年作 bache「一次烤出的量」，16 世纪定为 batch。18 世纪扩指任何一起处理的集合，1950 年代进入计算机成为 batch processing。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses, one container of time: what one oven produces, what one moment gathers, and what a machine queues.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项，一个装时间的容器：一炉所出、一刻所聚、一机所排。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a full tray pushed into the oven at three in the morning
core.cn: 核心意象：凌晨三点整盘推进炉膛

branches.en: Steam clouding the bakery glass.
branches.cn: 热气糊白了面包房玻璃。

branches.en: A second tray, slightly darker.
branches.cn: 第二盘颜色略深。

branches.en: Fifty names on one list.
branches.cn: 一张名单上的五十个名字。

branches.en: A queue running before dawn.
branches.cn: 天亮前跑完的一列作业。

branches.en: One operation, many items.
branches.cn: 一次操作，多件东西。

intro.en: Batch shares its root with bake; the plural needs -es after ch, and the trade synonyms bring in Latin prefixes.
intro.cn: batch 与 bake 同根；ch 之后的复数要用 -es，而贸易类近义词带来拉丁语前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer sits in the near-synonyms: cohors for a company, processus for a going forward, signare for marking.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次藏在近义词里：cohors 表「一队人」，processus 表「向前行进」，signare 表「标记」。
