definition_zh: 女修道院院长；尼姑庵住持
definition_en: a woman who is the head of a convent of nuns
core_image: 高墙修道院里，一位手持权杖、走在修女最前面的女性长者
scene: 晨钟响起，修女们在长廊列队等候。 The abbess led the silent procession into the chapel.
sceneCN: 这里 abbess 是「女修道院院长」（第 1 个义项：女修道团体的首领）；句意为女院长领着安静的队列走进礼拜堂。

pos.zh: 女修道院院长（女修道团体的首领）
（泛称）隐修女团的领导者

derivatives.zh: 同族男性形式，义为「男修道院院长」
同根名词，义为「修道院；大寺院」
由 abbot 加形容词后缀构成，义为「修道院长的」

senses.title: Head of a convent of nuns
senses.definition: the woman elected to govern a community of nuns and answer for its discipline and property
senses.definitionCN: 被推选管理修女团体、对其纪律与财产负责的女性
senses.example: The abbess signed the deed that granted the village its well.
senses.exampleCN: 女院长在授予该村水井的契据上签了字。
senses.why: A Syrian word for spiritual father crossed into Latin; adding the feminine ending turns the father into the mother of the house.
senses.whyCN: 一个叙利亚语的「属灵之父」传入拉丁语；加上阴性词尾，家父便成了女修道院的母亲。

senses.title: Female superior in religious life generally
senses.titleCN: 隐修女团的领导者（泛称）
senses.definition: any woman who holds the corresponding office of spiritual leadership over a female monastic community
senses.definitionCN: 泛指在女性隐修团体中担任相应属灵领袖职分的女性
senses.example: In old chronicles every abbess is listed with the year she took office.
senses.exampleCN: 在古老编年史中，每位女院长都记有就任年份。
senses.why: The office outlives any single building; wherever nuns gather under a rule, the word names the one who keeps it.
senses.whyCN: 这一职分超越了任何一座建筑；凡有修女依会规聚集之处，这个词就指维持会规的那个人。

intro.en: Abbess is the Latin feminine of abbot, a title that travelled from Syria through Greek and Latin into English.
intro.cn: abbess 是 abbot 的拉丁阴性形式，这一头衔经叙利亚语、希腊语和拉丁语传入英语。

items.en: Abba meant father, the address given to respected spiritual teachers.
items.cn: 叙利亚语 abba 意为父亲，是对受尊敬的属灵导师的称呼。

items.en: Abbas passed into Greek as a title for monastic elders.
items.cn: 希腊语 abbas 作为修道长者的称号传入。

items.en: Abbas became the formal title of the head of a monastery.
items.cn: 拉丁语 abbas 成为修道院院长的正式称号。

items.en: Abbesse was formed with a feminine ending and entered English as abbess.
items.cn: 古法语加阴性词尾构成 abbesse，进入英语成为 abbess。

items.en: The word names the head of a convent of nuns.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词指女修道院院长。

note.en: The word sits inside a small family: abbot, abbey, and its own feminine ending.
note.cn: 该词属于一个小词族：abbot、abbey 及其阴性词尾。

entries.definition: the male head of a monastery
entries.definitionCN: 男修道院院长；abbess 的男性对应形式

entries.definition: the building or community itself
entries.definitionCN: 修道院建筑或团体；同出 abba 词根

entries.definition: relating to an abbot or abbess
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「修道院长的」

entries.definition: the head of a priory of nuns
entries.definitionCN: 小修道院（priory）的女院长；层级略低

entries.definition: the head of some religious orders of women
entries.definitionCN: 某些女修会的负责人称谓

entries.definition: a general title for head of a religious house
entries.definitionCN: 修会负责人的通称

normalIntro.en: The abb- family offers five quick anchors.
normalIntro.cn: abb- 词族提供五个快速记忆抓手。

normal.en: abbess = abbot + ess, the female form.
normal.cn: abbess ＝ abbot ＋ ess，阴性形式。

normal.en: -ess marks women: actress, princess, abbess.
normal.cn: -ess 标记女性：actress、princess、abbess。

normal.en: abbey is the building; abbot or abbess leads it.
normal.cn: abbey 是建筑；abbot 或 abbess 是其首领。

normal.en: Double b remembers the Syrian abba, father.
normal.cn: 双写 b 提示叙利亚语 abba「父亲」。

normal.en: Pair it with abbot to fix the gender ending.
normal.cn: 与 abbot 配对记忆阴性词尾。

abstract.en: See a ring of keys at a black-robed waist.
abstract.cn: 想象黑袍腰间的一串钥匙。

abstract.en: Hear one bell that the whole convent obeys.
abstract.cn: 听一声全院遵从的钟。

abstract.en: Picture a seat slightly higher in the chapel.
abstract.cn: 想象礼拜堂里略高一级的座位。

examples.en: The abbess welcomed two new novices last spring.
examples.cn: 去年春天女院长接纳了两名新见习修女。

examples.en: Visitors were received in the hall beneath the abbess's window.
examples.cn: 访客在女院长窗下的厅堂受到接待。

examples.en: An abbess of great learning governed the convent for forty years.
examples.cn: 一位极有学问的女院长执掌这座修道院四十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿贝斯」——阿贝嬷嬷是院里说一不二的女当家

root: 叙利亚语 abba「父亲」→ 希腊语 abbas → 拉丁语 abbas「男修道院院长」；古法语加阴性词尾 abbesse，约十四世纪进入英语作 abbess。阴性后缀 -ess 出自拉丁语 -issa。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses share one office: the elected head of nuns, and the same leadership named generally.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项同属一个职分：被推选的修女首领，及其泛称用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mother of a house of nuns, keys and staff in hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座修女院的母亲，手持钥匙与权杖。

branches.en: THE OFFICE ITSELF: one elected woman governs the convent.
branches.cn: 职分本身：一位被推选的女性治理修道院。

branches.en: THE OFFICE IN RECORDS: the title marks leadership wherever nuns live under a rule.
branches.cn: 记载中的职分：凡有修女依规而居，此称号即指其领袖。

branches.en: THE FEMININE PAIR: both senses stand opposite abbot.
branches.cn: 阴性对应：两个义项都与 abbot 相对。

branches.en: AUTHORITY WITHIN WALLS: both are powers inside the enclosure.
branches.cn: 墙内权威：两者都是院墙之内的权力。

branches.en: ONE TITLE, TWO USES: specific head, then general superior.
branches.cn: 一名两用：从具体院长到泛称领袖。

intro.en: The word is a borrowed title with one feminine suffix added in French.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个借来的头衔，法语中加了一个阴性后缀。

latinIntro.en: Syriac abba and Latin abbas are both recorded, so the line of descent is historical.
latinIntro.cn: 叙利亚语 abba 与拉丁语 abbas 均有记载，承传脉络有史可查。

items.example: It began as an address to spiritual teachers.
items.exampleCN: 它起初是对属灵导师的称呼。

items.example: It formalised the title.
It is the English masculine form.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语中的阳性形式。

items.example: It forms abbess and actress alike.
items.exampleCN: 它同样构成 abbess 与 actress。

items.example: It comes from the same title for the place.
items.exampleCN: 它由同一称号转指场所。

items.example: It forms the learned adjective.
It is the masculine base.
It became French -esse.

derivatives.zh: 同族阳性名词，义为「男修道院院长」

definition_zh: 人类；作为整体的全体人（中性集体称谓）
definition_en: human beings taken collectively, used as a neutral term for the species
core_image: 一根冰芯与一片陶片被摆在同一张长桌上，标签写着同一个年份，却来自地球两端
scene: 冰芯与陶片被并排放在同一张长桌上，解说员说这两样记的是同一笔账。 Climate records trapped in ice now count as part of the archive of humankind.
sceneCN: 这里「人类」指作为整体的全体人（第 1 个义项：全体人的集体称谓）；句意为封在冰里的气候记录如今也算作人类档案的一部分。

pos.zh: 人类（不可数集体名词，中性语体；不作复数）

derivatives.zh: humankind 的前件：拉丁 humanus「人的」→ 人的；人
古英语 gecynd「天性、族类」→ 种类；族类（语义偏移：从「天性」到「一类」）
古英语 mancynn「人的族类」→ 人类（语义偏移：第二成分与 man 的阳性用法合并，今多被回避）
human + -ity → 人类；仁厚（语义偏移：兼指全体与品质）
humanus 经法语与拉丁两次借入 → 人的

senses.title: All people collectively
senses.titleCN: 全体人：作为一个整体的集体称谓
senses.definition: human beings considered as one collective, especially in statements about the species
senses.definitionCN: 被当作一个集体的全体人，尤用于关于物种的陈述
senses.example: Climate records trapped in ice now count as part of the archive of humankind.
senses.exampleCN: 封在冰里的气候记录如今也算作人类档案的一部分。
senses.why: Human supplies the species and kind supplies the class; the compound says 'the class of people' in one word, which is why it can stand as the subject of a sentence about everyone.
senses.whyCN: human 提供物种，kind 提供「类」；这个复合词用一个词说出「人这一类」，因此能在一句关于所有人的话里充当主语。

senses.title: The species as a biological entity
senses.titleCN: 作为物种：生物学上的一个单位
senses.definition: the species Homo sapiens treated as a single biological population
senses.definitionCN: 被当作单一生物种群的智人
senses.example: A virus can spread through humankind faster than any border can close.
senses.exampleCN: 病毒穿越人类的速度比任何边界关闭得都快。
senses.why: Once the compound names a class, it can be handed to biology, where a class of people is simply one species with one gene pool.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个复合词命名一个类，便可交给生物学使用；在那里，「人这一类」就是拥有一个基因库的一个物种。

senses.title: The subject of history
senses.titleCN: 历史的主体：文明进程的承担者
senses.definition: people viewed as the collective agent of history and invention
senses.definitionCN: 被看作历史与发明之集体承担者的人
senses.example: Every tool in the case belongs to the long apprenticeship of humankind.
senses.exampleCN: 柜里的每一件工具都属于人类漫长的学徒期。
senses.why: History needs a singular actor for long processes; humankind supplies an actor that is not a nation, a class or a leader.
senses.whyCN: 历史需要为长进程找一个单数行动者；humankind 提供的行动者不是国家、阶级或领袖。

senses.title: Common fate and survival
senses.titleCN: 共同命运：存续与未来的共同承担
senses.definition: the shared stake people have in survival and in what comes next
senses.definitionCN: 人在存续与未来上所共有的利害
senses.example: The treaty was written as a promise to humankind, not to its signatories.
senses.exampleCN: 这份条约写成了对人类的承诺，而不是对签署国的承诺。
senses.why: If the word names everyone, then risks that reach everyone can be addressed to it; the compound became the natural addressee of climate and pandemic arguments.
senses.whyCN: 若这个词指所有人，则波及所有人的风险就可以向它发话；这个复合词于是成了气候与疫病论证的天然受话者。

senses.title: A moral community
senses.titleCN: 道义共同体：人对彼此的义务
senses.definition: all people regarded as bound by obligations to one another
senses.definitionCN: 被视为对彼此负有义务的全体人
senses.example: The argument appealed to a duty owed to humankind rather than to neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 这项论证诉诸对人类的义务，而不是对邻人的义务。
senses.why: Because kind also means a class or a family, the compound can carry a family's mutual obligation and stretch it to the widest possible kinship.
senses.whyCN: 因为 kind 也指一类或一族，这个复合词能带着家族式的相互义务，并把它拉到最宽的亲属范围。

senses.title: The human stock in anthropology
senses.titleCN: 人类这一支：谱系意义上的共同祖先群体
senses.definition: the human lineage viewed as one stock descended from shared ancestors
senses.definitionCN: 被视为出自共同祖先的单一人类谱系
senses.example: Geneticists trace the migrations of humankind from a single African population.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传学家追索人类从单一非洲种群开始的迁徙。
senses.why: Anthropology and genetics need a word for the lineage, not for a culture; humankind fits because it names the stock rather than any of its societies.
senses.whyCN: 人类学与遗传学需要一个指谱系、而非指文化的词；humankind 正合适，因为它命名的是这一支，而非其中任何一个社会。

senses.title: Emphatic rhetorical use
senses.titleCN: 修辞上的强调：把范围推到极限
senses.definition: used in appeals to stress that no group is excluded
senses.definitionCN: 在呼吁中强调不排除任何群体
senses.example: The letter began with a phrase meant to include all humankind and then named only one continent.
senses.exampleCN: 这封公开信开头一句意在涵盖全人类，随后却只点了一个大陆。
senses.why: Because it is slightly formal, the compound suits declarations; the same breadth that makes it useful in appeals makes it easy to abuse.
senses.whyCN: 由于语体略正式，这个复合词适合宣言；使它适用于呼吁的那份广度，也使它容易被滥用。

senses.title: Rational creatures in older discourse
senses.titleCN: 旧时论述中的理性造物：与神相对的受造者
senses.definition: people considered as rational created beings, in older religious and philosophical writing
senses.definitionCN: 旧时宗教与哲学论述中作为理性受造者的人
senses.example: Older sermons addressed humankind as a creature that must account for its reason.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的布道把人类当作须为自己的理性交账的受造者。
senses.why: Before the modern biological sense, the compound's parts pointed to a class defined by nature or creation, so it could stand opposite divinity.
senses.whyCN: 在现代生物学义之前，复合词的两部分指向一个由天性或受造而定的类，因此能与神性相对。

intro.en: Humankind is not a Latin inheritance but an English compound, deliberately assembled in the nineteenth century beside the older mankind; kind is native English, human is Latin-derived.
intro.cn: humankind 不是拉丁遗产，而是英语复合词，于 19 世纪有意在更早的 mankind 之外组装而成；kind 是英语本族词，human 则来自拉丁。

items.en: Gecynd meant 'nature, kind, race', from the root of cynn 'family, tribe'; the modern kind keeps that sense of a class in such phrases as what kind of.
items.cn: gecynd 意为「天性、种类、族类」，出自 cynn「家族、部族」的词根；现代 kind 在「哪一种」这类说法里仍保留「类」的意思。

items.en: Humanus, the adjective of homo 'person', entered English as human and supplied the first element of the compound.
items.cn: humanus 是 homo「人」的形容词，作为 human 进入英语，并提供复合词的前件。

items.en: Mancyn, literally 'the kind of man', had named the race since before the Norman conquest and became the modern mankind.
items.cn: mancyn 字面为「人的族类」，自诺曼征服之前就指人类，后来成为现代的 mankind。

items.en: Humankind was formed by replacing the first element of mankind with human, at a time when man was increasingly felt to exclude women; the word appears in print from the nineteenth century.
items.cn: humankind 是把 mankind 的前件换成 human 而构成，当时 man 越来越被认为排除了女性；该词自 19 世纪见于印刷品。

items.en: In the twentieth century the compound became the standard neutral word in policy, science and declarations about the species.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪，这个复合词成为政策、科学与物种宣言中的标准中性词。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): no single first citation is agreed for the compound, and the pre-English origin of homo behind human remains unsettled, with the humus 'earth' reading a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个复合词没有公认的最早书证；human 背后的 homo 在英语之前来源未定，与 humus「土地」的读法是假说。

note.en: Group one holds the collective nouns that compete directly with humankind; group two holds the words for the species or for people as subjects.
note.cn: 第一组是直接与 humankind 竞争的集体名词；第二组是指物种或以人为主体的词。

entries.definition: The inherited collective noun, increasingly avoided because its first element also means 'adult male'.
entries.definitionCN: 承继而来的集体名词，因前件也指「成年男性」而日渐被回避。

entries.definition: Also means all people, but it additionally means kindness and carries the humanities in the plural.
entries.definitionCN: 也指全体人，但另含仁厚义，复数还指人文学科。

entries.definition: A plainer phrase for the species, common in older writing and in sports commentary.
entries.definitionCN: 指物种的更朴素说法，旧文与体育解说中常见。

entries.definition: The plural of the individual noun: it counts people rather than naming their class.
entries.definitionCN: 个体名词的复数：数人，而非命名人的类。

entries.definition: The technical label for humans as one interbreeding population; colder but more precise.
entries.definitionCN: 把人作为一个可杂交种群的技术称谓；更冷峻也更精确。

entries.definition: The people of a polity considered as an audience or a body of citizens, far narrower than the species.
entries.definitionCN: 把政治共同体中的人视为受众或公民总体，范围远窄于物种。

entries.definition: People considered as an organised system of institutions, not as a biological class.
entries.definitionCN: 把人视为有组织的制度体系，而非生物类别。

entries.definition: A countable set of people in a defined area or category, the unit of demographic work.
entries.definitionCN: 在限定地区或类别中可计数的人群，是人口统计的单位。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds, real origins and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合方式、真实来源与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: human + kind, where kind is the native word for a class or a race, as in what kind of.
normal.cn: human + kind，kind 是表示类或族的本族词，如「哪一种」里的 kind。

normal.en: The word was assembled to replace mankind at a time when man was felt to leave women out.
normal.cn: 这个词是为取代 mankind 而组装的，当时 man 被认为把女性排除在外。

normal.en: The family runs human, humanity, mankind, humankind, human race, human being.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 human、humanity、mankind、humankind、human race、human being。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: the future of humankind, a threat to humankind, for all humankind.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：人类的未来、对人类的威胁、为了全人类。

normal.en: It takes a singular verb: humankind is, not humankind are.
normal.cn: 它接单数谓语，而非复数谓语。

abstract.en: Picture one ledger in which every country has the same signature line.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账，每个国家都在同一行签名。

abstract.en: Picture a family tree so wide that the page must be folded many times.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵宽到纸要折很多次的家谱。

abstract.en: Picture a word built by swapping one brick out of an old wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词，是从一堵旧墙上换下一块砖建成的。

examples.en: The exhibition framed the ice core as a document of humankind.
examples.cn: 展览把这根冰芯呈现为一份人类文献。

examples.en: No single generation owns the climate; it is held in trust for humankind.
examples.cn: 没有哪一代人拥有气候；它是为人类代管的。

examples.en: The word humankind avoids the old objection to mankind without changing the meaning.
examples.cn: humankind 一词避开了对 mankind 的旧异议，而含义不变。

dict_mnemonic.text: human（人的）+ kind（类）＝ 人这一类；记「换下一块旧砖：mankind 的 man 换成 human」。

root: 英语复合词：human（拉丁 humanus「人的」，出自 homo「人」）+ kind（古英语 gecynd「天性、族类」）；19 世纪为回避 mankind 的阳性前件而造。homo 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one compound from a simple class to a formal addressee: everyone, the species, the actor of history, a shared fate, a moral community, the human lineage, a rhetorical breadth and the older rational creature.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着一个复合词从一个简单的类走到正式的受话者：全体人、物种、历史的主体、共同命运、道义共同体、人类谱系、修辞上的广度，以及旧时的理性造物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an ice core and a potsherd on one long table, labelled with the same year though they come from opposite ends of the earth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根冰芯与一片陶片摆在同一张长桌上，标签是同一年份，却来自地球两端。

branches.en: CLASS AND SPECIES: the plain collective, then the same class handed to biology.
branches.cn: 类与物种：先是朴素的集体，再把同一个类交给生物学。

branches.en: LONG PROCESSES: history's singular actor, and the lineage traced by genes.
branches.cn: 长进程：历史的单数行动者，以及由基因追出的谱系。

branches.en: WHAT IS OWED: a fate no group can opt out of, and an obligation that reaches the enemy.
branches.cn: 所欠之物：没有哪个群体能退出的命运，以及延伸到敌人的义务。

branches.en: THE DECLARATION TONE: the breadth that suits appeals and invites abuse.
branches.cn: 宣言腔：适合呼吁的那份广度，也招致滥用。

branches.en: THE OLDER READING: a class defined by creation, standing opposite the divine.
branches.cn: 更早的读法：由受造而定的类，与神性相对。

intro.en: The word is a native-English compound whose first element is Latin-derived and whose second element is inherited Old English, so it mixes two systems openly.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语本族复合词，前件来自拉丁，后件承自古老英语，两套系统公开混在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin humanus supplies the first element through human; Old English gecynd supplies the second through kind. Latin contributes no second element here, since kind is native.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 humanus 经 human 提供前件；古英语 gecynd 经 kind 提供后件。拉丁语在此不提供后件，因为 kind 是本族词。

items.example: The first element names the species.
The second element names the class.
The compound names the class in one word.
items.exampleCN: 复合词用一个词命名这个类。

items.example: The older compound used man for the species.
items.exampleCN: 旧复合词用 man 指物种。

items.example: Humanity overlaps the collective sense.
The possessive marks what belongs to the whole class.
items.exampleCN: 所有格标记属于整个类的东西。

items.example: The adverb modifies how something is done.
The doublet supplies the warm sense.
items.exampleCN: 同源双式词提供温度义。

items.example: The suffix describes shape, not class.
items.exampleCN: 该后缀描述形状，而非类别。

definition_zh: 营养级；生物在取食序列中所处的层级位置
definition_en: the position an organism occupies in a feeding sequence, counted in steps from the primary producer
core_image: 一段被分成几层的阶梯：最下层是藻类，往上依次是小虾、鱼、鹭，每层都标着取食的步数
scene: 同一片水塘里，藻类站在最下面一级，小虾在它上面一级，鱼再上一级，鹭在最上面。 Each species occupies a different trophic level according to what it eats.
sceneCN: 这里指按取食步数确定的位置（第 1 个义项：由取食步数决定的层级位置）；句意为每个物种依据所吃的东西处在不同的营养级。

pos.zh: 营养级（可数短语名词）
取食序列中的层级位置（用于能量与稳定性分析）

derivatives.zh: 该短语的限定词，源自希腊语表示「营养」的词，义为「营养的；取食的」
由该形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「在营养层面上」
由该形容词与表示「级联」的词构成，义为「营养级联」，指跨级的连锁效应
由该形容词与表示「位置」的词构成，义为「营养位置」，是更精确的连续量
由表示「良好」的前缀加词根构成，义为「富营养的」，指养分过多的水体
由表示「稀少」的前缀加词根构成，义为「贫营养的」，指养分很少的水体

senses.title: A position counted in feeding steps
senses.titleCN: 按取食步数计算的位置
senses.definition: the number of steps by which an organism is removed from the primary producer in a feeding sequence
senses.definitionCN: 生物在取食序列中离初级生产者相隔的步数
senses.example: Algae sit at the first trophic level and the heron at the fourth.
senses.exampleCN: 藻类位于第一个营养级，鹭位于第四个。
senses.why: Counting steps is the only way to place an organism without listing its whole diet.
senses.whyCN: 数步数是把生物定位的唯一办法，不必列出它的全部食谱。

senses.title: The standard ladder of producers and consumers
senses.titleCN: 生产者与消费者的标准阶梯
senses.definition: the conventional rungs of producers, primary consumers, secondary consumers and so on
senses.definitionCN: 生产者、初级消费者、次级消费者等惯用层次
senses.example: Primary consumers form the second trophic level in every pond.
senses.exampleCN: 初级消费者在每一片水塘里都构成第二个营养级。
senses.why: Field guides needed fixed rungs, so the conventional order was written into the term.
senses.whyCN: 野外手册需要固定的层级，于是惯用次序被写进了术语。

senses.title: A position, not a species
senses.titleCN: 是位置而非物种的固定属性
senses.definition: a slot that one species can occupy differently depending on diet and life stage
senses.definitionCN: 一个可由同一物种依据食性与生活阶段而占据不同位置的槽位
senses.example: A fish can move between trophic levels as it grows.
senses.exampleCN: 一条鱼会随着长大在营养级之间移动。
senses.why: Diets change with age and season, so the position has to be able to move.
senses.whyCN: 食性随年龄与季节变化，这个位置必须能够移动。

senses.title: A continuous trophic position
senses.definition: a fractional value calculated from diet proportions instead of a whole rung
senses.definitionCN: 由食性比例算出的小数值，而不是整级
senses.example: The goby has a trophic level of two point seven.
senses.exampleCN: 这种虾虎鱼的营养级为二点七。
senses.why: Whole rungs hide mixed diets, so a fractional value was calculated to keep the proportion.
senses.whyCN: 整级掩盖了混合食谱，于是算出小数值以保留比例。

senses.title: Efficiency of transfer between rungs
senses.titleCN: 层与层之间的传递效率
senses.definition: the share of energy passed upward, commonly about a tenth at each step
senses.definitionCN: 向上传递的能量份额，通常每一步约为一成
senses.example: Only a small fraction of energy crosses from one trophic level to the next.
senses.exampleCN: 只有一小部分能量从一个营养级越过到下一个。
senses.why: Energy is lost as heat at every transfer, so the step between rungs became a measurable share.
senses.whyCN: 每次传递都有能量以热的形式损失，层间的这一步于是成了可度量的份额。

senses.title: The basis of trophic cascades
senses.definition: a ladder used to describe effects that skip down several rungs after a top predator changes
senses.definitionCN: 用来描述顶级捕食者改变后效应向下跳过数级的阶梯
senses.example: Wolves altered the whole trophic level structure of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 狼改变了整个谷地的营养级结构。
senses.why: A change at the top shows up several rungs below, and the ladder gave that spread a name.
senses.whyCN: 顶端的改变会显现在下面数层，阶梯给了这种传播一个名字。

senses.title: An index used in water assessment
senses.definition: a score computed from the proportions of organisms at different rungs to judge water quality
senses.definitionCN: 由不同层级生物比例算出、用以判断水质的分数
senses.example: The river's trophic level index rose after the sewage plant opened.
senses.exampleCN: 污水处理厂启用之后，这条河的营养级指数上升了。
senses.why: Water managers needed one number, so the proportions at each rung were folded into a score.
senses.whyCN: 水体管理者需要一个数字，于是各层比例被折叠成一个分数。

senses.title: The apex at the top rung
senses.definition: the highest occupied rung, held by predators that are rarely eaten
senses.definitionCN: 被占据的最高一层，由很少被吃的捕食者把持
senses.example: The shark stands at the highest trophic level in this bay.
senses.exampleCN: 在这片海湾里，鲨鱼站在最高的营养级。
senses.why: The top rung is defined by the absence of predators rather than by any trait of the animal.
senses.whyCN: 最高一层由「没有捕食者」而非动物的任何特征来定义。

senses.title: Rungs in detrital pathways
senses.definition: positions counted from dead matter rather than from living producers
senses.definitionCN: 从死有机质而非活生产者开始计算的位置
senses.example: In the detrital trophic level, the first step is fallen leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 在碎屑营养级路径中，第一步是落下的叶子。
senses.why: Dead matter feeds a sequence of its own, so the count had to start from litter as well as from leaves.
senses.whyCN: 死有机质喂养着它自己的序列，因此计数也必须从枯落物起算。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek adjective for nourishing to a Latin-derived word for a balance. The pairing is a twentieth-century ecology usage built on nineteenth-century energy studies.
intro.cn: 这个短语把希腊语表示「滋养」的形容词，接到一个源自拉丁语、意为「天平」的词上。这一配对是二十世纪生态学在十九世纪能量研究基础上建立的用法。

items.en: Trophe meant nourishment or food, and it supplied the adjective for what feeds.
items.cn: 这个词意为营养或食物，提供了表示「有营养的」的形容词。

items.en: Trephein meant to nourish or to raise, and it is the verb behind the noun.
items.cn: 这个词意为养育、养大，是名词背后的动词。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physiology made the adjective for feeding and nutrition.
items.cn: 十九世纪的生理学造出这个表示取食与营养的形容词。

items.en: Libella meant a small balance or a level, a diminutive of the word for scales.
items.cn: 这个词意为小天平或水平仪，是表示「秤」的词的小称形式。

items.en: French carried the noun into English as level, meaning a flat position in a scale.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词带入英语，意为刻度上的一个水平位置。

items.en: Energy studies of the nineteen forties fixed the phrase as a rung in a feeding ladder; the exact first use is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 二十世纪四十年代的能量研究把这个短语固定为取食阶梯上的一层；确切首见时间只能给约数。

note.en: The first group shares trophic or level; the second group names the quantities and structures built on the rung.
note.cn: 第一组共用 trophic 或 level；第二组是建立在这一层之上的量与结构。

entries.definition: Relating to feeding and nutrition, the first element.
entries.definitionCN: 指与取食和营养有关的，是前半部分。

entries.definition: At the level of feeding relations.
entries.definitionCN: 指在取食关系的层面上。

entries.definition: A flat position on a scale, the second element.
entries.definitionCN: 指刻度上的水平位置，是后半部分。

entries.definition: Rich in nutrients, built on the same feeding stem.
entries.definitionCN: 指养分丰富的，建立在同一个「营养」词干上。

entries.definition: A prize or memorial; it looks close but comes from a word for turning away.
entries.definitionCN: 指奖品或纪念物；形近，但出自表示「转开」的词。

entries.definition: The continuous version of the rung, calculated from diet proportions.
entries.definitionCN: 指这一层的连续形式，由食性比例算出。

entries.definition: The linear sequence on which the rungs are counted.
entries.definitionCN: 指计算层级所依据的线性序列。

entries.definition: The network in which rungs are not single positions but ranges.
entries.definitionCN: 指层级不是单一点而是范围的网络。

entries.definition: A stack showing the losses between rungs.
entries.definitionCN: 指展示层间损耗的堆叠图。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the feeding stem, the balance word and the tenth rule.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「营养」词干、「天平」一词与「一成」规则。

normal.en: Trophe is nourishment, so trophic means to do with feeding.
normal.cn: 词根意为营养，所以这个形容词意为与取食有关。

normal.en: The rungs are producer, first consumer, second consumer, and so on.
normal.cn: 层级依次是生产者、第一消费者、第二消费者，如此类推。

normal.en: A species is not nailed to a rung; a growing fish climbs.
normal.cn: 物种并不被钉在某一层；长大的鱼会往上爬。

normal.en: Roughly a tenth of the energy passes to the next rung, which caps the ladder's height.
normal.cn: 大约一成能量传到下一层，这给阶梯的高度设了上限。

normal.en: Level came from a small balance, so each rung is a weighing point.
normal.cn: 后半原指小天平，所以每一层都是一个称量点。

abstract.en: A trophic level is a coordinate, not an identity: it says where a body sits in the flow, not what it is.
abstract.cn: 营养级是一个坐标，不是身份：它说的是一个身体在能流中的位置，而不是它是什么。

abstract.en: Each step upward is a tax paid in energy, which is why the top of any ladder is thinly populated.
abstract.cn: 每向上一层都要用能量缴税，这就是任何阶梯顶端都稀疏的原因。

abstract.en: The same animal can be a predator in one calculation and prey in the next, so the rung is a relation rather than a rank.
abstract.cn: 同一只动物在一次计算里是捕食者，在下一次里是猎物，因此这一层是关系而不是等级。

examples.en: Grasshoppers feed at the second trophic level in this meadow.
examples.cn: 在这片草甸里，蝗虫在第二个营养级取食。

examples.en: Long-lived predators sit at a high trophic level and accumulate toxins.
examples.cn: 寿命长的捕食者处在高营养级，因而累积毒素。

examples.en: The study compared biomass across four trophic levels.
examples.cn: 这项研究比较了四个营养级上的生物量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「特罗菲克 莱沃」——特罗菲克是营养，莱沃是层级，按营养排出的层级就是营养级

root: 希腊语 trophē「营养」← trephein「养育」→ 英语中表示「营养的」形容词；拉丁语 libella「小天平」← libra「秤」→ 古法语 livel → 英语中表示「层级」的名词。二十世纪四十年代的能量研究把两者固定为取食阶梯的层级，确切首见时间只能给约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses hold one coordinate and vary what is counted: steps, the standard ladder, species versus position, fractional values, transfer efficiency, cascades, indices, the apex and detrital rungs.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项守住同一个坐标，只改变所数的东西：步数、标准阶梯、物种与位置的差别、连续数值、传递效率、级联、指数、顶端与碎屑路径。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a short ladder from algae through shrimp and fish to the heron, each step marked with a feeding count.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段从藻类经小虾、鱼到鹭的短阶梯，每一层都标着取食步数。

branches.en: THE LADDER: positions counted from the producer, in the conventional order.
branches.cn: 阶梯：从生产者起算的位置，按惯用顺序排列。

branches.en: THE SLOT: a position a species may occupy differently as it grows or changes diet.
branches.cn: 槽位：同一物种随生长或食性变化可能占据的不同位置。

branches.en: THE CONTINUOUS VALUE: a fractional position computed from diet proportions.
branches.cn: 连续值：由食性比例算出的分数位置。

branches.en: THE ACCOUNTING: a tenth passing upward, and indices used to judge water.
branches.cn: 核算：一成向上传递，以及用来判断水质的指数。

branches.en: THE STRUCTURES: cascades across rungs, an apex at the top, and rungs counted from dead matter.
branches.cn: 结构：跨层的级联、顶端的顶级者，以及从死有机质起算的层级。

intro.en: A Greek nourishment stem and a Latin balance word make the phrase, and both still generate vocabulary.
intro.cn: 希腊语「营养」词干与拉丁语「天平」词构成这个短语，两者至今都在生成词汇。

latinIntro.en: The first element is Greek, so Latin entries belong to the second half and to the derived scientific words.
latinIntro.cn: 前半是希腊语，因此拉丁语词条属于后半以及派生出的科学词。

items.example: It marks everything to do with feeding.
items.exampleCN: 它标记与取食有关的一切。

items.example: It makes the adjective.
It is the recorded Greek source.
items.exampleCN: 它是有记录的希腊语来源。

items.example: It is the verb behind the noun.
It is the recorded source of the second element.
items.exampleCN: 它是后半部分有记录的来源。

items.example: It is the base of the diminutive.
It forms the adjective of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 它构成该名词的形容词。

items.example: It marks nutrient-rich water.
items.exampleCN: 它标记养分丰富的水体。

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语词干加形容词词尾构成，义为「营养的」
由该形容词与表示「级联」的词构成，义为「营养级联」
由表示「良好」的前缀加该词干构成，义为「富营养的」
由表示「稀少」的前缀加该词干构成，义为「贫营养的」

definition_zh: 证人陈述；证人证言书；目击者笔录
definition_en: a written account by a witness of what they saw, used as evidence in an investigation or a case
core_image: 一页签过名的陈述纸被夹进案卷，页脚是日期与警员编号
scene: 警员把目击者口述的内容逐条写下，请他在页脚签名。 She signed her witness statement at the station.
sceneCN: 这里 witness statement 指证人签署的书面陈述（第 1 个义项：警方记录并用作证据的证人书面陈述）；句意为她在警局签了自己的证人陈述。图中可辨识物件：陈述纸、签名栏、警员编号、案卷夹。

pos.zh: 证人陈述（可数名词短语，复数 witness statements）
（英国程序）证人依规则交换的书面陈述

senses.title: A police-recorded statement
senses.titleCN: 警方记录的证人书面陈述
senses.definition: the written account a witness gives to the police, signed as accurate
senses.definitionCN: 证人向警方提供并签名确认内容属实的书面陈述
senses.example: She signed her witness statement at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她在警局签了自己的证人陈述。
senses.why: The phrase joins the person who saw the event to the paper that records it, so the written record replaces the spoken voice.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把看见事件的人与记录其言的纸页连在一起，于是书面记录替代了口头陈述。

senses.title: An account given to investigators
senses.titleCN: 目击者向调查者提供的书面说明
senses.definition: a written description supplied to any official investigator
senses.definitionCN: 向任何官方调查者提交的书面描述
senses.example: Inspectors took a witness statement from every worker on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员向车间每位工人都取了一份证人陈述。
senses.why: Once the phrase leaves police stations it keeps the shape: a witness, a written account, a signature.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语离开警局后仍保持原形：一个证人、一份书面叙述、一个签名。

senses.title: A document tendered as proof
senses.titleCN: 作为证据提交的书面证词
senses.definition: a written statement put before a court or tribunal as evidence
senses.definitionCN: 提交给法院或审裁机构作为证据的书面陈述
senses.example: The bundle of witness statements ran to four hundred pages.
senses.exampleCN: 那捆证人陈述多达四百页。
senses.why: A bundle is the court's way of counting many separate pairs of eyes.
senses.whyCN: 一捆材料是法院清点许多双眼睛的方式。

senses.title: A record in an accident inquiry
senses.titleCN: 事故调查中的目击记录
senses.definition: the written account of a bystander collected after an accident
senses.definitionCN: 事故发生后采集的旁观者书面叙述
senses.example: The rail inquiry relied on witness statements taken the same night.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路调查依靠当晚采集的目击记录。
senses.why: An inquiry collects statements early, while memories are still close to the event.
senses.whyCN: 调查组尽早采集陈述，因为此时记忆还贴近事件。

senses.title: A step in civil procedure
senses.titleCN: 民事诉讼中交换的证人陈述
senses.definition: a signed statement exchanged between parties under court rules before trial
senses.definitionCN: 依法院规则在审前由各方交换的签名陈述
senses.example: Under the rules each side must exchange witness statements before the hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 依规则，双方必须在听证前交换证人陈述。
senses.why: Civil procedure gave the compound a fixed place in the timetable, not merely a record of what someone saw.
senses.whyCN: 民事程序给这个复合词确定了时间表上的位置，它不再只是「某人看见了什么」的记录。

senses.title: A form in insurance claims
senses.titleCN: 保险理赔中的目击者说明
senses.definition: a written account from a bystander attached to a claim file
senses.definitionCN: 附在理赔档案中的旁观者书面说明
senses.example: The insurer asked for a witness statement from the driver behind her.
senses.exampleCN: 保险公司要求她后方那辆车的司机提供目击者说明。
senses.why: An insurer needs the same structure as a court: a named person, a signed account, a date.
senses.whyCN: 保险公司需要与法院相同的结构：一个具名的人、一份签名的叙述、一个日期。

senses.title: A quotation in reporting
senses.titleCN: 媒体引述的目击者说法
senses.definition: the account a reporter attributes to a person who was present
senses.definitionCN: 记者归到在场者名下的叙述
senses.example: The report quoted a witness statement describing the smoke.
senses.exampleCN: 报道引用了一段描述烟情的目击者说法。
senses.why: Journalism borrows the legal label to make a quotation look attested.
senses.whyCN: 新闻业借用这个法律标签，让引语看起来经过核实。

senses.title: A spoken account written down
senses.definition: a loose term for an account written down from a witness's dictation
senses.definitionCN: 对「按证人口述记录下来的说法」的宽泛称呼
senses.example: The clerk typed the witness statement while the man spoke.
senses.exampleCN: 那名男子说话时，职员把他的陈述打了下来。
senses.why: When a clerk writes down dictation, the paper records a voice rather than a signed account.
senses.whyCN: 当职员照口述记录时，纸页记录的是声音，而不是一份签名的陈述。

intro.en: Witness statement is an English compound of two elements: witness, a native word from Old English witnes, and statement, from state plus -ment, where state goes back to Latin status 'standing, position'. The compound is recorded in police and legal usage from the nineteenth century onward. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: witness statement 是由两个成分构成的英语复合词：witness 是古英语 witnes 的本族词，statement 由 state 加 -ment 构成，而 state 可追溯至拉丁 status「站立、状态」。这个复合词自十九世纪起见于警务与法律用法。年代均为约数。

items.en: Witnes joined wit 'knowledge' to an abstract suffix and named a person who knows an event.
items.cn: witnes 由 wit「知识」加抽象后缀构成，指对事件知情的人。

items.en: Status meant 'standing, position, condition' and gives English state and status.
items.cn: status 意为「站立、位置、状况」，衍生英语 state 与 status。

items.en: State plus -ment produced statement, first a statement of facts and later a formal account.
items.cn: state 加 -ment 构成 statement，最初指事实陈述，后指正式叙述。

items.en: Witness statement appears in police practice once statements were written down and signed as routine procedure.
items.cn: 当书面陈述与签名成为例行程序后，witness statement 便出现在警务实践中。

items.en: Modern civil rules gave the phrase a precise slot: a signed document exchanged before trial.
items.cn: 现代民事规则给这个短语一个精确位置：审前交换的签名文件。

items.en: Both parts of the compound are well documented and the chain is clear; only the earliest use of the exact phrase is not firmly dated.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：复合词的两个成分都有充分记录，构词链清楚，只有这个确切短语的最早书证没有确定年代。

note.en: Group one holds near-identical compounds that differ by one element; group two holds the legal documents most often confused with a witness statement.
note.cn: 第一组是只差一个成分的近形复合词；第二组是最常与证人陈述混淆的法律文件。

entries.definition: Any formal account of facts; without witness it does not say who gave it.
entries.definitionCN: 任何正式的事实陈述；不带 witness 就不说明是谁说的。

entries.definition: Re- plus statement: a second version of an account, often in clearer words.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀 re-（表示「再、重新」）加 statement：同一说法的第二次表述，往往更清楚。

entries.definition: Under- plus statement: an account that deliberately makes something sound smaller than it is.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀 under-（表示「不足」）加 statement：故意把某事说得比实际更轻的表述。

entries.definition: Mis- plus statement: a statement containing an error, whether careless or deliberate.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀 mis-（表示「错误」）加 statement：含有错误的陈述，无论疏忽还是有意。

entries.definition: A written statement confirmed by oath before an authorised person; the oath is what defines it.
entries.definitionCN: 在有权者面前宣誓确认的书面陈述，定义性特征是誓言。

entries.definition: Sworn testimony recorded out of court during litigation, used later at trial.
entries.definitionCN: 诉讼过程中在庭外录取的宣誓证词，供审判时使用。

entries.definition: The evidence a witness gives orally, not the paper it is written on.
entries.definitionCN: 证人口头提供的证据，而不是承载它的纸页。

entries.definition: A formal statement on paper, which may or may not carry an oath.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的书面陈述，可能宣誓也可能没有。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Witness plus statement: the person who saw, plus the paper that records it.
normal.cn: witness 加 statement：看见的人，加上记录其言的纸。

normal.en: The compound keeps a regular plural: witness statements.
normal.cn: 这个复合词的复数是规则的：witness statements。

normal.en: Procedure verbs pair with it: make, sign, exchange, retract.
normal.cn: 程序动词与它搭配：作出、签署、交换、撤回。

normal.en: Police and civil courts both use it, but with different routines around it.
normal.cn: 警方与民事法院都用它，只是围绕它的程序不同。

normal.en: Affidavit and deposition are sworn documents; a witness statement need not be sworn in the same way.
normal.cn: affidavit 与 deposition 都是宣誓文件，证人陈述则未必以同样方式宣誓。

abstract.en: Picture a spoken sentence pressed flat onto paper and given a signature.
abstract.cn: 想象一句口头的话被压平到纸上，再配上一个签名。

abstract.en: Picture a case file where each page is one person's pair of eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象一册案卷，每一页都是一个人的一双眼睛。

abstract.en: Picture a statement that has been signed but not yet tested.
abstract.cn: 想象一份已经签名、尚未经受检验的陈述。

examples.en: The officer read the witness statement back to her before she signed.
examples.cn: 警员在她签名前把证人陈述读了一遍给她听。

examples.en: Both parties must exchange witness statements two weeks before the hearing.
examples.cn: 双方必须在听证前两周交换证人陈述。

examples.en: A single witness statement cannot carry the whole case.
examples.cn: 仅凭一份证人陈述撑不起整个案子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「witness（证人）+ statement（陈述）」——证人签字的书面陈述

root: 英语复合词：witness（古英语 witnes，本族词）+ statement（state + -ment，state 出自拉丁 status「站立、状况」）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one sheet of paper: it starts in a police station, then serves any investigator, then a court bundle, an accident file, a civil timetable, an insurance claim, a news quotation and finally a loose name for dictation written down.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一页纸走：先在警局，再供任何调查者使用，随后进入庭审材料、事故档案、民事时间表、理赔档案、新闻引述，最后成为「按口述记录」的宽泛说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signed sheet of paper with a date and an officer number at the foot, clipped into a case file.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页签过名的陈述纸，页脚写着日期与警员编号，被夹进案卷。

branches.en: THE FIRST SETTING: a police station statement and the same practice used by any investigator.
branches.cn: 最初的场景：警局里的陈述，以及任何调查者采用的同样做法。

branches.en: ON THE RECORD: a bundle for court and a file for an accident inquiry both hold signed pages.
branches.cn: 进入记录：庭审材料与事故档案里装的都是签名页。

branches.en: THE TIMETABLE: civil rules turn the sheet into a step to be completed before trial.
branches.cn: 时间表：民事规则把这页纸变成审前必须完成的一步。

branches.en: ELSEWHERE USED: an insurer's file and a newspaper quotation both borrow the phrase.
branches.cn: 别处借用：保险档案与报纸引述都借用了这个说法。

branches.en: THE LOOSE NAME: dictation typed down by a clerk is still called by the same phrase.
branches.cn: 宽泛的称呼：职员照口述打下来的记录，仍用同一个说法。

intro.en: Witness statement is an English compound: one native element and one element that goes back to Latin status.
intro.cn: witness statement 是英语复合词：一个本族成分，一个可追溯至拉丁 status 的成分。

latinIntro.en: Only statement has a Latin line, through state and status. Witness is Germanic, so the Latin list records status and its relatives rather than any supposed source of the whole phrase.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 statement 有拉丁线索，经 state 上溯至 status。witness 属日耳曼语层，因此拉丁词条记录 status 及其同族，而不是整个短语的所谓来源。

items.meaning: a person who knows an event
items.example: The witness signed at the foot.
The state of the file was recorded.
items.exampleCN: 档案的状态被记录在案。

items.example: The suffix turns the act of stating into a thing stated.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「陈述」的动作变成「陈述」的成品。

items.example: The statement ran to three pages.

items.example: The officer took a witness statement.

items.example: The statements were exchanged on time.
She was ready to testify.
The testimony matched the sheet.
items.exampleCN: 证词与那份书面材料一致。

definition_zh: 秃；秃头；光秃；直白无饰
definition_en: the state of having little or no hair on the head; also, plainness or bareness of style or land
core_image: 头顶那片亮得能反光的空白
scene: 剃刀划过，理发师吹去碎发。 His baldness began at the crown in his thirties.
sceneCN: 这里 baldness 指「秃头」（第 1 个义项：头发脱落的状态）；句意：他三十多岁起就从头顶开始谢顶。

pos.zh: 秃头；光秃；直白

derivatives.zh: 秃的；光秃的；直白的（baldness 的形容词基础）
白头海雕（bald 旧义 white-haired 的存留）

senses.title: Loss of hair on the head
senses.definition: the condition of having little or no scalp hair, natural or shaved
senses.definitionCN: 头皮少发或无发的状态，无论自然脱落还是剃除
senses.example: Baldness runs in his family.
senses.exampleCN: 他家有秃头遗传。
senses.why: The root is bald, from a word for white or shining patch.
senses.whyCN: 词根是 bald，源于一个表「白斑、亮斑」的词。

senses.title: Pattern loss, the medical state
senses.definition: in medicine, progressive hair loss, as alopecia or male-pattern baldness
senses.definitionCN: 医学上指进行性脱发，如斑秃、男性型脱发
senses.example: Treatments slow male-pattern baldness but rarely reverse it.
senses.exampleCN: 疗法能延缓男性型脱发，却很少逆转。
senses.why: Clinics named the common condition with the common word.
senses.whyCN: 临床用日常词命名了常见病症。

senses.title: Bareness of land or things
senses.definition: the bare, unadorned state of hills, tires, or furniture
senses.definitionCN: 山丘、轮胎、家具等裸露无饰的状态
senses.example: The baldness of the hilltop showed every rock.
senses.exampleCN: 山顶光秃，每块岩石都一览无余。
senses.why: No hair, no grass, no tread: the metaphor is one bareness.
senses.whyCN: 无发、无草、无胎纹：共享同一个「裸」的隐喻。

senses.title: Plainness of language
senses.definition: of writing or speech, stark plainness without ornament or hedge
senses.definitionCN: 指文字或言语不加修饰、不留余地的朴素
senses.example: The memo's baldness stunned the staff.
senses.exampleCN: 备忘录直白得让员工震惊。
senses.why: Uncovered truth is bald truth: nothing hides it.
senses.whyCN: 赤裸的事实即 bald truth：无一物遮掩。

senses.title: Bluntness that discomforts
senses.definition: frankness so bare it embarrasses or offends
senses.definitionCN: 直白到令人尴尬或冒犯的坦率
senses.example: The baldness of his verdict silenced the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他裁断之直率令满室哑然。
senses.why: Bareness exposes; exposure stings.
senses.whyCN: 裸露即曝光，曝光即刺痛。

senses.title: The bald eagle's white head
senses.definition: in bald eagle, an older sense of bald meaning white-patched
senses.definitionCN: bald eagle 中保留 bald 的旧义「白斑的」
senses.example: The bald eagle's baldness is feathers, white as snow.
senses.exampleCN: 白头海雕的「秃」其实是雪白的羽毛。
senses.why: An obsolete meaning survives fossilized in the bird's name.
senses.whyCN: 废义在鸟名中化石化保存。

senses.title: Shorn acceptance, a style
senses.definition: deliberate shaving as a look, not a loss
senses.definitionCN: 作为造型的主动剃光，而非脱发
senses.example: His baldness was a decision, razor and mirror.
senses.exampleCN: 他的光头是剃刀与镜子共同的决定。
senses.why: Loss became choice as shaving went mainstream.
senses.whyCN: 随着剃头流行，「失去」变成了「选择」。

senses.title: Figurative stripping of excuses
senses.definition: the exposure of an argument stripped of its padding
senses.definitionCN: 论证被剥去铺垫后的赤裸状态
senses.example: Cross-examination laid bare the baldness of the defense.
senses.exampleCN: 交叉质证让辩方论证的不堪一击暴露无遗。
senses.why: Strip the wig of rhetoric and the scalp shows.
senses.whyCN: 剥去修辞的假发，头皮便露了出来。

intro.en: Baldness is bald plus -ness; bald itself first meant white-patched or shining, probably from a Celtic or Germanic root for a white blaze, and came to mean hairless by the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: baldness 由 bald + -ness 构成；bald 本义「有白斑的、发亮的」，或出自凯尔特或日耳曼语中表「白色斑纹」的词根，14 世纪起转指「无发的」。

items.en: The blaze-root is reconstructed as bhel-, to shine or burn white.
items.cn: 「白亮」词根被重构为 bhel-「发白光、燃烧」。

items.en: Welsh bal and ball meant a white forehead or bald head, the likely source.
items.cn: 威尔士语 bal、ball 意为白额或秃头，是可能的来源。

items.en: Bald meant white-patched, then hairless, by the 1300s.
items.cn: 中古英语 bald 先指有白斑，14 世纪转指无发。

items.en: The older white sense fossilized in the bird's seventeenth-century name.
items.cn: 「白斑」旧义化石化于 17 世纪的鸟名中。

items.en: The figurative plainness sense grew in prose criticism.
items.cn: 16 至 18 世纪「直白无饰」的比喻义在散文批评中发展。

items.en: Baldness names a medical condition, a style, and a critical verdict on prose.
items.cn: 如今 baldness 兼指医学病症、造型选择与文风评语。

note.en: Group one gathers the blaze family and a famous homophone; group two gathers bareness words.
note.cn: 第一组收「白亮」词族与著名同音词；第二组收裸露义场的词。

entries.definition: past of bawl, to shout or wail; sounds identical to bald.
entries.definitionCN: bawl 的过去式，大声喊叫；与 bald 同音异义。

entries.definition: a narrative song; nearly the spelling of baldness's base with an extra l.
entries.definitionCN: 叙事歌谣；与 bald 拼写仅差一个 l，词源无关。

entries.definition: brave; one vowel from bald, a classic ESL slip.
entries.definitionCN: 大胆的；与 bald 仅一元音之差，常见混淆。

entries.definition: the medical term for hair loss.
entries.definitionCN: 脱发的医学术语。

entries.definition: the general state of being uncovered.
entries.definitionCN: 裸露无覆盖的一般状态。

entries.definition: frankness without polish.
entries.definitionCN: 不加修饰的直率。

entries.definition: barrenness of land or style.
entries.definitionCN: 土地或文风的贫瘠。

entries.definition: hairiness; the direct opposite state.
entries.definitionCN: 多毛；baldness 的直接反义。

normalIntro.en: The word is bald plus -ness: take the adjective, add the state.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 bald 加 -ness：形容词加状态。

normal.en: bald, bold, bawled: three ways to trip in spelling.
normal.cn: bald、bold、bawled：三个易混拼写。

normal.en: bald eagle keeps the old sense: white-patched head.

normal.cn: male-pattern baldness 是标准医学短语。

normal.en: bald statement means plain, unadorned speech.
normal.cn: bald statement 指直白无饰的陈述。

normal.en: Root memory: bhel-, shine; the shiny scalp gave the name.
normal.cn: 词根记忆：bhel-「发亮」，亮头皮由此得名。

abstract.en: See noon light land on a bare crown.
abstract.cn: 看正午的光落在光秃的头顶。

abstract.en: Baldness of prose is the room with the furniture gone.
abstract.cn: 文风的秃，是搬走家具后的空房间。

abstract.en: Feel the wind where hair used to argue with it.
abstract.cn: 感受风吹过头发曾与之争执的地方。

examples.en: He embraced baldness at forty and never looked back.
examples.cn: 他四十岁时坦然接受秃顶，再无回头。

examples.en: The report's baldness left no room for spin.
examples.cn: 报告直白得没有回旋余地。

examples.en: Wind combed the baldness of the moor all afternoon.
examples.cn: 整个下午，风梳理着荒原的光秃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「暴力的」——暴力的发型，一根头发都不留

root: baldness = bald + -ness。bald 约于 14 世纪见于中古英语，本义「有白斑的、发亮的」，词根可追溯至印欧语 bhel-「发白光」，一般认为经不列颠凯尔特语（威尔士语 bal「白额」）进入英语，后转指「无发的」；旧义「白斑」存留于 bald eagle（白头海雕）。16 世纪起发展出「直白无饰」的比喻义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the scalp outward: the medical condition, the bare hill, the stark sentence, the uncomfortable truth, the eagle's fossilized white, and the shaved choice.
sensesIntro.cn: 八义项从头皮向外延展：医学病症、光秃的山、直白的句子、刺人的真相、白头海雕的化石化旧义，以及剃发的选择。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright, bare patch where covering used to be.
core.cn: 核心意象：原本有覆盖的地方，如今只剩一块发亮的空白。

branches.en: THE HAIR SIDE: loss, disease, and chosen shaving.
branches.cn: 头发一面：脱落、病症与主动剃除。

branches.en: THE LAND SIDE: grassless hills and worn tires.
branches.cn: 土地一面：无草之丘与磨平的轮胎。

branches.en: THE LANGUAGE SIDE: plainness, bluntness, stripped arguments.
branches.cn: 语言一面：直白、刺人的坦率、被剥净的论证。

branches.en: THE FOSSIL SIDE: the eagle's old white sense.
branches.cn: 化石一面：鹰名中保留的旧义「白」。

branches.en: THE WHITE SIDE: the older meaning kept in the eagle's name.
branches.cn: 白色一面：鹰名中留存的旧义「白」。

intro.cn: baldness 由形容词 bald 加名词后缀 -ness 构成。

latinIntro.cn: 词根属凯尔特-日耳曼系而非拉丁系；临床语域由拉丁借词 alopecia 承担。

definition_zh: 住所；住宅；（考古）居址；居住的状态
definition_en: a place where a person or animal lives; the fact or state of living in a place
core_image: 山坡上一座低矮的石屋，屋顶压着厚草，窗内亮着一盏灯，门外只有风声
scene: 考古队在河谷台地上清理出一处下沉地面的房屋遗迹。 The team uncovered a sunken-floor dwelling on the river terrace.
sceneCN: 这里 dwelling 指「供人居住的房屋」（第 1 个义项：人长期居住的建筑）；句意为考古队在河谷台地上发掘出一座地面下凹的住所。图中可辨识物件：石砌墙基、草顶残迹、门洞、散落陶片。

pos.zh: 住所；住宅；居所
居住用的（多用于复合词，如 dwelling house）

derivatives.zh: 居住；栖身（由「停留」义转来）
住宅房屋，法律文本中与商业建筑相对

senses.title: A building used as a home
senses.definition: a building or part of a building in which people live
senses.definitionCN: 供人居住的建筑物或其一部分
senses.example: The old farmhouse is the only dwelling on the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老农舍是山脊上唯一的住所。
senses.why: dwelling is the noun made from the present participle of dwell, so it names the place where the staying happens.
senses.whyCN: dwelling 由「居住」这一动词的现在分词转为名词，因此指「停留这件事发生的那个地方」。

senses.title: A simple shelter rather than a house
senses.definition: a place that gives shelter, especially a simple, rough or temporary one
senses.definitionCN: 提供遮蔽的处所，尤指简陋或临时的住所
senses.example: They spent the winter in a turf dwelling cut into the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在河岸上挖出的草皮小屋里过冬。
senses.why: the older verb meant simply to stay in one spot, so the noun can cover a hut or a hole as readily as a house.
senses.whyCN: 旧义只表示「待在一个地方」，所以这个词既能指房屋，也能指草棚土穴。

senses.title: A housing unit counted in official records
senses.titleCN: 统计与法规中的住宅单位
senses.definition: a unit of housing counted separately in a census or defined by housing law
senses.definitionCN: 人口普查中单独计数、或由住房法规界定的住宅单元
senses.example: The census counts each dwelling and the people inside it.
senses.exampleCN: 人口普查把每套住宅和住在里面的人分别计数。
senses.why: statistics needed a countable object, so the noun was narrowed to one self-contained place of residence.
senses.whyCN: 统计需要一个可计数的对象，这个词于是被收窄为「一套独立住宅」。

senses.title: The home of a wild animal
senses.definition: the place where a wild animal lives, such as a burrow, den or nest
senses.definitionCN: 野生动物生活的地方，如洞穴、兽窝或巢
senses.example: Badgers enlarge a dwelling that is passed down through generations.
senses.exampleCN: 獾会把一代代传下来的洞穴越挖越大。
senses.why: since dwell can be said of any creature that stays in one place, the noun followed animals as easily as people.
senses.whyCN: 既然任何长居一处的生物都能说「居住」，这个名词自然也能用于动物。

senses.title: A habitation site studied by archaeologists
senses.definition: the remains of a place where people once lived, studied as a site
senses.definitionCN: 古人曾经居住、作为遗址被研究的遗存
senses.example: The dwelling yielded pottery shards and a hearth.
senses.exampleCN: 这处居址出土了陶片和一个火塘。
senses.why: archaeology borrowed the word because it names the place of living without promising that a building still stands.
senses.whyCN: 考古学借用这个词，因为它只指明「居住过的地方」，并不保证建筑还存在。

senses.title: The state of living in a place
senses.definition: the condition or fact of living in a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地点生活的状态或事实
senses.example: Forest dwelling shaped the architecture of the upland villages.
senses.exampleCN: 林中居住的生活方式塑造了高地村落的建筑。
senses.why: the participle still keeps the verb's action, so it can name the fact of living and not only the building.
senses.whyCN: 分词仍保留动词的动作义，因此既能指建筑，也能指「居住」这一事实。

senses.title: A place where a deity is said to live
senses.definition: a place where a divine being is said to live or to be present
senses.definitionCN: 据说神灵居住或降临的处所
senses.example: Pilgrims climbed toward the dwelling of the mountain god.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者向着山神的居所攀登。
senses.why: religious language reused the same image: a being that stays in one place has a dwelling there.
senses.whyCN: 宗教语言沿用同一意象：长驻一处的存在，在那里就有居所。

senses.title: A house type named by its structure
senses.titleCN: 按形制划分的住屋类型
senses.definition: a category of house named by its structure or material, as a cave, stilt or cliff dwelling
senses.definitionCN: 按结构或材料命名的一类房屋，如窑洞、吊脚楼、崖居
senses.example: Stilt dwellings line the estuary to stay above the tide.
senses.exampleCN: 吊脚楼沿河口排开，以避开潮水。
senses.why: architecture turns the noun into a classifier, so one word can label many building types found around the world.
senses.whyCN: 建筑学把这个名词当作分类标签，于是一个词就能命名世界各地多种住屋形式。

intro.en: Dwelling is native English: it is the noun use of the participle of dwell, a Germanic verb recorded in Old English as dwellan. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: dwelling 是英语本族词：由日耳曼语动词 dwell 的分词转作名词，该动词在古英语中写作 dwellan。年代均为约数。

items.en: Old English dwellan is recorded with the sense 'to lead astray, hinder, delay', a meaning still visible in the verb's early use.
items.cn: 古英语 dwellan 有「使迷路、阻碍、延迟」的意思，这一含义在动词早期用法中仍可见到。

items.en: In Middle English the verb shifted toward 'to remain, continue in a place', and that sense drove out the older one in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 到中古英语，动词转向「停留、继续待在某地」，这一词义在日常语言中取代了旧义。

items.en: The participial noun dwelling is recorded from the late fourteenth century in the sense 'place of residence'.
items.cn: 分词名词 dwelling 自十四世纪后期起有书证，意为「居住之处」。

items.en: English law fixed the compound dwelling house, and social surveys made dwelling a countable unit of housing.
items.cn: 英国法律固定了复合词 dwelling house，社会调查又把 dwelling 变成可计数的住房单位。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): no pre-Old-English form is established, and the links proposed to a Germanic root meaning 'to delay' are hypotheses rather than demonstrated derivations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：古英语之前的形态没有定论，把它联系到某个意为「延迟」的日耳曼词根，只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close to dwelling, including one different root that is often mistaken for a relative; group two holds nouns with a similar meaning but a different focus.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近的词，其中有一个不同词根常被误认作同族；第二组是意义相近但侧重不同的名词。

entries.definition: The verb from which the noun is formed; it means to live in a place and also, in the phrase dwell on, to keep talking or thinking about something.
entries.definitionCN: 构成该名词的动词，意为居住在某地；在 dwell on 中又指反复谈论或思考某事。

entries.definition: Dwell plus the agent suffix -er, naming the person who lives in a place, as in city dweller.
entries.definitionCN: dwell 加施事后缀 -er，指住在某处的人，如城市居民。

entries.definition: From swell 'to grow larger', not from dwell; it looks close on the page but has no family relation.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 swell「膨胀」，与 dwell 无关；书写形近，但并非同族。

entries.definition: The older irregular past and past participle of dwell, still common in British usage beside dwelled.
entries.definitionCN: dwell 较旧的规则外过去式与过去分词，在英式用法中仍常与 dwelled 并存。

entries.definition: A formal word for the home where someone lives, often used of impressive houses or official homes.
entries.definitionCN: 指某人居所的正式用词，常用于气派的宅第或官邸。

entries.definition: A literary or slightly old-fashioned word for a home, often suggesting a humble or fixed place.
entries.definitionCN: 文学性或略旧的「住所」一词，常暗示简陋或固定。

entries.definition: A formal word that stresses the act or fact of living in a place, and only secondarily the building.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用词，强调居住这一行为或事实，指建筑反而是次要的。

entries.definition: A place to stay for a time, usually paid for and not a permanent home.
entries.definitionCN: 短期居住的地方，通常付费，并非永久住所。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实复合词与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: dwell plus -ing: the suffix turns the verb into the place where the staying happens.
normal.cn: dwell 加 -ing：后缀把动词变成「停留发生的那个地方」。

normal.en: The verb has two past forms, irregular dwelt and regular dwelled, and both are acceptable.
normal.cn: 这个动词有两种过去式：不规则 dwelt 与规则 dwelled，两者都可接受。

normal.en: Compounds name building types: cave dwelling, cliff dwelling, stilt dwelling.
normal.cn: 复合词标出建筑类型：窑洞、崖居、吊脚楼。

normal.en: Legal English says dwelling house when it means a building protected as a home.
normal.cn: 法律英语用 dwelling house 指受住宅法规保护的房屋。

normal.en: The family runs dwell, dweller, dwelling, indwelling.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 dwell、dweller、dwelling、indwelling。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that has stayed lit in a valley for years, and the room beneath it is the dwelling.
abstract.cn: 想象山谷里一盏亮了多年的灯，灯下的那间屋子就是居所。

abstract.en: Picture a snail carrying its shell, a home that moves only because the owner moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一只背着壳的蜗牛，家之所以移动，只因主人移动。

abstract.en: Picture a pin pressed into a map, and the single point under it is where life is anchored.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚按在地图上的图钉，钉尖那一点就是生活被固定下来的地方。

examples.en: The survey found that half the dwellings in the district lacked running water.
examples.cn: 调查发现该区半数住宅没有自来水。

examples.en: Owls nested in the ruined dwelling for decades.
examples.cn: 猫头鹰在那座废弃的住所里筑巢数十年。

examples.en: The law protects a dwelling from being demolished without a permit.
examples.cn: 法律保护住宅，未经许可不得拆除。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「dwell（停留）+ ing」——停下来不走的地方 → 住所、居所

root: 古英语 dwellan「使迷路、延迟」→ 中古英语「停留、居留」；分词 dwelling 转指「住所」。古英语之前的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: a creature stays in one place, and the place of that staying becomes a home, a counted housing unit, an animal burrow, an excavated site and finally a building type.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：生物在一处停留，停留之处便成为家、可计数的住宅、动物洞穴、考古居址，最后成为一类建筑形制。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit room that stays put while everything outside moves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间亮着灯的屋子停在原处，屋外一切都在移动。

branches.en: STAYING AND ITS FACT: the act of staying and the place of staying are two sides of the same participle.
branches.cn: 停留与停留之事：停留的动作与停留的地点，是同一个分词的两面。

branches.en: ANIMAL HOME: any creature that stays put has a dwelling, so the word crosses the line between people and beasts.
branches.cn: 动物的家：任何长居一处的生物都有居所，这个词因此跨越人与兽的界限。

branches.en: COUNTED AND EXCAVATED: officials count a dwelling as a unit, while archaeologists read it as a site of remains.
branches.cn: 计数与发掘：官员把住宅当作统计单位，考古学家则把它读作遗存遗址。

branches.en: SHELTER AND SACRED PLACE: both keep the simple image of a place where someone or something stays.
branches.cn: 栖身与神圣处所：两者都保留「某人或某物停留之处」这一朴素意象。

branches.en: BUILDING TYPE: architecture turns the noun into a label for cave, cliff and stilt homes.
branches.cn: 建筑类型：建筑学把这个名词变成窑洞、崖居与吊脚楼的标签。

intro.en: Dwelling is a native English formation, a Germanic verb plus an English suffix, so it reads quite differently from the Latin-built words around it.
intro.cn: dwelling 是英语本族构词：日耳曼语动词加英语后缀，因此与周围那些拉丁构词读法很不一样。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin ancestor, so no Latin forms are listed; its formal neighbours such as habitation come from a separate Latin family.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖先，故不列拉丁词形；habitation 等正式近邻来自另一个拉丁词族。

items.meaning: to live in a place; to remain
items.example: They dwell above the timber line.

items.meaning: the act, result or place of doing something
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a name for the place.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成地点的名称。

items.example: A single dwelling stood by the ford.

items.meaning: a person who lives in a place
items.example: The cliff dwellers kept goats in the gorge.
items.exampleCN: 崖居者在峡谷里养山羊。

items.meaning: a person or thing that performs the action
items.example: The suffix marks the one who acts.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出动作的执行者。

items.meaning: a house protected as a residence
items.meaningCN: 受住宅法规保护的房屋
items.example: The statute defines a dwelling house as a self-contained home.
items.exampleCN: 该法规把住宅房屋界定为独立成套的住所。

items.meaning: one self-contained home in a building
items.meaningCN: 一栋建筑中独立成套的一套住宅
items.example: Each dwelling unit has its own entrance.
items.exampleCN: 每套住宅都有自己的入口。

items.example: Theology speaks of an indwelling presence.
items.exampleCN: 神学谈论一种内住的存在。

items.meaning: the length of time spent in one place or state
items.example: Engineers measure the dwell time of each batch.
items.exampleCN: 工程师测量每一批料的停留时间。
